E eis que a glória do SENHOR apareceu na nuvem –Êx 16:10.

Que fenômeno estranho é essa massa concentrada de vapor que navega pelo céu acima de nós. Em um instante, uma nuvem pode conceder imensa bênção e esperança, enquanto em outro pode ser a causadora de uma persistente incerteza e até despertar um medo angustiante. Sem dúvida, muitas vezes as nuvens eram a sombra bem-vinda para os pescadores cansados da Galileia e uma fonte de esperança para o lavrador laborioso. Quantas vezes essas nuvens se abrem ao meio-dia para permitir que os raios brilhantes do sol alcancem a terra. Então, à noite, fornecem a estrutura opaca para a beleza requintada de um traçado prateado.

Podemos nos maravilhar ao ver um avião que pesa mais de 700.000 libras elevar-se com suas asas e voar pelos céus; contudo, uma nuvem pode carregar milhões de toneladas de água sem qualquer intervenção humana. As nuvens se formam quando o ar quente e úmido sobe a uma altitude mais fria e a água se condensa em “sementes” microscópicas, como poeira, cinza ou bactérias. Se há mais vapor de água do que lugares onde ele possa se condensar, cristais de gelo também podem servir de sementes e absorver umidade—Prende as águas nas suas densas nuvens; e a nuvem não se rompe debaixo delas –Jó 26:8. Por fim, essas sementes ficam pesadas demais para serem sustentadas pelas correntes ascendentes e, então, eis que chega a hora do guarda-chuva.

Para a terra ressequida nos dias de Elias, a menor das nuvens (como a mão de um homem em 1 Reis 18:44) foi a resposta do Todo-Poderoso de que Ele estava novamente disposto a abençoar Seu povo com chuva. No entanto, para outros, como Jó e Jeremias, a nuvem representava o emblema supremo da dúvida, do desespero e do desalento. Os terrores se voltam contra mim; perseguem a minha alma como o vento, e a minha prosperidade passa como uma nuvem –Jó 30:15, e Tu te cobriste de nuvem, para que a oração não passe –Lm 3:44. Muitas vezes, é em condições tão estressantes que Deus escolhe esconder-se numa nuvem. Nessas ocasiões, tateamos através da densa e ameaçadora neblina em busca do caminho da luz, mas não o encontramos. Em nosso desalento, podemos desejar o brilho de um dia sem nuvens, mas ele nos escapa. Sabemos que Deus está em meio à névoa, mas não conseguimos apreendê-lo nem ver Sua bênção. Ele cobre a luz com nuvens e ordena que ela não brilhe por causa da nuvem que se interpõe –Jó 36:32.

Por que nosso Deus, que ama comungar conosco, vasos de Sua própria criação, escolheria esconder-se numa nuvem? Por que tantas vezes oculta Sua vontade de nossos corações aflitos e perscrutadores? Nossas mentes finitas muitas vezes se perguntam que glória poderia surgir de um Deus aparentemente tão distante, e …para que este desperdício? –Mt 26:8. Embora jamais esperássemos que o plano divino de Deus fosse deixar-nos para sempre num torpor enevoado, talvez essa seja Sua vontade por algum tempo. Como num passeio pelo vale da sombra da morte, pode haver um caráter eterno sendo forjado na alma de quem experimentou uma falta temporária de clareza em seu caminho. Sabemos muito bem que a vereda dos justos é como a luz da aurora, que vai brilhando mais e mais até ser dia perfeito –Pv 4:18. Ainda assim, a maioria de nós já experimentou, por vezes, a névoa desesperançada que envolve nosso presente e nosso futuro. Nessas ocasiões, de dia encontram as trevas, e ao meio-dia andam às apalpadelas como de noite –Jó 5:14. Em nosso desalento abatido, podemos facilmente perder de vista a bondade de Deus. A consequente falta de gratidão é um caminho seguro para toda uma série de outras tentações, enquanto o gigante do desespero se ergue sobre nós, na tentativa de enfraquecer nossa resistência ao pecado.

Sabemos que Elias era homem sujeito às mesmas paixões que nós –Tg 5:17. No entanto, poucos de nós já experimentaram uma vitória tão emocionante quanto a que ele alcançou ao triunfar sobre os profetas de Baal no monte Carmelo. Ainda assim, muitos de nós podem muito bem compreender o desalento que veio depois, quando ele chegou a Horebe e se alojou ali numa caverna. Esse é o mesmo lugar do monte Sinai, onde a primeira grande cena montanhosa se descortinou diante de nós nas Escrituras. Naquela ocasião, foi Moisés quem se encontrou com Deus na nuvem. A lei foi dada, e a glória de Deus se manifestou de modo tão maravilhoso que, de tão terrível que era a visão, Moisés disse: Estou todo aterrorizado e trêmulo –Hb 12:21. Esse monte que se podia tocar era uma montanha imponente e intimidadora, ladeada por picos escuros de granito que se fragmentavam e por cumes austeros de uma grandeza indescritível. A face ousada e terrível de Horebe ergue-se em majestade ameaçadora, com uma altura vertical de mil e duzentos a mil e quinhentos pés.

Com a visão de Elias encoberta e o espírito se esvaindo, no ponto mais baixo de todos os tempos, Deus lhe respondeu de modo espantoso—…E eis que o SENHOR passou, e um grande e forte vento fendia os montes e despedaçava as rochas diante do SENHOR; porém o SENHOR não estava no vento; e depois do vento, um terremoto; porém o SENHOR não estava no terremoto; e depois do terremoto, um fogo; porém o SENHOR não estava no fogo; e depois do fogo, uma voz mansa e delicada. E sucedeu que, ouvindo-a Elias, envolveu o rosto no seu manto, e saiu… –1 Rs 19:11-13.

De algum modo, passamos a acreditar que uma experiência que abala a terra é o auge da presença manifesta de Deus. Pensamos que Deus estava mais perto de Elias no monte Carmelo do que no monte Horebe. Foi o “dia de glória” de Elias ao falar no monte Carmelo. Ele repreendeu o povo e zombou dos profetas. Pregou com ousadia em nome do Senhor e ordenou ao povo que se arrependesse de sua duplicidade. Mas agora sua voz foi silenciada, e ele está ouvindo… ouvindo a voz mansa e delicada que o chama a prestar contas de suas próprias ações e ambições. Assim, se simplesmente pararmos e ouvirmos, a lembrança de nossos fracassos sombrios nos conduzirá à entrada da casa de nosso Senhor, em vez de nos permitir gloriar-nos nos sucessos que imaginamos ter alcançado.

Esta é a bendita ministração da nuvem. Muitas vezes, ela é o veículo que o Senhor usará para nos levar ao lugar onde poderemos verdadeiramente receber em nosso coração Sua glória manifesta. Não se trata das nuvens cúmulos brancas e fofas de um ameno dia de verão, mas, antes, das nuvens stratus planas e sem forma, que cobrem os céus de leste a oeste e eclipsam totalmente todos os raios da luz celestial do sol. Elas podem envolver o dia, em pleno meio-dia, num arsenal de tristeza que nos corrói o coração até o âmago. As pequenas coisas que, em outros dias, pouco afetavam nossas atitudes, agora parecem erguer-se diante de nós como gigantes. Podemos enfrentar acontecimentos que sabemos estar fora de nosso controle, mas nossa mente se recusa a encontrar descanso. Em ocasiões como essas, se por acaso houver uma alma desafortunada do outro lado de nossa conversa passando por uma situação semelhante, talvez experimentemos em primeira mão que …o homem nasce para a aflição, como as faíscas voam para cima –Jó 5:7. Em outras ocasiões, nosso humor melancólico talvez se contente em se retrair e alimentar-se de nossa própria autopiedade isolada e miséria enevoada.

Alguns, em seu desespero, recorrem a medicamentos para a mente e encontram neles uma válvula de alívio limitada. Mas Deus não nos levou à nuvem para que buscássemos a ajuda de médicos e psicólogos. A ministração da nuvem é fechar todas as outras alternativas para que possamos receber dEle a plenitude da bênção de Seu consolo. Deus está disposto a que sacrifiquemos o sol cintilante de hoje pela plenitude de Sua presença amanhã.

Vós não sabeis o que acontecerá amanhã. Pois que é a vossa vida? É um vapor que aparece por um pouco e depois se desvanece –Tg 4:14. Em anos passados, preguei sobre este versículo, exortando as pessoas quanto à brevidade da vida e incentivando-as a não desperdiçar seus anos. Mas eu havia ignorado completamente o fundamento dele—vós não sabeis o que acontecerá amanhã. Isso talvez pareça banal para os jovens de espírito, mas, à medida que os frutos da minha idade continuam a amadurecer, tenho apreciado cada vez mais os ditados comuns e óbvios. Nosso mundo científico moderno persegue com tanta determinação o amor à vida que não consegue apreciar a vida de amor gerada pelo sofrimento. Embora os que, em épocas passadas, sofreram na carne e cessaram de pecar (1 Pe 4:1), não vejo razão para que aqueles que experimentam os frágeis sofrimentos de uma mente nublada não possam compartilhar da mesma glória, se apenas perseverarem e confiarem a Deus os resultados.

Somos um povo arrogante, que se apoia nas previsões de amanhã. Imaginamos que podemos planejar nossa aposentadoria e programar os acontecimentos da vida com detalhes impecáveis. Os meteorologistas nos dizem a temperatura de amanhã para que possamos planejar meticulosamente o nosso dia. Nosso seguro nos dá a garantia de que não estaremos sujeitos à pobreza futura. Nossos congeladores e contas bancárias estão suficientemente cheios para nos manter bem além de amanhã, e nos acostumamos a acreditar que …estou sentada como rainha, não sou viúva e nunca verei o pranto –Ap 18:7. No entanto, a tristeza do coração não pode ser tão facilmente eliminada pelas comodidades terrenas. Nossa vida é um vapor (nuvem) porque …não sabemos o que acontecerá amanhã… –Tg 4:14. Apesar de toda a nossa tecnologia, ainda não podemos eliminar esse fato. É aqui que devemos deixar de lado todas as nossas intuições, expectativas e ambições quanto ao que nossa vida deveria ser e encontrar nosso Deus na nuvem.

Ele encobre a face do seu trono e estende sobre ele a sua nuvem –Jó 26:9. Que benefício há em a nuvem cobrir a face do trono de Deus? Se fosse fácil contemplá-lo, a maioria de nós se contentaria em viver com Ele à distância. Contudo, por causa da neblina que se aproxima, temos de nos achegar para experimentar Sua plenitude. Como devemos ser gratos por ser assim, pois quão devastadora seria nossa perda espiritual se não fosse assim.

Se nossa vida autossuficiente estivesse sempre vigorosamente plena e Deus pudesse ser apreendido com facilidade, perderíamos…

…a Fé

Buscamos a garantia de que nossas provações terminarão felizes para sempre e de que nossas orações naturalmente se tornarão desnecessárias. Pela fé, cremos na provisão de Deus, mas o fato de não sabermos o que um dia trará exige que nos prostremos de joelhos, apesar de nossa fraqueza, e oremos. Muitas coisas podem dificultar nossa confiança em Deus, mas o amanhã encoberto a torna mais fácil. Pesquisadores gastaram milhões em seus esforços para controlar o clima. Semearam no ar todas as sementes de nuvem imagináveis, na tentativa de produzir nuvens de chuva. Depois de analisar 40 anos de esforços para semear nuvens numa região ao norte de Israel, pesquisadores da Universidade de Tel Aviv concluíram que a semeadura de nuvens não produz, de fato, qualquer precipitação adicional. Como devemos ser gratos. Quanto mais pudermos controlar o amanhã desconhecido, menos precisaremos da fé no Senhor do Universo.

Ao deixar para trás um irmão irado, um pai decepcionado e um vínculo rompido com sua mãe, Jacó enfrentou um futuro completamente desconhecido. Isso faz parte da escada para o trono e fortalece nosso compromisso com nosso Deus onipotente. Agora conhecemos em parte e vemos em parte. Talvez essa pequena fração nos traga mais riqueza interior do que teríamos se compreendêssemos tudo plenamente. Se nosso futuro estivesse amplamente ao alcance de nosso poder de manipulação, formularíamos uma utopia perfeita, abastecida com o número perfeito de filhos vivendo luxuosamente na casa perfeita, sustentados pelo emprego perfeito e cercados por um comportamento perfeito, estéril e morto.

…a Esperança

Pergunto-me se percebemos o quanto devemos ao inesperado. O escritor aos Hebreus declara que nossa esperança é …âncora da alma, segura e firme… –Hb 6:19. As crianças são felizes porque têm grandes sonhos. Muitas vezes, a expectativa e o planejamento de um acontecimento são quase tão emocionantes quanto o próprio passeio. Cada dia é uma janela nova e luminosa para a mente imaculada e esperançosa. As experiências muitas vezes podem nos levar à beira do cinismo e da amargura quando vistas através das decepções de ontem. Jacó, após a maravilhosa reunião com seu filho José, ainda comentou: poucos e maus foram os dias da minha vida. Embora seja natural que assim seja, não precisa ser assim. Paulo afirma que …a tribulação produz a paciência; e a paciência, a experiência; e a experiência, a esperança –Rm 5:3-4. Certamente, se soubéssemos o que nos espera amanhã (tanto de bom como de mau), o elemento revigorante da esperança diminuiria. Eva fingiu que a vida seria melhor se pudesse apenas obter mais conhecimento. Mas quanta esperança bendita foi perdida em sua busca lasciva por clareza.

…o Amor

Há no amor uma ternura saudosa que nada além da incerteza pode proporcionar. É a maravilha incerta que envolve o caminho de um jovem com uma moça. Os perigos desconhecidos de amanhã levam uma mãe a amar e orar por seus filhos. É a visão de um amanhã melhor para sua família que leva um pai a dedicar-se ao trabalho diário. Sempre que marido e mulher estão unidos na unidade bíblica do santo matrimônio, o mistério que envolve o amanhã é como o acorde menor numa grande melodia. Ele fala alegremente de uma tristeza sugerida e ilumina a tristeza com uma alegria que a envolve. A espera de sete anos de Jacó teria parecido durar poucos dias se ele soubesse o que o amanhã traria? Se soubéssemos tudo, o amor seria difícil demais. Se soubéssemos tudo, o amor seria fácil demais. Se soubéssemos tudo, ficaríamos de coração partido. Se soubéssemos tudo, ficaríamos indiferentes. Em outras palavras, não saber o pior nos torna mais fortes, e não saber o melhor nos torna mais ternos. Pois, através de nossa visão enevoada e obscurecida, …permanecem a fé, a esperança e o amor, estes três; mas o maior destes é o amor –1 Co 13:13.

Não é por acaso que, enquanto os discípulos …olhavam, ele foi elevado às alturas, e uma nuvem o recebeu, ocultando-o a seus olhos –At 1:9. E, portanto, não devemos nos surpreender se, às vezes, formos chamados a sofrer a tensão e o estresse mental de um amanhã obscuro e desconhecido. …Pois que é a vossa vida? É um vapor que aparece por um pouco e depois se desvanece –Tg 4:14. Está chegando o dia em que …verão o Filho do Homem vindo numa nuvem, com poder e grande glória –Lc 21:27. E está escrito novamente: Eis que vem com as nuvens, e todo olho o verá… Assim seja. Amém –Ap 1:7.

Behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud –Exo 16:10.

What a strange phenomenon is this concentrated mass of vapor that navigates the sky above us. In one instance, a cloud can minister such immense blessedness and hope, while in another it can be the instigator of nagging uncertainty and even the arousal of ragged fear. Clouds were often, no doubt, the welcome shade to the heads of weary fishermen upon Galilee and the propagator of hope to the toiling farmer. How often these clouds part at midday to allow the sun’s beaming rays access to the earth. Then in the evening, they provide the opaque structure for the exquisite beauty of a silver lineation.

We may marvel to see an airplane weighing over 700,000 pounds mount up with wings and soar through the heavens, yet a cloud can carry millions of tons of water without any of the dynamics of human intervention. Clouds are formed when moist, warm air rises to a cooler elevation and water condenses onto microscopic “seeds” such as dust, ash, or bacteria. If there’s more water vapor than places on which it can condense, then ice crystals can also serve as seeds and take on moisture—He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them –Job 26:8. Eventually, these seeds become too heavy for updrafts to support, and then, behold, it is time for the umbrella.

To the parched land in Elijah’s day, the smallest of clouds (like a man’s hand in 1 Kings 18:44) was the answer from the Almighty that He was again prepared to bless His people with rain. Yet, to others like Job and Jeremiah, the cloud represented the ultimate emblem of doubt, despair, and discouragement. Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud –Job 30:15, and Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through –Lam 3:44. It is often in such stressful conditions that God chooses to hide Himself in a cloud. At these times, we grope through the thick foreboding fog in search of the pathway of light, but we find it not. In our discouragement, we may long for the beam of a cloudless day, but it eludes us. We know that God is in the midst of the mist, but we cannot apprehend Him, nor see His blessedness. With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt –Job 36:32.

Why would our God, who loves to commune with us, the vessels of His own creation, choose to hide Himself in a cloud? Why does He often hide His will from our searching and aching hearts? Our finite minds often wonder what glory could possibly arise from such a seemingly distant God, and …to what purpose is this waste –Mat 26:8. While we would never expect it to be God’s divine plan to leave us in a foggy stupor forever, it may be His will for a time. Like a stroll through the valley of the shadow of death, there can be eternal character wrought in the soul who has experienced a seasonal lack of clarity in their path. We are well aware that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Pro 4:18. Still, most of us have, at times, experienced the hopeless fog that surrounds our present and our future. In these times, we meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night –Job 5:14. In our bedraggled discouragement, we can easily lose sight of the goodness of God. Our resulting lack of thankfulness is a sure road to a host of other temptations, while the giant of despair rises overhead in an attempt to weaken our resistance to sin.

We know that Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are –Jam 5:17. Yet, few of us have ever experienced a victory as exhilarating as he did when he triumphed over the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Still, many of us can well relate to the discouragement that followed as he came unto Horeb and lodged in a cave there. This is the same place as Mount Sinai where the first great mountain scene opened before us in the Scriptures. Then it was Moses who met God in the cloud. The law was given, and God’s glory was so marvelously manifested and so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake –Heb 12:21. This mount that might be touched was a formidable and intimidating mountain flanked by splintering dark granite peaks and stern ridges of indescribable grandeur. The bold and awful front of Horeb, rises in frowning majesty from twelve hundred to fifteen hundred feet in perpendicular height.

With Elijah’s vision clouded over and his spirit ebbing away at an all-time low, God responded to him in astounding methodology—…And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out… –1 Kin 19:11-13.

Somehow, we have come to believe that an earthshaking experience is the epitome of God’s manifest presence. We reckon that God was closer to Elijah on Mt. Carmel than He was on Mt. Horeb. It was Elijah’s “day in the sun” while speaking on Mt. Carmel. He chided the people and mocked the prophets. He preached boldly in the name of the Lord and commanded the people to repent of their duplicity. But now his voice has been silenced and he is listening … listening to the still small voice calling into account his own actions and ambitions. Thus, if we will but stop and listen, the memory of our dismal failures will escort us to the front porch of our Lord, rather than allow us to glory in our perceived successes.

This is the blessed ministration of the cloud. It is often the vehicle that the Lord will use to bring us to the place where we can truly receive His manifest glory in our hearts. This is not the white, fluffy, cumulus clouds of a balmy summer day but, rather, the flat and featureless stratus clouds that blanket the heavens from east to west and totally eclipse all the rays of heavenly sunshine. They can enshroud the day at high noon with an arsenal of gloom that rankles our hearts to the core. The little things, that on other days had little effect on our attitudes, now seem to tower as giants before us. We may face advents that we know are beyond our control, but our minds refuse to enter into rest. In times like these, if there happens to be an unfortunate soul on the other end of our conversation experiencing a similar plight, we may experience firsthand that …man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward –Job 5:7. At other times, our melancholy mood may be content to withdraw and feed itself with our own reclusive pity and foggy misery.

Some, in their desperation, turn to medication for the mind and there find a limited valve of relief. But God has not brought us into the cloud so that we may seek the help of physicians and psychologists. The ministration of the cloud is to shut off all other alternatives so that we may receive of Him the full blessedness of His consolation. God is willing that we should sacrifice the shimmering sunshine of today for the fullness of His presence tomorrow.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. In bygone years, I have preached on this verse, exhorting souls concerning the brevity of life and encouraging them to not squander their years away. But I had totally ignored the foundation of it—ye know not what shall be on the morrow. This, perhaps, seems trite to the young at heart, but as the fruit of my age continues to ripen, I have a growing appreciation for the common and obvious idioms. Our modern scientific world is so adamantly pursuing the love of life that it cannot appreciate the life of love that is begotten through suffering. While those who, in ages past, suffered in the flesh and ceased from sin (1 Pet 4:1), I see no reason why those who experience the frail sufferings of a clouded mind may not share the same glory if they will but endure and trust to God the results.

We are an arrogant people who lean on the predictions of tomorrow. We fancy that we can plan our retirement and schedule our life events with immaculate detail. The weather forecasters tell us of tomorrows temperature so that we can meticulously plan our day. Our insurance gives assurance that we will not be subject to future poverty. Our freezers and bank accounts are full enough to see us well past tomorrow, and we have grown accustomed to believing that we …sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow –Rev 18:7. Yet the sorrow of heart cannot be so easily absolved by earthly amenities. Our life is a vapour (cloud) because we …know not what shall be on the morrow… –Jas 4:14. In spite of all our technology we still cannot absolve that fact. It is here that we must lay aside all our intuitions, expectations, and ambitions of what our life ought to be and find our God in the cloud.

He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it –Job 26:9. To what benefit is the cloud covering the face of God’s throne? If it were easily beholden, most of us would be content to dwell with Him from afar. However, due to the impending fog, we must draw nigh to experience His fullness. How thankful we ought to be that it is thus, for how devastating would be our spiritual loss if it were not so.

If our self-sufficient life was always vibrantly full and God were easily apprehended, we would lose…

…Faith

We seek a guarantee that our trials will end happily ever after and that our prayers will naturally become unnecessary. In faith, we believe in God’s provision, but the fact that we know not what a day will bring demands that we fall upon our feeble knees and pray. There may be many things that make it hard for us to trust in God, but the shrouded tomorrow makes it easier. Researchers have spent millions in their efforts to control the weather. They have sown every imaginable cloud seed into the air in efforts to produce rain clouds. After reviewing 40 years of cloud-seeding efforts in an area north of Israel, researchers at Tel Aviv University have concluded that cloud seeding doesn’t actually produce any additional precipitation. How thankful we should be. The more we can control the unknown morrow, the less faith in the Master of the Universe we need.

Jacob, in leaving behind an angry brother, a disappointed father, and a severed tie with his mother, faced an altogether unknown future. This is a part of the ladder to the throne and it fortifies our commitment to our omnipotent God. Now we know in part and we see in part. Perhaps that fractional sliver brings us more inner wealth than if the whole were fully understood. If our future were amply within our manipulative power, we would formulate a perfect utopia supplied with the perfect number of children living sumptuously in the perfect home supported by the perfect job surrounded by perfect behavior that is perfectly sterile and dead.

…Hope

I question if we realize how deeply our debt is to the unexpected. The Hebrew writer declares our hope to be …an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast… –Heb 6:19. Children are happy because they have big dreams. Often the anticipation and planning of an event is almost as thrilling as the excursion itself. Every day is a bright new window to the unspoiled, hopeful mind. Experiences can often bring us to the brink of cynicism and bitterness when viewed through yesterday’s disappointments. Jacob, upon the marvelous reunification with his son, Joseph, still remarked, few and evil have been my days. Though it is naturally so, it needs not to be. Paul states …that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope –Rom 5:3-4. Surely, if we knew what was in store tomorrow (both good and evil) the invigorating element of hope would dwindle. Eve feigned that life would be better if she could only secure more knowledge. But what blessed hope was forfeited in her lustful pursuit of clarity.

…Love

There is a wistful tenderness in love that nothing but uncertainty can give. It is uncertain wonder that encompasses the way of a young man with a maid. The unknown perils of tomorrow drive a mother to love and prayer for her children. It is the vision of a brighter tomorrow for his family that moves a father to diligence in his daily work. Wherever a husband and his wife are knit together in Biblical oneness of holy matrimony, the mystery that envelops tomorrow is like the minor chord in a great melody. It speaks in joy of a suggested sorrow and brightens sorrow with encircling joy. Would Jacob’s seven-year wait have seemed like a few days if he had known what the morrow would bring? If we knew everything, love would be too hard. If we knew everything, love would be too easy. If we knew everything, we would be brokenhearted. If we knew everything, we would be unconcerned. In other words, it makes us stronger to not know the worst and it makes us more tender to not know the best. For in our clouded and darkened lens there …abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Cor 13:13.

It is no coincidence that while the disciples …beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight –Act 1:9. And so we dare not be surprised that, at times, we shall be called to suffer the mental strain and stress of an obscure and unknown tomorrow. …For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. There is coming a day when we shall …see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory –Luk 21:27. And again it is written, Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him … Even so, Amen –Rev 1:7.

He aquí, la gloria del SEÑOR apareció en la nube –Éxo 16:10.

¡Qué fenómeno tan extraño es esta masa concentrada de vapor que navega por el cielo sobre nosotros! En un momento, una nube puede impartir una bendición y una esperanza inmensas, mientras que en otro puede ser la causa de una incertidumbre persistente e incluso despertar un miedo desgarrador. Sin duda, a menudo las nubes eran la sombra bienvenida para las cabezas de los cansados pescadores del mar de Galilea y propagaban esperanza al agricultor laborioso. ¡Cuántas veces estas nubes se abren al mediodía para permitir que los radiantes rayos del sol lleguen a la tierra! Luego, por la tarde, proporcionan la estructura opaca para la exquisita belleza de un trazo plateado.

Podemos maravillarnos al ver que un avión de más de 700 000 libras se eleve con sus alas y surque los cielos; sin embargo, una nube puede transportar millones de toneladas de agua sin ninguna intervención humana. Las nubes se forman cuando el aire cálido y húmedo asciende a una altura más fría y el agua se condensa sobre «semillas» microscópicas, como polvo, ceniza o bacterias. Si hay más vapor de agua que lugares donde pueda condensarse, los cristales de hielo también pueden servir de semillas y absorber humedad: Él recoge las aguas en sus densas nubes, y la nube no se rasga bajo ellas –Job 26:8. Finalmente, estas semillas se vuelven demasiado pesadas para que las corrientes ascendentes las sostengan, y entonces, he aquí, llega la hora del paraguas.

Para la tierra reseca en los días de Elías, la más pequeña de las nubes (como la mano de un hombre en 1 Reyes 18:44) fue la respuesta del Todopoderoso de que estaba dispuesto otra vez a bendecir a su pueblo con lluvia. Sin embargo, para otros, como Job y Jeremías, la nube representaba el emblema supremo de la duda, la desesperación y el desaliento. Se vuelven contra mí los terrores; persiguen mi alma como el viento, y mi bienestar pasa como una nube –Job 30:15, y Te cubriste con una nube para que no pasara nuestra oración –Lam 3:44. A menudo es en esas condiciones de angustia cuando Dios decide ocultarse en una nube. En esos momentos, avanzamos a tientas por la espesa niebla amenazadora en busca del camino de la luz, pero no lo encontramos. Desalentados, podemos anhelar el resplandor de un día sin nubes, pero se nos escapa. Sabemos que Dios está en medio de la bruma, pero no podemos comprenderlo ni ver su bendición. Con las nubes cubre la luz, y manda que no brille la nube que se interpone –Job 36:32.

¿Por qué nuestro Dios, que ama comunicarse con nosotros, las criaturas que él mismo creó, elegiría ocultarse en una nube? ¿Por qué suele ocultar su voluntad a nuestros corazones que la buscan con dolor? Nuestras mentes finitas a menudo se preguntan qué gloria podría surgir de un Dios que parece tan distante, y …¿con qué fin este desperdicio? –Mat 26:8. Aunque nunca esperaríamos que el plan divino de Dios fuera dejarnos para siempre en un estupor nebuloso, puede ser su voluntad por un tiempo. Como en un paseo por el valle de sombra de muerte, el alma que ha experimentado una falta temporal de claridad en su camino puede forjar un carácter eterno. Sabemos muy bien que la senda de los justos es como la luz de la aurora, que va en aumento hasta que el día es perfecto –Pro 4:18. Aun así, la mayoría de nosotros hemos experimentado a veces la niebla desesperanzadora que envuelve nuestro presente y nuestro futuro. En esos momentos, en pleno día tropezamos como de noche, y a mediodía andamos a tientas como si fuera de noche –Job 5:14. En nuestro abatimiento, es fácil perder de vista la bondad de Dios. La consiguiente falta de gratitud es un camino seguro hacia muchas otras tentaciones, mientras el gigante de la desesperación se alza sobre nosotros en un intento de debilitar nuestra resistencia al pecado.

Sabemos que Elías era un hombre sujeto a pasiones semejantes a las nuestras –Sant 5:17. Sin embargo, pocos de nosotros hemos experimentado una victoria tan emocionante como la suya cuando triunfó sobre los profetas de Baal en el monte Carmelo. Aun así, muchos podemos comprender bien el desaliento que vino después, cuando llegó a Horeb y se alojó allí en una cueva. Este es el mismo lugar que el monte Sinaí, donde se nos presentó la primera gran escena montañosa de las Escrituras. Entonces fue Moisés quien se encontró con Dios en la nube. Se dio la ley, y la gloria de Dios se manifestó de manera tan maravillosa que …fue tan terrible el espectáculo, que Moisés dijo: Estoy espantado y temblando –Heb 12:21. Este monte que podía tocarse era un monte imponente e intimidante, flanqueado por cumbres de granito oscuro que se desmoronaban y crestas severas de una grandeza indescriptible. La audaz e imponente fachada de Horeb se eleva con majestad ceñuda entre mil doscientos y mil quinientos pies en altura perpendicular.

Con la visión de Elías nublada y su espíritu desfalleciendo hasta tocar fondo, Dios le respondió de una manera asombrosa: …Y he aquí que el SEÑOR pasó, y un viento grande y poderoso rompía los montes y quebraba las peñas delante del SEÑOR; pero el SEÑOR no estaba en el viento. Y tras el viento, un terremoto; pero el SEÑOR no estaba en el terremoto. Y tras el terremoto, un fuego; pero el SEÑOR no estaba en el fuego. Y tras el fuego, una voz apacible y delicada. Y sucedió que cuando Elías la oyó, cubrió su rostro con su manto y salió… –1 Rey 19:11-13.

De algún modo, hemos llegado a creer que una experiencia estremecedora es el máximo exponente de la presencia manifiesta de Dios. Suponemos que Dios estaba más cerca de Elías en el monte Carmelo que en el monte Horeb. Elías tuvo su «día de gloria» al hablar en el monte Carmelo. Reprendió al pueblo y se burló de los profetas. Predicó con valentía en el nombre del Señor y ordenó al pueblo que se arrepintiera de su duplicidad. Pero ahora su voz ha sido silenciada y está escuchando… escuchando la voz apacible y delicada que le pide cuentas por sus propias acciones y ambiciones. Así pues, si tan solo nos detenemos a escuchar, el recuerdo de nuestros lamentables fracasos nos acompañará hasta el umbral de nuestro Señor, en lugar de permitirnos gloriarnos en nuestros éxitos percibidos.

Este es el bendito ministerio de la nube. A menudo es el vehículo que el Señor usará para llevarnos al lugar donde podamos recibir de verdad la gloria manifiesta de él en nuestros corazones. No se trata de las nubes cúmulo blancas y esponjosas de un apacible día de verano, sino de las nubes estratos, planas y sin rasgos, que cubren los cielos de este a oeste y eclipsan por completo todos los rayos del sol celestial. Pueden envolver el día, incluso al mediodía, en un arsenal de pesadumbre que nos irrita el corazón hasta lo más profundo. Las cosas pequeñas que otros días apenas influían en nuestra actitud ahora parecen alzarse ante nosotros como gigantes. Podemos enfrentarnos a acontecimientos que sabemos que están fuera de nuestro control, pero nuestra mente se niega a descansar. En momentos así, si resulta que hay un alma desafortunada al otro extremo de nuestra conversación que está pasando por una situación similar, podemos comprobar de primera mano que …el hombre nace para la aflicción, como las chispas vuelan hacia arriba –Job 5:7. En otras ocasiones, nuestro ánimo melancólico puede conformarse con retraerse y alimentarse de nuestra propia autocompasión aislada y nuestra desdicha nebulosa.

Algunos, en su desesperación, recurren a medicamentos para la mente y encuentran allí un alivio limitado. Pero Dios no nos ha llevado a la nube para que busquemos la ayuda de médicos y psicólogos. El ministerio de la nube consiste en cerrar todas las demás alternativas para que recibamos de él toda la plenitud del consuelo que nos da. Dios está dispuesto a que sacrifiquemos el sol resplandeciente de hoy por la plenitud de su presencia mañana.

Cuando no sabéis lo que será mañana. Porque ¿qué es vuestra vida? Ciertamente es vapor que aparece por un poco de tiempo y luego se desvanece –Sant 4:14. En años pasados, he predicado sobre este versículo, exhortando a las almas acerca de lo breve que es la vida y animándolas a no desperdiciar sus años. Pero había pasado totalmente por alto su fundamento: no sabéis lo que será mañana. Esto quizá parezca una trivialidad para quienes se sienten jóvenes de corazón, pero, mientras el fruto de mi edad sigue madurando, aprecio cada vez más las expresiones comunes y evidentes. Nuestro mundo científico moderno persigue con tanto empeño el amor a la vida que no puede apreciar la vida de amor que nace del sufrimiento. Aunque quienes vivieron en épocas pasadas sufrieron en la carne y dejaron de pecar (1 Pe 4:1), no veo por qué quienes experimentan los frágiles sufrimientos de una mente nublada no puedan compartir la misma gloria si tan solo perseveran y confían a Dios los resultados.

Somos un pueblo arrogante que se apoya en las predicciones del mañana. Nos imaginamos que podemos planificar nuestra jubilación y programar los acontecimientos de nuestra vida con precisión impecable. Los meteorólogos nos dicen cuál será la temperatura de mañana para que podamos planificar meticulosamente el día. Nuestro seguro nos garantiza que no sufriremos pobreza en el futuro. Nuestros congeladores y cuentas bancarias están lo bastante llenos para que podamos pasar holgadamente de mañana, y nos hemos acostumbrado a creer que …estoy sentada como reina, y no soy viuda, y no veré llanto –Apoc 18:7. Sin embargo, el dolor del corazón no puede aliviarse tan fácilmente con comodidades terrenales. Nuestra vida es un vapor (una nube) porque …no sabemos lo que será mañana… –Sant 4:14. A pesar de toda nuestra tecnología, todavía no podemos cambiar ese hecho. Es aquí donde debemos dejar a un lado todas nuestras intuiciones, expectativas y ambiciones acerca de cómo debería ser nuestra vida y encontrar a nuestro Dios en la nube.

Él cubre la faz de su trono y extiende sobre él su nube –Job 26:9. ¿Qué beneficio tiene que la nube cubra la faz del trono de Dios? Si fuera fácil contemplarlo, la mayoría de nosotros nos conformaríamos con morar con él desde lejos. Sin embargo, debido a la niebla que se avecina, debemos acercarnos para experimentar su plenitud. ¡Cuán agradecidos deberíamos estar de que sea así! ¡Qué devastadora sería nuestra pérdida espiritual si no lo fuera!

Si nuestra vida autosuficiente estuviera siempre rebosante de vitalidad y fuera fácil comprender a Dios, perderíamos…

…La fe

Buscamos la garantía de que nuestras pruebas terminarán con un final feliz y de que nuestras oraciones dejarán de ser necesarias de manera natural. Por la fe creemos en la provisión de Dios, pero el hecho de que no sabemos qué traerá un día nos exige caer de rodillas, débiles como somos, y orar. Puede haber muchas cosas que nos dificulten confiar en Dios, pero el mañana velado lo hace más fácil. Los investigadores han invertido millones en sus esfuerzos por controlar el clima. Han sembrado en el aire todas las semillas de nube imaginables con el propósito de producir nubes de lluvia. Tras analizar 40 años de esfuerzos de siembra de nubes en una zona al norte de Israel, investigadores de la Universidad de Tel Aviv han concluido que la siembra de nubes en realidad no produce precipitación adicional. ¡Cuán agradecidos deberíamos estar! Cuanto más podamos controlar el mañana desconocido, menos fe necesitaremos en el Señor del universo.

Al dejar atrás a un hermano enojado, a un padre decepcionado y el vínculo roto con su madre, Jacob se enfrentó a un futuro completamente desconocido. Esto forma parte de la escalera hacia el trono y fortalece nuestro compromiso con nuestro Dios omnipotente. Ahora conocemos en parte y vemos en parte. Quizá esa pequeña porción nos aporte más riqueza interior que si comprendiéramos plenamente el todo. Si nuestro futuro estuviera por completo bajo nuestro poder para manipularlo, formularíamos una utopía perfecta, con el número perfecto de hijos que vivirían en la opulencia en el hogar perfecto, sustentados por el empleo perfecto y rodeados de una conducta perfecta, estéril y muerta.

…La esperanza

Me pregunto si nos damos cuenta de cuán profundamente estamos en deuda con lo inesperado. El escritor de Hebreos declara que nuestra esperanza es …un ancla del alma, segura y firme… –Heb 6:19. Los niños son felices porque tienen grandes sueños. A menudo, la ilusión y la planificación de un acontecimiento son casi tan emocionantes como la excursión misma. Cada día es una ventana nueva y luminosa para la mente pura y esperanzada. Las experiencias a menudo pueden llevarnos al borde del cinismo y la amargura cuando las vemos a través de las decepciones de ayer. Jacob, después de reunirse de manera maravillosa con su hijo José, aun así comentó: pocos y malos han sido mis días. Aunque es algo natural, no tiene por qué ser así. Pablo afirma que …la tribulación produce paciencia; y la paciencia, experiencia; y la experiencia, esperanza –Rom 5:3-4. Sin duda, si supiéramos lo que nos depara el mañana (tanto lo bueno como lo malo), el elemento estimulante de la esperanza se debilitaría. Eva fingió que la vida sería mejor si tan solo pudiera obtener más conocimiento. Pero ¡qué esperanza bendita perdió en su búsqueda lujuriosa de claridad!

…El amor

En el amor hay una ternura nostálgica que solo puede surgir de la incertidumbre. Es la incertidumbre llena de asombro que envuelve el camino de un joven con una doncella. Los peligros desconocidos del mañana impulsan a una madre a amar y orar por sus hijos. Es la visión de un mañana más luminoso para su familia lo que mueve a un padre a trabajar con diligencia cada día. Allí donde un esposo y su esposa están unidos en la unidad bíblica del santo matrimonio, el misterio que envuelve el mañana es como el acorde menor de una gran melodía. Expresa con alegría un dolor insinuado e ilumina el dolor con una alegría envolvente. ¿Le habría parecido a Jacob que los siete años de espera eran solo unos días si hubiera sabido lo que traería el mañana? Si lo supiéramos todo, amar sería demasiado difícil. Si lo supiéramos todo, amar sería demasiado fácil. Si lo supiéramos todo, nos romperían el corazón. Si lo supiéramos todo, nos sería indiferente. En otras palabras, no conocer lo peor nos hace más fuertes, y no conocer lo mejor nos hace más tiernos. Pues en nuestra visión nublada y oscurecida …permanecen la fe, la esperanza y el amor, estos tres; pero el mayor de ellos es el amor –1 Cor 13:13.

No es casualidad que, mientras los discípulos …miraban, él fue llevado arriba, y una nube lo recibió y lo ocultó de su vista –Hch 1:9. Por eso no debemos sorprendernos de que, a veces, se nos llame a soportar la tensión y el estrés mental de un mañana oscuro y desconocido. …Porque ¿qué es vuestra vida? Ciertamente es vapor que aparece por un poco de tiempo y luego se desvanece –Sant 4:14. Se acerca el día en que …verán al Hijo del Hombre venir en una nube con poder y gran gloria –Luc 21:27. Y también está escrito: He aquí, viene con las nubes, y todo ojo le verá… Así sea. Amén –Apoc 1:7.

“My lady, I thank you very much for your affection and favor towards me, but I have given myself entirely to God to be His friend, and with that I hope to live and die,” rang the confident, faith-filled words of Jacques “zhahk” (a French form of the male name Jacob or James).

Persecution was fiercely raging in Europe in the year 1550. For their profession of faith in Jesus Christ, men, women, and even children were snatched from their homes and meeting places and thrown into the dark and cold dungeon cells of area castles. Among these captives, fifteen-year-old Jacques Dosie found himself imprisoned in Leeuwarden, Holland, for the truth of the Gospel. Even though he was only fifteen years old, he was known by his upright testimony and knowledge of the Scriptures, bringing glory to God through the power of the Spirit.

The Lord and Lady Friesland, with many nobles and ladies, were assembled in the royal halls in Leeuwarden. Their conversation turned to the “baptist heretics” that were filling the land.

“Let’s bring in that young lad, Jacques. Surely he has not been too contaminated with this heresy.”

So, he was brought in to be interrogated. Lord Friesland spoke only a few words and seemed in a hurry to finish. He had no time for this talk of religion, especially with guests waiting for a more enjoyable entertainment. Lady Friesland, however, seemed moved with compassion for this youth who was so cruelly bound in the dungeon.

“Why are you in prison? You are only a youth. What brought you here?” she asked.

Jacques answered, “I was captured and thrown into prison only because I believe in Jesus Christ. I abide by Him alone and will not forsake Him.”

The royal lady asked him, “Surely you are not one of those heretics who rebaptized themselves and have perpetrated so much evil in our country? They say they are dispersed on account of their faith and boast of being the church of God. But they are a wicked and rebellious people and cause great commotion in the land.”

“My lady, I do not know any rebellious people nor am I one of their number,” replied Jacques. “But we would much rather, according to the teachings of the Scriptures, assist our enemies. If they hunger and thirst, we bless them with food and drink. We never resist them with revenge or violence as we read in Matthew 5:39.”

“If you were in a position of power it would be seen whether you would assist your enemies,” sneered one of the nobles.

Jacques replied, “Oh, no, my lord, if it were permitted among us to resist the evil with the carnal sword, I would never do so.”

“I know there are sects among you who are very wicked and kill the people. They have their goods and wives in common,” said Lady Friesland.

“Oh, no,” replied Jacques. “We are unjustly charged with these wicked things. We are falsely accused of evil as a means to be persecuted. But as taught in Matthew 5:11, we must suffer and endure all this with patience.”

“Was it not your people who with great dishonor took up arms against the government at Amsterdam and Muenster?” asked Lady Friesland.

“No, my lady, we are not of them,” answered Jacques. “Those people erred greatly. We regard it as a doctrine of the devil to resist the authorities with the sword and violence. We would much rather suffer persecution and death from the authorities.”

“Nevertheless, you are considered to be one of them, because you too make an uproar in the land,” insisted the royal lady. “However, I believe what you say concerning those Muensterites.”

“But, my lady, don’t we read about this in Acts 24:5, how wicked men spoke evil of the apostles themselves as well as the whole band of Christians?” countered Jacques. “Did not wicked men seek to incite the authorities to vengeance against the Christians, though it was all falsehood?”

Lady Friesland didn’t answer but quickly diverted to another topic. “Do you believe that all are damned who are not baptized according to your way?” she asked.

“Oh, no, my lady,” answered Jacques. “Judgement concerning other men belongs to God alone, who shall reward everyone according to his works. This is clearly stated in many places of the Holy Scriptures. Moreover, the water does not have the power to cleanse us from sin, as 1 Peter 3:21 says, but is merely a sign of all obedience.”

“Can you still sin after you are baptized?” asked Lady Friesland.

“Yes, my lady, for this is clearly evident from the words of Paul in Romans 7:18,” replied Jacques. “We are still clothed in a weak and sinful body, and sin in many things. But we must constantly crucify and mortify the flesh, and not practice or fulfill the works of the flesh. If we fail to do this, the righteousness of God will condemn us to eternal death.”

Lady Friesland was becoming agitated. “Why don’t you listen to the church inquisitor?” she demanded.

Jacques replied, “My lady, because I will not accept his doctrine, unless he first can clearly prove to me that it agrees in all points with the Word of God. Otherwise he is laboring in vain. My faith is founded on the pure Word of God alone. As for the practice of infant baptism, I contradict his argument with reason since it is not a command of God Almighty but much rather the invention of men. Infants do not have the least bit of knowledge or discernment about what is required for baptism. But Christ in His love for such innocent ones has promised them the kingdom of God through grace, without requiring baptism.

“And further, my lady, I find that the Roman church is infected with many other errors besides this. They seek to make Christ come into the bread, or that the bread and wine should become changed into His flesh and blood. I do not believe this but regard it as an exceedingly gross error and absurdity. But I believe that Christ truly ascended to heaven and sits on the right hand of His Father as we find in Mark 16:19. There is no salvation in their flour, mass, purgatory, or any of their services for the dead. All of their human inventions, and there are many, are nowhere recognized in the Holy Scriptures. But on the contrary, we call upon God and seek our salvation in Him. Our salvation is not in any creation of man, that we may not corrupt God’s own glory and give it to any of His creatures.”

At this point the mayor, who was also present, interrupted, “So don’t you believe in the sacrament which Christ Himself instituted?”

“Sir, Paul says that the bread is broken in remembrance of Him, and that the cup of blessing is the communion of the blood of Christ,” replied Jacques.

The mayor had nothing to answer to this.

“I consider this the worst thing about you, that you will not have the children baptized,” stated Lady Friesland. “All Germany and every kingdom regard your doings as heresy.”

“It is indeed true we are despised everywhere even as the apostles were,” replied Jacques. “But we do not believe that unbaptized children shall perish at the judgment day.”

“My dear child,” said the lady pleadingly. “Come over to our side, and repent, and you shall get out of this trouble. I promise to secure your release.”

“My lady, I thank you very much for your affection and favor towards me,” answered Jacques boldly. “But I will not change my faith to please mortal man unless it be proven to me with the Scriptures. I have given myself entirely to God, to be His friend, and with that I hope to live and die.”

“My son, I have compassion for you,” she pleaded again. “Repent of your baptism and do not be so stubborn. It would be a heavy cross for my heart if you should die for this cause, being such a young child. If you repent, I will see that you are released and may go home.”

“I cannot see that there is any crime at all in my baptism. I have not followed my own cause but the Holy institution of our Lord Jesus Christ. I have not been able to find another better way to the kingdom of God except through baptism,” replied Jacques. “I am inclined to seek the Lord my God with my whole heart.”

“Look at all these men around you. Do you dare be so presumptuous to say all of them are in error?” asked Lady Friesland.

“My lady,” replied Jacques. “In Israel, four hundred prophets were against the prophet Micaiah, who alone spoke the truth. For speaking the truth, he was imprisoned on bread and water. Later in his distress, King Ahab realized prophet Micaiah spoke the truth, but it was too late. We read of this in 2 Chronicles 18.”

The lady finally said, “I find many good things in you; but your greatest error lies in your baptism. To me that does not seem to be of God.”

Lady Friesland had Jacques brought before her many times. Even though he was young in years, he was mature in the knowledge of Jesus Christ. He had built his foundation upon the Rock, Jesus Christ. With the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God, he valiantly repelled all the subtle devices of Satan, whether consisting in many severe threats, or in fair promises of the kingdom of this world. Nothing could move him to forsake Christ.

Jacques was condemned to death by the rulers of the darkness of this world. Consequently, he testified and confirmed the true faith with his death and blood and, through grace, obtained the crown of everlasting glory.

Now let us fast forward from this scene to 469 years later. Times have changed. Men, women, and children are no longer thrown into cold dungeons for their faith, at least not here in North America. But the enemy of our soul is the same. He may not go around as a roaring lion, but he surely comes around as an angel of light.

Dear youth, you may not realize it, but today you are on trial. Your faith and convictions are being challenged. Satan, in the form of the Lady Frieslands of today, is questioning you. In her audience are the worldly-wise men, the progressive Protestants, and even some contemporary folks bearing the Anabaptist name.

“Why are you looking so pious?” asks Lady Friesland. “In this day and age, you need to loosen up. How do you expect to win the world when you appear so somber?”

You are the Jacques of today, so what is your answer?

Lady Friesland continues, “You claim to be part of a separated people. Yet I see you immersing yourselves into sports, hunting, and fishing. I see you following fashions. How are you different from other Christians? Or even from the world for that matter?”

Jacques, do you have any convictions of your own? Do your choices make a difference in eternity for yourself or others? Are your lifestyle decisions a life-or-death matter to you?

Seductively, Lady Friesland leans in closer and whispers, “What does it matter? Your parents are old-fashioned. Everyone does it today. Just doing it once is harmless. Why are you such a prude?”

Jacques, is the Bible in your heart like it was with Jacques of old? Do you know and love the Word? Can you withstand temptation?

Now Lady Friesland comes from a different angle. “Why do you wear that small covering on your head? What does it mean to today’s culture? Nothing. Enlightened Christians are getting rid of it everywhere. And young Jacques, don’t you think that girl at your side who you are courting would look prettier with that covering gone? It’s just a symbol anyway.”

Jacques and Jacqueline, will you stand true to God? Do you have a ready answer?

It is time to take a serious reflection of your faith and convictions. Jacques, in his youth, was standing to become the church of tomorrow in his day. Today you are Jacques. Tomorrow the church will consist of you and all the Jacqueses and Jacquelines who are around you today. Is this a church you want to be a part of? Are you satisfied with what you see? Are you satisfied with your own lifestyle convictions and faith? Will they carry you through when the raging battles of life hit?

So, dear youth of today, will you take some time to honestly consider your personal life in the mirror of God’s Word? If God’s Spirit gives you an answer of peace and rest, praise the Lord. If in any way your heart is troubled, or convicted, don’t become discouraged. Remember it is …the goodness of God [that] leadeth thee to repentance –Rom 2:4.

„Gnädige Frau, ich danke Ihnen sehr für Ihre Zuneigung und Ihre Gunst mir gegenüber, aber ich habe mich ganz Gott hingegeben, um sein Freund zu sein, und darauf hoffe ich zu leben und zu sterben“, lauteten die selbstbewussten, glaubensstarken Worte von Jacques „schak“ (einer französischen Form des männlichen Namens Jakob oder James).

Im Jahr 1550 wütete die Verfolgung in Europa mit großer Härte. Weil sie ihren Glauben an Jesus Christus bekannten, wurden Männer, Frauen und sogar Kinder aus ihren Häusern und Versammlungsorten gerissen und in die dunklen und kalten Kerkerzellen der Schlösser in der Umgebung geworfen. Unter diesen Gefangenen fand sich der fünfzehnjährige Jacques Dosie in Leeuwarden in Holland inhaftiert, weil er an der Wahrheit des Evangeliums festhielt. Obwohl er erst fünfzehn Jahre alt war, war er für sein aufrechtes Zeugnis und seine Kenntnis der Schrift bekannt und verherrlichte durch die Kraft des Geistes Gott.

Der Herr und die Herrin von Friesland waren mit vielen Edelleuten und Damen in den königlichen Sälen in Leeuwarden versammelt. Ihr Gespräch kam auf die „baptistischen Ketzer“, die das Land bevölkerten.

„Bringen wir den jungen Burschen Jacques herein. Sicher ist er von dieser Ketzerei noch nicht allzu sehr verdorben.“

Also wurde er hereingebracht, um verhört zu werden. Der Herr von Friesland sagte nur wenige Worte und schien es eilig zu haben, zum Ende zu kommen. Für dieses Gerede über Religion hatte er keine Zeit, zumal die Gäste auf eine unterhaltsamere Darbietung warteten. Die Herrin von Friesland hingegen schien Mitleid mit dem jungen Mann zu haben, der so grausam im Kerker gefesselt war.

„Warum bist du im Gefängnis? Du bist doch noch ein Junge. Was hat dich hierhergebracht?“, fragte sie.

Jacques antwortete: „Ich wurde gefangen genommen und ins Gefängnis geworfen, nur weil ich an Jesus Christus glaube. Ich halte allein an ihm fest und werde ihn nicht verleugnen.“

Die königliche Dame fragte ihn: „Du gehörst doch nicht zu jenen Ketzern, die sich selbst erneut taufen ließen und so viel Böses in unserem Land angerichtet haben? Sie sagen, sie seien ihres Glaubens wegen zerstreut und brüsten sich damit, die Kirche Gottes zu sein. Aber sie sind ein gottloses und rebellisches Volk und stiften im Land große Unruhe.“

„Gnädige Frau, ich kenne keine rebellischen Menschen, und ich gehöre auch nicht zu ihnen“, erwiderte Jacques. „Doch viel lieber würden wir nach den Lehren der Schrift unseren Feinden helfen. Wenn sie hungern und dürsten, versorgen wir sie mit Speise und Trank. Wir vergelten es ihnen niemals mit Rache oder Gewalt, wie wir in Matthäus 5,39 lesen.“

„Wenn du in einer Machtposition wärst, würde sich zeigen, ob du deinen Feinden helfen würdest“, höhnte einer der Edelleute.

Jacques erwiderte: „O nein, mein Herr, selbst wenn es uns erlaubt wäre, dem Bösen mit dem fleischlichen Schwert zu widerstehen, würde ich es niemals tun.“

„Ich weiß, dass es unter euch Sekten gibt, die sehr böse sind und Menschen töten. Sie haben ihren Besitz und ihre Frauen gemeinsam“, sagte die Herrin von Friesland.

„O nein“, erwiderte Jacques. „Diese bösen Dinge werden uns zu Unrecht vorgeworfen. Man beschuldigt uns fälschlich des Bösen, um uns verfolgen zu können. Doch wie in Matthäus 5,11 gelehrt wird, müssen wir all dies geduldig erleiden und ertragen.“

„Waren es nicht eure Leute, die sich unter großer Schande gegen die Regierung in Amsterdam und Münster bewaffneten?“, fragte die Herrin von Friesland.

„Nein, gnädige Frau, wir gehören nicht zu ihnen“, antwortete Jacques. „Diese Leute irrten schwer. Wir betrachten es als eine Lehre des Teufels, den Obrigkeiten mit dem Schwert und mit Gewalt zu widerstehen. Viel lieber würden wir Verfolgung und Tod durch die Obrigkeiten erleiden.“

„Dennoch hält man dich für einen von ihnen, weil auch du im Land Unruhe stiftest“, beharrte die königliche Dame. „Doch ich glaube, was du über jene Münsteraner sagst.“

„Aber, gnädige Frau, lesen wir nicht in Apostelgeschichte 24,5, wie böse Menschen schlecht über die Apostel selbst und die ganze Schar der Christen redeten?“, entgegnete Jacques. „Versuchten böse Menschen nicht, die Obrigkeiten zur Rache an den Christen aufzustacheln, obwohl alles erlogen war?“

Die Herrin von Friesland antwortete nicht, sondern wechselte rasch das Thema. „Glaubst du, dass alle verdammt sind, die nicht nach eurer Art getauft sind?“, fragte sie.

„O nein, gnädige Frau“, antwortete Jacques. „Das Urteil über andere Menschen steht allein Gott zu, der jedem nach seinen Werken vergelten wird. Das wird an vielen Stellen der Heiligen Schrift klar gesagt. Außerdem hat das Wasser nicht die Kraft, uns von der Sünde zu reinigen, wie 1. Petrus 3,21 sagt, sondern ist lediglich ein Zeichen für allen Gehorsam.“

„Kannst du nach deiner Taufe noch sündigen?“, fragte die Herrin von Friesland.

„Ja, gnädige Frau, denn das geht aus den Worten des Paulus in Römer 7,18 klar hervor“, erwiderte Jacques. „Wir sind noch immer mit einem schwachen und sündigen Leib bekleidet und sündigen in vielerlei Hinsicht. Doch wir müssen das Fleisch beständig kreuzigen und abtöten und die Werke des Fleisches weder ausüben noch vollbringen. Wenn wir dies versäumen, wird die Gerechtigkeit Gottes uns zum ewigen Tod verurteilen.“

Die Herrin von Friesland wurde zunehmend aufgebracht. „Warum hörst du nicht auf den Inquisitor der Kirche?“, verlangte sie.

Jacques erwiderte: „Gnädige Frau, weil ich seine Lehre nicht annehmen werde, solange er mir nicht klar beweisen kann, dass sie in allen Punkten mit dem Wort Gottes übereinstimmt. Andernfalls müht er sich vergeblich. Mein Glaube gründet allein auf dem reinen Wort Gottes. Was die Kindertaufe angeht, so widerlege ich sein Argument mit Vernunft, denn sie ist kein Gebot des allmächtigen Gottes, sondern vielmehr eine menschliche Erfindung. Säuglinge haben nicht die geringste Kenntnis oder Unterscheidungsfähigkeit hinsichtlich dessen, was für die Taufe erforderlich ist. Christus aber hat in seiner Liebe zu solchen Unschuldigen ihnen aus Gnade das Reich Gottes verheißen, ohne die Taufe zu verlangen.

„Und außerdem, gnädige Frau, stelle ich fest, dass die römische Kirche neben diesem Irrtum von vielen weiteren Irrtümern befallen ist. Sie wollen Christus ins Brot hineinbringen oder bewirken, dass Brot und Wein sich in sein Fleisch und Blut verwandeln. Das glaube ich nicht, sondern halte es für einen äußerst groben Irrtum und eine Absurdität. Ich glaube aber, dass Christus tatsächlich in den Himmel aufgefahren ist und zur Rechten seines Vaters sitzt, wie wir in Markus 16,19 lesen. In ihrem Mehl, ihrer Messe, ihrem Fegefeuer oder irgendeinem ihrer Totendienste gibt es keine Erlösung. All ihre menschlichen Erfindungen – und es gibt viele davon – finden in der Heiligen Schrift nirgends Anerkennung. Wir hingegen rufen Gott an und suchen unser Heil bei ihm. Unser Heil liegt in keiner menschlichen Schöpfung, damit wir nicht Gottes eigene Herrlichkeit schmälern und sie irgendeinem seiner Geschöpfe zuschreiben.“

An diesem Punkt unterbrach der ebenfalls anwesende Bürgermeister: „Glaubst du also nicht an das Sakrament, das Christus selbst eingesetzt hat?“

„Mein Herr, Paulus sagt, dass das Brot zu seinem Gedächtnis gebrochen wird und dass der Kelch des Segens die Gemeinschaft am Blut Christi ist“, erwiderte Jacques.

Der Bürgermeister wusste darauf nichts zu erwidern.

„Das Schlimmste an euch ist meiner Meinung nach, dass ihr die Kinder nicht taufen lasst“, stellte die Herrin von Friesland fest. „Ganz Deutschland und jedes Königreich halten euer Tun für Ketzerei.“

„Es stimmt tatsächlich, dass wir überall verachtet werden, so wie es auch den Aposteln erging“, erwiderte Jacques. „Aber wir glauben nicht, dass ungetaufte Kinder am Tag des Gerichts zugrunde gehen werden.“

„Mein liebes Kind“, sagte die Dame flehend. „Komm auf unsere Seite und bereue, dann wirst du aus dieser Notlage herauskommen. Ich verspreche dir, deine Freilassung zu erwirken.“

„Gnädige Frau, ich danke Ihnen sehr für Ihre Zuneigung und Ihre Gunst mir gegenüber“, antwortete Jacques mutig. „Doch ich werde meinen Glauben nicht ändern, um einem sterblichen Menschen zu gefallen, es sei denn, es wird mir durch die Schrift bewiesen. Ich habe mich ganz Gott hingegeben, um sein Freund zu sein, und darauf hoffe ich zu leben und zu sterben.“

„Mein Sohn, ich habe Mitleid mit dir“, flehte sie erneut. „Bereue deine Taufe und sei nicht so starrsinnig. Es wäre ein schweres Kreuz für mein Herz, wenn du für diese Sache sterben solltest, wo du doch noch so jung bist. Wenn du bereust, werde ich dafür sorgen, dass du freigelassen wirst und nach Hause gehen kannst.“

„Ich sehe überhaupt kein Verbrechen in meiner Taufe. Ich bin nicht meiner eigenen Sache gefolgt, sondern der heiligen Ordnung unseres Herrn Jesus Christus. Ich konnte keinen besseren Weg zum Reich Gottes finden als durch die Taufe“, erwiderte Jacques. „Ich bin entschlossen, den Herrn, meinen Gott, mit ganzem Herzen zu suchen.“

„Sieh dir all diese Männer um dich herum an. Wagst du wirklich so vermessen zu behaupten, sie alle irrten?“, fragte die Herrin von Friesland.

„Gnädige Frau“, erwiderte Jacques. „In Israel standen vierhundert Propheten gegen den Propheten Micha, der als Einziger die Wahrheit sprach. Weil er die Wahrheit sagte, wurde er bei Wasser und Brot gefangen gehalten. Später erkannte König Ahab in seiner Not, dass der Prophet Micha die Wahrheit gesprochen hatte, doch da war es zu spät. Wir lesen davon in 2. Chronik 18.“

Schließlich sagte die Dame: „Ich finde vieles Gute an dir; doch dein größter Irrtum liegt in deiner Taufe. Mir scheint nicht, dass sie von Gott ist.“

Die Herrin von Friesland ließ Jacques viele Male vor sich führen. Obwohl er noch jung an Jahren war, war er in der Erkenntnis Jesu Christi reif. Er hatte sein Fundament auf den Felsen Jesus Christus gebaut. Mit dem Schwert des Geistes, dem Wort Gottes, wehrte er tapfer alle listigen Anschläge Satans ab, mochten sie in vielen schrecklichen Drohungen oder in verlockenden Versprechungen des Reiches dieser Welt bestehen. Nichts konnte ihn dazu bringen, Christus zu verleugnen.

Jacques wurde von den Herrschern der Finsternis dieser Welt zum Tode verurteilt. So bezeugte und bestätigte er den wahren Glauben mit seinem Tod und seinem Blut und erlangte durch Gnade die Krone ewiger Herrlichkeit.

Springen wir nun von dieser Szene 469 Jahre weiter. Die Zeiten haben sich geändert. Männer, Frauen und Kinder werden nicht mehr ihres Glaubens wegen in kalte Kerker geworfen, zumindest nicht hier in Nordamerika. Doch der Feind unserer Seele ist derselbe. Vielleicht geht er nicht als brüllender Löwe umher, aber ganz gewiss kommt er als Engel des Lichts daher.

Liebe Jugendliche, vielleicht ist euch nicht bewusst, dass ihr heute auf dem Prüfstand steht. Euer Glaube und eure Überzeugungen werden hinterfragt. Satan stellt euch Fragen in Gestalt der heutigen Herrinnen von Friesland. In ihrem Gefolge befinden sich weltkluge Männer, fortschrittliche Protestanten und sogar einige Zeitgenossen, die den Namen der Täufer tragen.

„Warum schaut ihr so fromm drein?“, fragt die Herrin von Friesland. „In der heutigen Zeit müsst ihr euch lockern. Wie wollt ihr die Welt gewinnen, wenn ihr so ernst wirkt?“

Ihr seid die Jacques von heute – was ist also eure Antwort?

Die Herrin von Friesland fährt fort: „Ihr behauptet, Teil eines abgesonderten Volkes zu sein. Doch ich sehe, wie ihr euch in Sport, Jagd und Fischerei verstrickt. Ich sehe, wie ihr Moden folgt. Worin unterscheidet ihr euch von anderen Christen? Oder überhaupt von der Welt?“

Jacques, hast du eigene Überzeugungen? Haben deine Entscheidungen für dich oder andere einen Unterschied in der Ewigkeit? Sind deine Lebensentscheidungen für dich eine Frage von Leben und Tod?

Verführerisch beugt sich die Herrin von Friesland näher zu dir und flüstert: „Was macht das schon? Deine Eltern sind altmodisch. Heutzutage macht es jeder. Es ist doch harmlos, es nur einmal zu tun. Warum bist du so prüde?“

Jacques, ist die Bibel in deinem Herzen, wie sie es bei Jacques vor langer Zeit war? Kennst und liebst du das Wort? Kannst du der Versuchung widerstehen?

Nun versucht die Herrin von Friesland es von einer anderen Seite. „Warum trägst du diese kleine Kopfbedeckung? Was bedeutet sie in der heutigen Kultur? Nichts. Überall legen aufgeklärte Christen sie ab. Und junger Jacques, meinst du nicht, das Mädchen an deiner Seite, mit dem du dich triffst, sähe ohne diese Bedeckung hübscher aus? Sie ist doch ohnehin nur ein Symbol.“

Jacques und Jacqueline, werdet ihr Gott treu bleiben? Habt ihr eine Antwort bereit?

Es ist an der Zeit, ernsthaft über euren Glauben und eure Überzeugungen nachzudenken. Jacques stand in seiner Jugend im Begriff, die Kirche seiner Zeit von morgen zu werden. Heute seid ihr Jacques. Morgen wird die Kirche aus euch und all den Jacques und Jacquelines bestehen, die heute um euch herum sind. Ist dies eine Kirche, zu der ihr gehören wollt? Seid ihr mit dem zufrieden, was ihr seht? Seid ihr mit euren eigenen Überzeugungen zu Lebensführung und Glauben zufrieden? Werden sie euch tragen, wenn die heftigen Kämpfe des Lebens hereinbrechen?

Liebe Jugendliche von heute, nehmt euch also Zeit, euer persönliches Leben ehrlich im Spiegel des Wortes Gottes zu prüfen. Wenn Gottes Geist euch eine Antwort des Friedens und der Ruhe gibt, preist den Herrn. Wenn euer Herz in irgendeiner Weise beunruhigt oder überführt ist, lasst euch nicht entmutigen. Denkt daran: …die Güte Gottes [führt] dich zur Buße – Römer 2,4.

Do not classify a synonym, grammatical alternative, punctuation preference, or correct idiomatic rendering as a major error. An unchanged proper name, established title of a cited work, or identifier is not by itself an untranslated substantive passage; judge its role in context. This does not exempt quoted prose or translatable article metadata. Any substantiated meaning, theology, omission, attribution, or reference error still requires a narrowly scoped correction in the target language. Do not invent findings merely to justify rejection. A suggested fix identical to the candidate is not an error and must not be reported. If the score meets the task's threshold and there are no substantive major or critical findings, set passed=true; minor findings alone do not justify passed=false.

Scripture quotations and other quoted substantive prose are translated as article text in this workflow, faithfully conveying the authoritative English as printed. Fidelity means preserving the printed meaning, not retaining English wording. Do not substitute another Bible version or require the translator to copy, retain, or restore English quoted prose as a fidelity workaround. Book names should use conventional target-language forms while preserving the exact chapter/verse numbers, ranges and the number and placement of references. Check the printed Scripture reference identities in context. Do not confuse clock notation with Scripture. When a source clock has no explicit AM/PM period, preserve its printed hour and minute exactly; do not infer an unprinted period.

Review source.html, source.title, source.subtitle, and source.section against the corresponding candidate fields. source_context.byline is attribution context only and is rendered separately by the website. Its absence from the translation is not an omission and must not lower the score or produce a finding. Do not request a new byline field or a paragraph such as p.byline. Preserve attribution already inside source.html in its existing structure. Suggested corrections must preserve HTML tags, attributes, links, images, and article structure. Compare every paragraph, heading, list item, quotation, poem line, note, caption, and image description in context. When an accepted_baseline is supplied, identify substantive regressions and correctable defects without demanding stylistic rewrites of already correct wording.

Return strict JSON with score (integer 0 through 100), passed (boolean), and findings (array). Each finding contains severity (minor/major/critical), location, source_quote, translation_quote, and suggested_fix, all textual. Quote concrete source and candidate evidence and propose an actionable, narrowly scoped correction. Return an empty findings array when there are no problems. Do not rewrite the article or add commentary.

Review response contract version 2: return no more than 30 findings, and also return findings_complete (boolean). Examine the complete article and metadata before assigning the score and verdict. The response limit never permits overlooking a substantive error or raising the score to make the result fit.

Prioritize critical findings, then major findings, then minor findings. Combine repeated instances only when they are the same underlying defect, retaining every affected location and the concrete source/translation evidence needed to repair them. Keep findings concise and actionable. Do not invent a finding merely to describe a reporting limit.

Set findings_complete=true only when all substantiated findings identified in this review are represented without omitted locations or evidence. If all identified findings cannot fit in 30 entries and the available response space, return the most serious substantiated findings, set findings_complete=false, and set passed=false. Do not claim the report is complete by silently dropping remaining findings. This marker describes whether the report includes what you found; it is not a claim that every possible error has been discovered. Return the existing score, passed, and findings fields as well. A report marked incomplete cannot approve publication.

Only substantiated major or critical meaning, omission, attribution, fact, or reference errors block approval; minor stylistic alternatives do not.
