Behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud –Exo 16:10.

What a strange phenomenon is this concentrated mass of vapor that navigates the sky above us. In one instance, a cloud can minister such immense blessedness and hope, while in another it can be the instigator of nagging uncertainty and even the arousal of ragged fear. Clouds were often, no doubt, the welcome shade to the heads of weary fishermen upon Galilee and the propagator of hope to the toiling farmer. How often these clouds part at midday to allow the sun’s beaming rays access to the earth. Then in the evening, they provide the opaque structure for the exquisite beauty of a silver lineation.

We may marvel to see an airplane weighing over 700,000 pounds mount up with wings and soar through the heavens, yet a cloud can carry millions of tons of water without any of the dynamics of human intervention. Clouds are formed when moist, warm air rises to a cooler elevation and water condenses onto microscopic “seeds” such as dust, ash, or bacteria. If there’s more water vapor than places on which it can condense, then ice crystals can also serve as seeds and take on moisture—He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them –Job 26:8. Eventually, these seeds become too heavy for updrafts to support, and then, behold, it is time for the umbrella.

To the parched land in Elijah’s day, the smallest of clouds (like a man’s hand in 1 Kings 18:44) was the answer from the Almighty that He was again prepared to bless His people with rain. Yet, to others like Job and Jeremiah, the cloud represented the ultimate emblem of doubt, despair, and discouragement. Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud –Job 30:15, and Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through –Lam 3:44. It is often in such stressful conditions that God chooses to hide Himself in a cloud. At these times, we grope through the thick foreboding fog in search of the pathway of light, but we find it not. In our discouragement, we may long for the beam of a cloudless day, but it eludes us. We know that God is in the midst of the mist, but we cannot apprehend Him, nor see His blessedness. With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt –Job 36:32.

Why would our God, who loves to commune with us, the vessels of His own creation, choose to hide Himself in a cloud? Why does He often hide His will from our searching and aching hearts? Our finite minds often wonder what glory could possibly arise from such a seemingly distant God, and …to what purpose is this waste –Mat 26:8. While we would never expect it to be God’s divine plan to leave us in a foggy stupor forever, it may be His will for a time. Like a stroll through the valley of the shadow of death, there can be eternal character wrought in the soul who has experienced a seasonal lack of clarity in their path. We are well aware that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Pro 4:18. Still, most of us have, at times, experienced the hopeless fog that surrounds our present and our future. In these times, we meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night –Job 5:14. In our bedraggled discouragement, we can easily lose sight of the goodness of God. Our resulting lack of thankfulness is a sure road to a host of other temptations, while the giant of despair rises overhead in an attempt to weaken our resistance to sin.

We know that Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are –Jam 5:17. Yet, few of us have ever experienced a victory as exhilarating as he did when he triumphed over the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Still, many of us can well relate to the discouragement that followed as he came unto Horeb and lodged in a cave there. This is the same place as Mount Sinai where the first great mountain scene opened before us in the Scriptures. Then it was Moses who met God in the cloud. The law was given, and God’s glory was so marvelously manifested and so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake –Heb 12:21. This mount that might be touched was a formidable and intimidating mountain flanked by splintering dark granite peaks and stern ridges of indescribable grandeur. The bold and awful front of Horeb, rises in frowning majesty from twelve hundred to fifteen hundred feet in perpendicular height.

With Elijah’s vision clouded over and his spirit ebbing away at an all-time low, God responded to him in astounding methodology—…And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out… –1 Kin 19:11-13.

Somehow, we have come to believe that an earthshaking experience is the epitome of God’s manifest presence. We reckon that God was closer to Elijah on Mt. Carmel than He was on Mt. Horeb. It was Elijah’s “day in the sun” while speaking on Mt. Carmel. He chided the people and mocked the prophets. He preached boldly in the name of the Lord and commanded the people to repent of their duplicity. But now his voice has been silenced and he is listening … listening to the still small voice calling into account his own actions and ambitions. Thus, if we will but stop and listen, the memory of our dismal failures will escort us to the front porch of our Lord, rather than allow us to glory in our perceived successes.

This is the blessed ministration of the cloud. It is often the vehicle that the Lord will use to bring us to the place where we can truly receive His manifest glory in our hearts. This is not the white, fluffy, cumulus clouds of a balmy summer day but, rather, the flat and featureless stratus clouds that blanket the heavens from east to west and totally eclipse all the rays of heavenly sunshine. They can enshroud the day at high noon with an arsenal of gloom that rankles our hearts to the core. The little things, that on other days had little effect on our attitudes, now seem to tower as giants before us. We may face advents that we know are beyond our control, but our minds refuse to enter into rest. In times like these, if there happens to be an unfortunate soul on the other end of our conversation experiencing a similar plight, we may experience firsthand that …man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward –Job 5:7. At other times, our melancholy mood may be content to withdraw and feed itself with our own reclusive pity and foggy misery.

Some, in their desperation, turn to medication for the mind and there find a limited valve of relief. But God has not brought us into the cloud so that we may seek the help of physicians and psychologists. The ministration of the cloud is to shut off all other alternatives so that we may receive of Him the full blessedness of His consolation. God is willing that we should sacrifice the shimmering sunshine of today for the fullness of His presence tomorrow.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. In bygone years, I have preached on this verse, exhorting souls concerning the brevity of life and encouraging them to not squander their years away. But I had totally ignored the foundation of it—ye know not what shall be on the morrow. This, perhaps, seems trite to the young at heart, but as the fruit of my age continues to ripen, I have a growing appreciation for the common and obvious idioms. Our modern scientific world is so adamantly pursuing the love of life that it cannot appreciate the life of love that is begotten through suffering. While those who, in ages past, suffered in the flesh and ceased from sin (1 Pet 4:1), I see no reason why those who experience the frail sufferings of a clouded mind may not share the same glory if they will but endure and trust to God the results.

We are an arrogant people who lean on the predictions of tomorrow. We fancy that we can plan our retirement and schedule our life events with immaculate detail. The weather forecasters tell us of tomorrows temperature so that we can meticulously plan our day. Our insurance gives assurance that we will not be subject to future poverty. Our freezers and bank accounts are full enough to see us well past tomorrow, and we have grown accustomed to believing that we …sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow –Rev 18:7. Yet the sorrow of heart cannot be so easily absolved by earthly amenities. Our life is a vapour (cloud) because we …know not what shall be on the morrow… –Jas 4:14. In spite of all our technology we still cannot absolve that fact. It is here that we must lay aside all our intuitions, expectations, and ambitions of what our life ought to be and find our God in the cloud.

He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it –Job 26:9. To what benefit is the cloud covering the face of God’s throne? If it were easily beholden, most of us would be content to dwell with Him from afar. However, due to the impending fog, we must draw nigh to experience His fullness. How thankful we ought to be that it is thus, for how devastating would be our spiritual loss if it were not so.

If our self-sufficient life was always vibrantly full and God were easily apprehended, we would lose…

…Faith

We seek a guarantee that our trials will end happily ever after and that our prayers will naturally become unnecessary. In faith, we believe in God’s provision, but the fact that we know not what a day will bring demands that we fall upon our feeble knees and pray. There may be many things that make it hard for us to trust in God, but the shrouded tomorrow makes it easier. Researchers have spent millions in their efforts to control the weather. They have sown every imaginable cloud seed into the air in efforts to produce rain clouds. After reviewing 40 years of cloud-seeding efforts in an area north of Israel, researchers at Tel Aviv University have concluded that cloud seeding doesn’t actually produce any additional precipitation. How thankful we should be. The more we can control the unknown morrow, the less faith in the Master of the Universe we need.

Jacob, in leaving behind an angry brother, a disappointed father, and a severed tie with his mother, faced an altogether unknown future. This is a part of the ladder to the throne and it fortifies our commitment to our omnipotent God. Now we know in part and we see in part. Perhaps that fractional sliver brings us more inner wealth than if the whole were fully understood. If our future were amply within our manipulative power, we would formulate a perfect utopia supplied with the perfect number of children living sumptuously in the perfect home supported by the perfect job surrounded by perfect behavior that is perfectly sterile and dead.

…Hope

I question if we realize how deeply our debt is to the unexpected. The Hebrew writer declares our hope to be …an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast… –Heb 6:19. Children are happy because they have big dreams. Often the anticipation and planning of an event is almost as thrilling as the excursion itself. Every day is a bright new window to the unspoiled, hopeful mind. Experiences can often bring us to the brink of cynicism and bitterness when viewed through yesterday’s disappointments. Jacob, upon the marvelous reunification with his son, Joseph, still remarked, few and evil have been my days. Though it is naturally so, it needs not to be. Paul states …that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope –Rom 5:3-4. Surely, if we knew what was in store tomorrow (both good and evil) the invigorating element of hope would dwindle. Eve feigned that life would be better if she could only secure more knowledge. But what blessed hope was forfeited in her lustful pursuit of clarity.

…Love

There is a wistful tenderness in love that nothing but uncertainty can give. It is uncertain wonder that encompasses the way of a young man with a maid. The unknown perils of tomorrow drive a mother to love and prayer for her children. It is the vision of a brighter tomorrow for his family that moves a father to diligence in his daily work. Wherever a husband and his wife are knit together in Biblical oneness of holy matrimony, the mystery that envelops tomorrow is like the minor chord in a great melody. It speaks in joy of a suggested sorrow and brightens sorrow with encircling joy. Would Jacob’s seven-year wait have seemed like a few days if he had known what the morrow would bring? If we knew everything, love would be too hard. If we knew everything, love would be too easy. If we knew everything, we would be brokenhearted. If we knew everything, we would be unconcerned. In other words, it makes us stronger to not know the worst and it makes us more tender to not know the best. For in our clouded and darkened lens there …abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Cor 13:13.

It is no coincidence that while the disciples …beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight –Act 1:9. And so we dare not be surprised that, at times, we shall be called to suffer the mental strain and stress of an obscure and unknown tomorrow. …For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. There is coming a day when we shall …see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory –Luk 21:27. And again it is written, Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him … Even so, Amen –Rev 1:7.

Voici que la gloire de l’Éternel apparut dans la nuée –Ex 16:10.

Quel étrange phénomène que cette masse concentrée de vapeur qui navigue dans le ciel au-dessus de nous ! Dans un cas, un nuage peut apporter une immense bénédiction et une grande espérance ; dans un autre, il peut être à l’origine d’une incertitude tenace et même susciter une peur désordonnée. Les nuages étaient souvent, sans aucun doute, une ombre bienvenue pour les têtes des pêcheurs épuisés sur la mer de Galilée et porteurs d’espérance pour les agriculteurs laborieux. Que de fois ces nuages se dissipent à midi pour laisser les rayons lumineux du soleil atteindre la terre ! Puis, le soir, ils offrent un écrin opaque à l’exquise beauté d’un liseré argenté.

Nous pouvons nous émerveiller de voir un avion pesant plus de 700 000 livres s’élever sur ses ailes et planer dans les cieux ; pourtant, un nuage peut porter des millions de tonnes d’eau sans aucune intervention humaine. Les nuages se forment lorsque de l’air chaud et humide s’élève vers une altitude plus froide et que l’eau se condense sur des « noyaux » microscopiques tels que la poussière, les cendres ou les bactéries. S’il y a davantage de vapeur d’eau que de surfaces sur lesquelles elle peut se condenser, des cristaux de glace peuvent aussi servir de noyaux et absorber l’humidité — Il renferme les eaux dans ses nuées épaisses, et les nuages ne se déchirent pas sous leur poids –Job 26:8. Finalement, ces noyaux deviennent trop lourds pour être soutenus par les courants ascendants, et alors, voici venu le temps du parapluie.

Pour la terre desséchée du temps d’Élie, le plus petit des nuages (comme une main d’homme en 1 Rois 18:44) était la réponse du Tout-Puissant, qui se tenait de nouveau prêt à bénir son peuple par la pluie. Pourtant, pour d’autres, comme Job et Jérémie, le nuage représentait le symbole ultime du doute, du désespoir et du découragement. Les terreurs fondent sur moi ; elles poursuivent mon âme comme le vent, et mon bien-être s’évanouit comme un nuage –Job 30:15, et Tu t’es enveloppé d’une nuée, afin que la prière ne puisse te parvenir –Lm 3:44. C’est souvent dans de telles circonstances éprouvantes que Dieu choisit de se cacher dans un nuage. Alors, nous tâtonnons dans un épais brouillard sinistre à la recherche du chemin de la lumière, mais nous ne le trouvons pas. Dans notre découragement, nous pouvons aspirer aux rayons d’une journée sans nuages, mais ils nous échappent. Nous savons que Dieu est au milieu de la brume, mais nous ne pouvons ni le saisir ni voir sa bonté. Il cache la lumière sous les nuages et lui commande de ne pas briller, car un nuage s’interpose –Job 36:32.

Pourquoi notre Dieu, qui aime communier avec nous, les vases de sa propre création, choisirait-il de se cacher dans un nuage ? Pourquoi cache-t-il souvent sa volonté à nos cœurs qui la cherchent et en souffrent ? Nos esprits limités se demandent souvent quelle gloire pourrait bien naître d’un Dieu apparemment si distant, et …à quoi bon cette perte ? –Mt 26:8. Même si nous ne nous attendrions jamais à ce que le plan divin de Dieu soit de nous laisser éternellement dans la stupeur d’un brouillard, sa volonté peut être que cela dure un temps. Comme une promenade dans la vallée de l’ombre de la mort, une période de manque de clarté sur le chemin peut façonner un caractère éternel dans l’âme de celui qui l’a vécue. Nous savons bien que le sentier des justes est comme la lumière resplendissante, dont l’éclat va croissant jusqu’au milieu du jour –Pr 4:18. Pourtant, la plupart d’entre nous avons connu, parfois, le brouillard sans espoir qui enveloppe notre présent et notre avenir. En ces moments-là, nous rencontrons l’obscurité en plein jour, et tâtonnons à midi comme dans la nuit –Job 5:14. Dans notre profond découragement, nous pouvons facilement perdre de vue la bonté de Dieu. L’ingratitude qui en résulte mène à coup sûr à quantité d’autres tentations, tandis que le géant du désespoir se dresse au-dessus de nous pour tenter d’affaiblir notre résistance au péché.

Nous savons qu’Élie était un homme de la même nature que nous –Jc 5:17. Pourtant, peu d’entre nous ont jamais connu une victoire aussi exaltante que la sienne, lorsqu’il triompha des prophètes de Baal sur le mont Carmel. Toutefois, beaucoup d’entre nous peuvent bien comprendre le découragement qui suivit, lorsqu’il arriva à Horeb et logea dans une grotte. C’est le même lieu que le mont Sinaï, où la première grande scène de montagne s’ouvrit devant nous dans les Écritures. Alors, c’est Moïse qui rencontra Dieu dans la nuée. La loi fut donnée, et la gloire de Dieu se manifesta si merveilleusement, et cette vue était si terrible que Moïse dit : Je suis épouvanté et tout tremblant –He 12:21. Cette montagne qu’on pouvait toucher était une montagne imposante et intimidante, flanquée de pics de granite sombre qui se fragmentaient et de crêtes austères d’une grandeur indescriptible. La face audacieuse et redoutable d’Horeb s’élève dans une majesté menaçante, de douze cents à quinze cents pieds à la verticale.

Alors que la vision d’Élie s’obscurcissait et que son esprit déclinait, tombé au plus bas, Dieu lui répondit d’une manière stupéfiante — …Et voici, l’Éternel passa. Un vent fort et violent déchirait les montagnes et brisait les rochers devant l’Éternel ; l’Éternel n’était pas dans le vent. Après le vent, il y eut un tremblement de terre ; l’Éternel n’était pas dans le tremblement de terre. Après le tremblement de terre, un feu ; l’Éternel n’était pas dans le feu. Après le feu, une voix douce, légère. Lorsque Élie l’entendit, il se couvrit le visage de son manteau et sortit… –1 R 19:11-13.

D’une manière ou d’une autre, nous en sommes venus à croire qu’une expérience qui ébranle la terre est l’apogée de la présence manifeste de Dieu. Nous pensons que Dieu était plus proche d’Élie au mont Carmel qu’au mont Horeb. Ce fut le « jour de gloire » d’Élie lorsqu’il parla au mont Carmel. Il réprimanda le peuple et se moqua des prophètes. Il prêcha hardiment au nom du Seigneur et ordonna au peuple de se repentir de sa duplicité. Mais maintenant, sa voix s’est tue et il écoute… il écoute la voix douce, légère qui l’interpelle au sujet de ses propres actes et ambitions. Ainsi, si seulement nous nous arrêtions pour écouter, le souvenir de nos échecs lamentables nous conduirait devant le porche de notre Seigneur, au lieu de nous laisser nous glorifier de nos succès présumés.

Telle est la bienfaisante action du nuage. Il est souvent le moyen dont le Seigneur se sert pour nous conduire au lieu où nous pouvons véritablement recevoir la manifestation de sa gloire dans nos cœurs. Il ne s’agit pas des nuages blancs et duveteux, cumulus d’une douce journée d’été, mais plutôt de nuages stratus, plats et sans relief, qui couvrent le ciel d’est en ouest et éclipsent totalement tous les rayons du soleil céleste. Ils peuvent envelopper le jour en plein midi d’un arsenal de morosité qui nous ronge le cœur jusqu’à la moelle. Les petites choses qui, les autres jours, avaient peu d’effet sur nos attitudes semblent maintenant se dresser devant nous comme des géants. Nous pouvons être confrontés à des événements dont nous savons qu’ils échappent à notre contrôle, mais notre esprit refuse de trouver le repos. En de tels moments, si une âme malheureuse se trouve à l’autre bout de notre conversation et traverse une épreuve semblable, nous pouvons constater par nous-mêmes que …l’homme naît pour la souffrance, comme les étincelles s’élèvent pour voler –Job 5:7. D’autres fois, notre humeur mélancolique peut se contenter de se retirer et de se nourrir de notre propre apitoiement solitaire et de notre misère brumeuse.

Certains, dans leur désespoir, se tournent vers des médicaments pour l’esprit et y trouvent un soulagement limité. Mais Dieu ne nous a pas fait entrer dans le nuage pour que nous cherchions l’aide des médecins et des psychologues. L’action du nuage consiste à fermer toutes les autres issues afin que nous recevions de lui toute la plénitude de sa consolation. Dieu veut que nous sacrifiions le soleil éclatant d’aujourd’hui pour la plénitude de sa présence demain.

Vous qui ne savez pas ce qui arrivera demain ! Car qu’est-ce que votre vie ? Vous êtes une vapeur qui paraît pour un peu de temps, puis disparaît –Jc 4:14. Autrefois, j’ai prêché sur ce verset, exhortant les âmes au sujet de la brièveté de la vie et les encourageant à ne pas gaspiller leurs années. Mais j’en avais complètement ignoré le fondement — vous ne savez pas ce qui arrivera demain. Cela semble peut-être banal aux jeunes de cœur, mais, à mesure que le fruit de mon âge continue de mûrir, j’apprécie de plus en plus les expressions courantes et évidentes. Notre monde scientifique moderne poursuit avec tant d’acharnement l’amour de la vie qu’il ne peut apprécier la vie d’amour qui naît de la souffrance. Alors que ceux qui, autrefois, ont souffert dans la chair et cessé de pécher (1 Pi 4:1), je ne vois aucune raison pour laquelle ceux qui connaissent les souffrances fragiles d’un esprit obscurci ne pourraient pas partager la même gloire, s’ils persévèrent et confient les résultats à Dieu.

Nous sommes un peuple arrogant qui s’appuie sur les prédictions de demain. Nous nous imaginons pouvoir planifier notre retraite et organiser les événements de notre vie avec une précision impeccable. Les prévisionnistes météo nous indiquent la température de demain afin que nous puissions organiser minutieusement notre journée. Nos assurances nous garantissent que nous ne connaîtrons pas la pauvreté à l’avenir. Nos congélateurs et nos comptes bancaires sont suffisamment remplis pour nous permettre de voir bien au-delà de demain, et nous avons pris l’habitude de croire que nous …siège en reine, je ne suis pas veuve, et je ne verrai pas de deuil –Ap 18:7. Pourtant, le chagrin du cœur ne peut être si facilement effacé par les commodités terrestres. Notre vie est une vapeur (un nuage), parce que nous …ne savons pas ce qui arrivera demain… –Jc 4:14. Malgré toute notre technologie, nous ne pouvons toujours pas effacer ce fait. C’est ici que nous devons mettre de côté toutes nos intuitions, nos attentes et nos ambitions quant à ce que notre vie devrait être, et trouver notre Dieu dans le nuage.

Il cache la face de son trône et étend sa nuée sur lui –Job 26:9. À quoi sert le nuage qui couvre la face du trône de Dieu ? Si nous pouvions facilement le contempler, la plupart d’entre nous se contenteraient de vivre loin de lui. Cependant, à cause du brouillard qui nous menace, nous devons nous approcher pour faire l’expérience de sa plénitude. Comme nous devrions être reconnaissants qu’il en soit ainsi, car quelle perte spirituelle dévastatrice nous subirions s’il en était autrement !

Si notre vie autosuffisante était toujours débordante de vitalité et que Dieu était facile à saisir, nous perdrions…

…La foi

Nous cherchons la garantie que nos épreuves finiront bien et que nos prières deviendront naturellement inutiles. Par la foi, nous croyons que Dieu pourvoit à nos besoins, mais le fait que nous ne sachions pas ce qu’un jour nous apportera exige que nous tombions à genoux, dans notre faiblesse, pour prier. Bien des choses peuvent rendre difficile notre confiance en Dieu, mais le lendemain voilé par l’inconnu la facilite. Des chercheurs ont dépensé des millions dans leurs efforts pour maîtriser le temps. Ils ont semé dans l’air toutes les graines de nuages imaginables pour tenter de produire des nuages de pluie. Après avoir examiné quarante années d’efforts d’ensemencement des nuages dans une région au nord d’Israël, des chercheurs de l’université de Tel-Aviv ont conclu que l’ensemencement des nuages ne produit en réalité aucune précipitation supplémentaire. Nous devrions en être reconnaissants. Plus nous pouvons maîtriser le lendemain inconnu, moins nous avons besoin de foi dans le Maître de l’Univers.

En laissant derrière lui un frère en colère, un père déçu et les liens rompus avec sa mère, Jacob fit face à un avenir totalement inconnu. Cela fait partie de l’échelle qui mène au trône et renforce notre engagement envers notre Dieu tout-puissant. Nous ne connaissons qu’en partie et nous ne voyons qu’en partie. Peut-être cette mince fraction nous procure-t-elle une plus grande richesse intérieure que si nous comprenions pleinement le tout. Si notre avenir était entièrement à notre merci, nous concevrions une utopie parfaite, avec le nombre idéal d’enfants vivant dans l’opulence dans une maison parfaite, grâce à un emploi parfait, entourés de comportements parfaits, stériles et morts.

…L’espérance

Je me demande si nous mesurons à quel point nous sommes redevables à l’imprévu. L’auteur de l’épître aux Hébreux déclare que notre espérance est …une ancre de l’âme, sûre et solide… –He 6:19. Les enfants sont heureux parce qu’ils ont de grands rêves. Souvent, l’anticipation et la préparation d’un événement sont presque aussi enthousiasmantes que l’excursion elle-même. Chaque jour est une fenêtre nouvelle et lumineuse pour l’esprit plein d’espoir et préservé. Les expériences peuvent souvent nous mener au bord du cynisme et de l’amertume lorsqu’on les voit à travers les déceptions d’hier. Après ses retrouvailles merveilleuses avec son fils Joseph, Jacob fit pourtant cette remarque : ils ont été peu nombreux et mauvais, les jours de ma vie. Bien qu’il en soit naturellement ainsi, ce n’est pas une fatalité. Paul affirme …que la tribulation produit la patience, la patience l’expérience, et l’expérience l’espérance –Rm 5:3-4. Assurément, si nous savions ce que demain nous réserve, en bien comme en mal, l’élément vivifiant de l’espérance s’amenuiserait. Ève faisait semblant de croire que la vie serait meilleure si seulement elle pouvait acquérir plus de connaissance. Mais quelle bienheureuse espérance fut abandonnée dans sa quête avide de clarté !

…L’amour

L’amour possède une tendresse nostalgique que seule l’incertitude peut donner. C’est une merveille incertaine qui enveloppe le chemin d’un jeune homme auprès d’une jeune fille. Les périls inconnus de demain poussent une mère à aimer ses enfants et à prier pour eux. C’est la vision d’un lendemain meilleur pour sa famille qui pousse un père à travailler avec diligence chaque jour. Partout où un mari et sa femme sont unis dans l’unité biblique du saint mariage, le mystère qui enveloppe demain ressemble à l’accord mineur d’une grande mélodie. Il exprime joyeusement un chagrin suggéré et illumine le chagrin d’une joie qui l’entoure. Les sept années d’attente de Jacob lui auraient-elles semblé n’être que quelques jours s’il avait su ce que demain apporterait ? Si nous savions tout, aimer serait trop difficile. Si nous savions tout, aimer serait trop facile. Si nous savions tout, nous aurions le cœur brisé. Si nous savions tout, nous resterions indifférents. Autrement dit, ne pas connaître le pire nous rend plus forts, et ne pas connaître le meilleur nous rend plus tendres. Car, à travers le voile obscur de notre regard, …ces trois choses demeurent : la foi, l’espérance et l’amour ; mais la plus grande de ces choses, c’est l’amour –1 Co 13:13.

Ce n’est pas un hasard si, tandis que les disciples …le regardaient, il fut enlevé, et une nuée le déroba à leurs yeux –Ac 1:9. Aussi, n’osons pas nous étonner que, parfois, nous soyons appelés à subir la tension et le stress mental d’un lendemain obscur et inconnu. …Car qu’est-ce que votre vie ? Vous êtes une vapeur qui paraît pour un peu de temps, puis disparaît –Jc 4:14. Un jour viendra où nous …verrons le Fils de l’homme venant sur une nuée avec puissance et une grande gloire –Lc 21:27. Et il est aussi écrit : Voici, il vient avec les nuées, et tout œil le verra… Amen ! –Ap 1:7.

“My lady, I thank you very much for your affection and favor towards me, but I have given myself entirely to God to be His friend, and with that I hope to live and die,” rang the confident, faith-filled words of Jacques “zhahk” (a French form of the male name Jacob or James).

Persecution was fiercely raging in Europe in the year 1550. For their profession of faith in Jesus Christ, men, women, and even children were snatched from their homes and meeting places and thrown into the dark and cold dungeon cells of area castles. Among these captives, fifteen-year-old Jacques Dosie found himself imprisoned in Leeuwarden, Holland, for the truth of the Gospel. Even though he was only fifteen years old, he was known by his upright testimony and knowledge of the Scriptures, bringing glory to God through the power of the Spirit.

The Lord and Lady Friesland, with many nobles and ladies, were assembled in the royal halls in Leeuwarden. Their conversation turned to the “baptist heretics” that were filling the land.

“Let’s bring in that young lad, Jacques. Surely he has not been too contaminated with this heresy.”

So, he was brought in to be interrogated. Lord Friesland spoke only a few words and seemed in a hurry to finish. He had no time for this talk of religion, especially with guests waiting for a more enjoyable entertainment. Lady Friesland, however, seemed moved with compassion for this youth who was so cruelly bound in the dungeon.

“Why are you in prison? You are only a youth. What brought you here?” she asked.

Jacques answered, “I was captured and thrown into prison only because I believe in Jesus Christ. I abide by Him alone and will not forsake Him.”

The royal lady asked him, “Surely you are not one of those heretics who rebaptized themselves and have perpetrated so much evil in our country? They say they are dispersed on account of their faith and boast of being the church of God. But they are a wicked and rebellious people and cause great commotion in the land.”

“My lady, I do not know any rebellious people nor am I one of their number,” replied Jacques. “But we would much rather, according to the teachings of the Scriptures, assist our enemies. If they hunger and thirst, we bless them with food and drink. We never resist them with revenge or violence as we read in Matthew 5:39.”

“If you were in a position of power it would be seen whether you would assist your enemies,” sneered one of the nobles.

Jacques replied, “Oh, no, my lord, if it were permitted among us to resist the evil with the carnal sword, I would never do so.”

“I know there are sects among you who are very wicked and kill the people. They have their goods and wives in common,” said Lady Friesland.

“Oh, no,” replied Jacques. “We are unjustly charged with these wicked things. We are falsely accused of evil as a means to be persecuted. But as taught in Matthew 5:11, we must suffer and endure all this with patience.”

“Was it not your people who with great dishonor took up arms against the government at Amsterdam and Muenster?” asked Lady Friesland.

“No, my lady, we are not of them,” answered Jacques. “Those people erred greatly. We regard it as a doctrine of the devil to resist the authorities with the sword and violence. We would much rather suffer persecution and death from the authorities.”

“Nevertheless, you are considered to be one of them, because you too make an uproar in the land,” insisted the royal lady. “However, I believe what you say concerning those Muensterites.”

“But, my lady, don’t we read about this in Acts 24:5, how wicked men spoke evil of the apostles themselves as well as the whole band of Christians?” countered Jacques. “Did not wicked men seek to incite the authorities to vengeance against the Christians, though it was all falsehood?”

Lady Friesland didn’t answer but quickly diverted to another topic. “Do you believe that all are damned who are not baptized according to your way?” she asked.

“Oh, no, my lady,” answered Jacques. “Judgement concerning other men belongs to God alone, who shall reward everyone according to his works. This is clearly stated in many places of the Holy Scriptures. Moreover, the water does not have the power to cleanse us from sin, as 1 Peter 3:21 says, but is merely a sign of all obedience.”

“Can you still sin after you are baptized?” asked Lady Friesland.

“Yes, my lady, for this is clearly evident from the words of Paul in Romans 7:18,” replied Jacques. “We are still clothed in a weak and sinful body, and sin in many things. But we must constantly crucify and mortify the flesh, and not practice or fulfill the works of the flesh. If we fail to do this, the righteousness of God will condemn us to eternal death.”

Lady Friesland was becoming agitated. “Why don’t you listen to the church inquisitor?” she demanded.

Jacques replied, “My lady, because I will not accept his doctrine, unless he first can clearly prove to me that it agrees in all points with the Word of God. Otherwise he is laboring in vain. My faith is founded on the pure Word of God alone. As for the practice of infant baptism, I contradict his argument with reason since it is not a command of God Almighty but much rather the invention of men. Infants do not have the least bit of knowledge or discernment about what is required for baptism. But Christ in His love for such innocent ones has promised them the kingdom of God through grace, without requiring baptism.

“And further, my lady, I find that the Roman church is infected with many other errors besides this. They seek to make Christ come into the bread, or that the bread and wine should become changed into His flesh and blood. I do not believe this but regard it as an exceedingly gross error and absurdity. But I believe that Christ truly ascended to heaven and sits on the right hand of His Father as we find in Mark 16:19. There is no salvation in their flour, mass, purgatory, or any of their services for the dead. All of their human inventions, and there are many, are nowhere recognized in the Holy Scriptures. But on the contrary, we call upon God and seek our salvation in Him. Our salvation is not in any creation of man, that we may not corrupt God’s own glory and give it to any of His creatures.”

At this point the mayor, who was also present, interrupted, “So don’t you believe in the sacrament which Christ Himself instituted?”

“Sir, Paul says that the bread is broken in remembrance of Him, and that the cup of blessing is the communion of the blood of Christ,” replied Jacques.

The mayor had nothing to answer to this.

“I consider this the worst thing about you, that you will not have the children baptized,” stated Lady Friesland. “All Germany and every kingdom regard your doings as heresy.”

“It is indeed true we are despised everywhere even as the apostles were,” replied Jacques. “But we do not believe that unbaptized children shall perish at the judgment day.”

“My dear child,” said the lady pleadingly. “Come over to our side, and repent, and you shall get out of this trouble. I promise to secure your release.”

“My lady, I thank you very much for your affection and favor towards me,” answered Jacques boldly. “But I will not change my faith to please mortal man unless it be proven to me with the Scriptures. I have given myself entirely to God, to be His friend, and with that I hope to live and die.”

“My son, I have compassion for you,” she pleaded again. “Repent of your baptism and do not be so stubborn. It would be a heavy cross for my heart if you should die for this cause, being such a young child. If you repent, I will see that you are released and may go home.”

“I cannot see that there is any crime at all in my baptism. I have not followed my own cause but the Holy institution of our Lord Jesus Christ. I have not been able to find another better way to the kingdom of God except through baptism,” replied Jacques. “I am inclined to seek the Lord my God with my whole heart.”

“Look at all these men around you. Do you dare be so presumptuous to say all of them are in error?” asked Lady Friesland.

“My lady,” replied Jacques. “In Israel, four hundred prophets were against the prophet Micaiah, who alone spoke the truth. For speaking the truth, he was imprisoned on bread and water. Later in his distress, King Ahab realized prophet Micaiah spoke the truth, but it was too late. We read of this in 2 Chronicles 18.”

The lady finally said, “I find many good things in you; but your greatest error lies in your baptism. To me that does not seem to be of God.”

Lady Friesland had Jacques brought before her many times. Even though he was young in years, he was mature in the knowledge of Jesus Christ. He had built his foundation upon the Rock, Jesus Christ. With the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God, he valiantly repelled all the subtle devices of Satan, whether consisting in many severe threats, or in fair promises of the kingdom of this world. Nothing could move him to forsake Christ.

Jacques was condemned to death by the rulers of the darkness of this world. Consequently, he testified and confirmed the true faith with his death and blood and, through grace, obtained the crown of everlasting glory.

Now let us fast forward from this scene to 469 years later. Times have changed. Men, women, and children are no longer thrown into cold dungeons for their faith, at least not here in North America. But the enemy of our soul is the same. He may not go around as a roaring lion, but he surely comes around as an angel of light.

Dear youth, you may not realize it, but today you are on trial. Your faith and convictions are being challenged. Satan, in the form of the Lady Frieslands of today, is questioning you. In her audience are the worldly-wise men, the progressive Protestants, and even some contemporary folks bearing the Anabaptist name.

“Why are you looking so pious?” asks Lady Friesland. “In this day and age, you need to loosen up. How do you expect to win the world when you appear so somber?”

You are the Jacques of today, so what is your answer?

Lady Friesland continues, “You claim to be part of a separated people. Yet I see you immersing yourselves into sports, hunting, and fishing. I see you following fashions. How are you different from other Christians? Or even from the world for that matter?”

Jacques, do you have any convictions of your own? Do your choices make a difference in eternity for yourself or others? Are your lifestyle decisions a life-or-death matter to you?

Seductively, Lady Friesland leans in closer and whispers, “What does it matter? Your parents are old-fashioned. Everyone does it today. Just doing it once is harmless. Why are you such a prude?”

Jacques, is the Bible in your heart like it was with Jacques of old? Do you know and love the Word? Can you withstand temptation?

Now Lady Friesland comes from a different angle. “Why do you wear that small covering on your head? What does it mean to today’s culture? Nothing. Enlightened Christians are getting rid of it everywhere. And young Jacques, don’t you think that girl at your side who you are courting would look prettier with that covering gone? It’s just a symbol anyway.”

Jacques and Jacqueline, will you stand true to God? Do you have a ready answer?

It is time to take a serious reflection of your faith and convictions. Jacques, in his youth, was standing to become the church of tomorrow in his day. Today you are Jacques. Tomorrow the church will consist of you and all the Jacqueses and Jacquelines who are around you today. Is this a church you want to be a part of? Are you satisfied with what you see? Are you satisfied with your own lifestyle convictions and faith? Will they carry you through when the raging battles of life hit?

So, dear youth of today, will you take some time to honestly consider your personal life in the mirror of God’s Word? If God’s Spirit gives you an answer of peace and rest, praise the Lord. If in any way your heart is troubled, or convicted, don’t become discouraged. Remember it is …the goodness of God [that] leadeth thee to repentance –Rom 2:4.

«Mia signora, vi ringrazio moltissimo per il vostro affetto e la vostra benevolenza nei miei confronti, ma mi sono consacrato interamente a Dio per essere suo amico, e spero di vivere e morire così», risuonarono le parole sicure e colme di fede di Jacques «zhahk» (forma francese del nome maschile Jacob o James).

Nel 1550 la persecuzione infuriava ferocemente in Europa. Per aver professato la fede in Gesù Cristo, uomini, donne e persino bambini venivano strappati dalle loro case e dai luoghi di riunione e gettati nelle celle buie e fredde dei sotterranei dei castelli della zona. Tra quei prigionieri, il quindicenne Jacques Dosie si ritrovò incarcerato a Leeuwarden, in Olanda, per la verità del Vangelo. Benché avesse soltanto quindici anni, era noto per la sua condotta integra e la sua conoscenza delle Scritture, e glorificava Dio mediante la potenza dello Spirito.

Il signore e la signora di Friesland, insieme a molti nobili e dame, si erano riuniti nelle sale reali di Leeuwarden. La conversazione si spostò sugli «eretici battisti» che stavano riempiendo il paese.

«Facciamo venire quel giovane, Jacques. Di certo non sarà stato contaminato troppo da questa eresia.»

Così, lo condussero al loro cospetto per interrogarlo. Il signore di Friesland pronunciò solo poche parole e sembrava avere fretta di concludere. Non aveva tempo per discorsi di religione, soprattutto con degli ospiti in attesa di uno svago più piacevole. La signora di Friesland, invece, sembrava impietosita da quel giovane, legato così crudelmente nel sotterraneo.

«Perché sei in prigione? Sei solo un ragazzo. Che cosa ti ha portato qui?» gli chiese.

Jacques rispose: «Sono stato catturato e gettato in prigione soltanto perché credo in Gesù Cristo. Rimango fedele solo a lui e non lo abbandonerò.»

La nobildonna gli domandò: «Di certo non sei uno di quegli eretici che si ribattezzano e hanno commesso tanto male nel nostro paese? Dicono di essere dispersi a causa della loro fede e si vantano di essere la chiesa di Dio. Ma sono un popolo malvagio e ribelle e causano grande scompiglio nel paese.»

«Mia signora, non conosco alcun popolo ribelle, né faccio parte di loro», rispose Jacques. «Ma, secondo gli insegnamenti delle Scritture, preferiremmo aiutare i nostri nemici. Se hanno fame e sete, li benediciamo con cibo e bevande. Non ci vendichiamo mai di loro né usiamo violenza, come leggiamo in Matteo 5:39.»

«Se fossi al potere, si vedrebbe se aiuteresti i tuoi nemici», sogghignò uno dei nobili.

Jacques rispose: «Oh no, mio signore, se tra noi fosse permesso opporre al male la spada carnale, non lo farei mai.»

«So che tra voi ci sono sette molto malvagie che uccidono la gente. Hanno in comune i beni e le mogli», disse la signora di Friesland.

«Oh no», rispose Jacques. «Siamo accusati ingiustamente di queste cose malvagie. Ci si attribuisce falsamente il male come pretesto per perseguitarci. Ma, come insegna Matteo 5:11, dobbiamo patire e sopportare tutto questo con pazienza.»

«Non fu forse la vostra gente a prendere le armi, con grande disonore, contro il governo ad Amsterdam e a Münster?» chiese la signora di Friesland.

«No, mia signora, noi non facciamo parte di loro», rispose Jacques. «Quelle persone si sono molto sbagliate. Consideriamo una dottrina del diavolo opporre resistenza alle autorità con la spada e la violenza. Preferiremmo di gran lunga subire persecuzione e morte per mano delle autorità.»

«Ciononostante, ti si considera uno di loro, perché anche tu provochi disordini nel paese», insistette la nobildonna. «Tuttavia, credo a ciò che dici riguardo a quei münsteriti.»

«Ma, mia signora, non leggiamo forse in Atti 24:5 che uomini malvagi parlarono male degli apostoli stessi e di tutta la comunità dei cristiani?» ribatté Jacques. «Uomini malvagi non cercarono forse di spingere le autorità a vendicarsi dei cristiani, benché fosse tutto falso?»

La signora di Friesland non rispose, ma passò rapidamente a un altro argomento. «Credi che tutti coloro che non sono battezzati secondo il vostro modo siano dannati?» gli chiese.

«Oh no, mia signora», rispose Jacques. «Il giudizio sugli altri uomini spetta soltanto a Dio, che ricompenserà ciascuno secondo le sue opere. Ciò è affermato chiaramente in molti passi delle Sacre Scritture. Inoltre, come dice 1 Pietro 3:21, l’acqua non ha il potere di purificarci dal peccato, ma è soltanto un segno di piena obbedienza.»

«Puoi ancora peccare dopo essere stato battezzato?» chiese la signora di Friesland.

«Sì, mia signora, come risulta chiaramente dalle parole di Paolo in Romani 7:18», rispose Jacques. «Siamo ancora rivestiti di un corpo debole e peccaminoso e pecchiamo in molte cose. Ma dobbiamo continuamente crocifiggere e mortificare la carne, e non praticare né compiere le opere della carne. Se non lo facciamo, la giustizia di Dio ci condannerà alla morte eterna.»

La signora di Friesland cominciava ad agitarsi. «Perché non ascolti l’inquisitore della chiesa?» pretese.

Jacques rispose: «Mia signora, perché non accetterò la sua dottrina, a meno che prima non riesca a dimostrarmi chiaramente che concorda in ogni punto con la Parola di Dio. Altrimenti fatica invano. La mia fede è fondata soltanto sulla pura Parola di Dio. Quanto alla pratica del battesimo dei bambini, confuto la sua argomentazione con la ragione, poiché non è un comandamento di Dio onnipotente, ma piuttosto un’invenzione degli uomini. I bambini non hanno la minima conoscenza o discernimento di ciò che è richiesto per il battesimo. Ma Cristo, nel suo amore per questi innocenti, ha promesso loro per grazia il regno di Dio, senza richiedere il battesimo.

«E inoltre, mia signora, trovo che la chiesa romana sia contaminata da molti altri errori oltre a questo. Cercano di far venire Cristo nel pane, o di far trasformare il pane e il vino nel suo corpo e nel suo sangue. Non ci credo, ma lo considero un errore grossolano e un’assurdità. Credo invece che Cristo sia veramente asceso al cielo e sieda alla destra del Padre suo, come leggiamo in Marco 16:19. Nella loro farina, nella messa, nel purgatorio o in alcuno dei loro riti per i morti non c’è salvezza. Tutte le loro invenzioni umane, e ce ne sono molte, non trovano alcun riconoscimento nelle Sacre Scritture. Al contrario, invochiamo Dio e cerchiamo in lui la nostra salvezza. La nostra salvezza non si trova in alcuna creazione dell’uomo, affinché non corrompiamo la gloria di Dio stesso e non la attribuiamo ad alcuna delle sue creature.»

A quel punto il sindaco, che era presente anche lui, intervenne: «Dunque non credi al sacramento istituito da Cristo stesso?»

«Signore, Paolo dice che il pane viene spezzato in memoria di lui e che il calice della benedizione è la comunione del sangue di Cristo», rispose Jacques.

Il sindaco non ebbe nulla da rispondere.

«Ritengo che la cosa peggiore di voi sia che non volete far battezzare i bambini», dichiarò la signora di Friesland. «Tutta la Germania e ogni regno considerano eretiche le vostre usanze.»

«È proprio vero che siamo disprezzati ovunque, come lo furono gli apostoli», rispose Jacques. «Ma non crediamo che i bambini non battezzati periranno nel giorno del giudizio.»

«Figlio mio», disse la signora implorante. «Passa dalla nostra parte e pentiti, e sarai liberato da questo guaio. Ti prometto che farò in modo che tu venga rilasciato.»

«Mia signora, vi ringrazio moltissimo per il vostro affetto e la vostra benevolenza nei miei confronti», rispose Jacques con coraggio. «Ma non cambierò la mia fede per compiacere un mortale, a meno che non mi venga dimostrato con le Scritture. Mi sono consacrato interamente a Dio, per essere suo amico, e spero di vivere e morire così.»

«Figlio mio, provo compassione per te», lo supplicò di nuovo. «Rinnega il tuo battesimo e non essere così ostinato. Mi si spezzerà il cuore se morirai per questa causa, essendo ancora così giovane. Se ti penti, farò in modo che tu venga rilasciato e possa tornare a casa.»

«Non vedo proprio quale colpa ci sia nel mio battesimo. Non ho seguito una causa mia, ma la santa istituzione del nostro Signore Gesù Cristo. Non sono riuscito a trovare una via migliore verso il regno di Dio se non attraverso il battesimo», rispose Jacques. «Sono propenso a cercare il Signore mio Dio con tutto il cuore.»

«Guarda tutti questi uomini intorno a te. Osi essere così presuntuoso da dire che si sbagliano tutti?» chiese la signora di Friesland.

«Mia signora», rispose Jacques. «In Israele, quattrocento profeti si opposero al profeta Michea, che da solo diceva la verità. Per aver detto la verità, fu imprigionato e nutrito a pane e acqua. Più tardi, nella sua angoscia, il re Acab capì che il profeta Michea diceva la verità, ma era troppo tardi. Ne leggiamo in 2 Cronache 18.»

Infine la signora disse: «Trovo in te molte buone qualità, ma il tuo errore più grande sta nel tuo battesimo. Non mi sembra che venga da Dio.»

La signora di Friesland fece condurre Jacques al suo cospetto molte volte. Benché fosse giovane d’età, era maturo nella conoscenza di Gesù Cristo. Aveva costruito le sue fondamenta sulla Roccia, Gesù Cristo. Con la spada dello Spirito, che è la Parola di Dio, respinse valorosamente tutti gli astuti stratagemmi di Satana, fossero essi costituiti da gravi minacce o da allettanti promesse del regno di questo mondo. Nulla poté indurlo ad abbandonare Cristo.

Jacques fu condannato a morte dai dominatori delle tenebre di questo mondo. Così, rese testimonianza e confermò con la sua morte e il suo sangue la vera fede e, per grazia, ottenne la corona della gloria eterna.

Ora facciamo un salto in avanti da questa scena di 469 anni. I tempi sono cambiati. Uomini, donne e bambini non vengono più gettati in fredde segrete per la loro fede, almeno non qui in Nord America. Ma il nemico della nostra anima è lo stesso. Forse non gira intorno come un leone ruggente, ma di certo si presenta come un angelo di luce.

Cari giovani, forse non ve ne rendete conto, ma oggi siete sotto processo. La vostra fede e le vostre convinzioni vengono messe alla prova. Satana, nelle vesti delle signore di Friesland dei nostri giorni, vi interroga. Tra il suo pubblico ci sono uomini saggi secondo il mondo, protestanti progressisti e persino alcuni contemporanei che portano il nome di anabattisti.

«Perché avete un’aria così devota?» chiede la signora di Friesland. «Al giorno d’oggi bisogna lasciarsi andare un po’. Come pensate di conquistare il mondo se apparite così cupi?»

Oggi voi siete Jacques: qual è la vostra risposta?

La signora di Friesland continua: «Dite di far parte di un popolo separato. Eppure vi vedo immergervi nello sport, nella caccia e nella pesca. Vi vedo seguire le mode. In che cosa siete diversi dagli altri cristiani? O persino dal mondo?»

Jacques, hai convinzioni tue? Le tue scelte fanno una differenza nell’eternità, per te o per gli altri? Le decisioni sul tuo stile di vita sono per te una questione di vita o di morte?

Con fare seducente, la signora di Friesland si avvicina e sussurra: «Che importanza ha? I tuoi genitori sono all’antica. Oggi lo fanno tutti. Farlo una volta sola non fa male. Perché sei così bacchettone?»

Jacques, la Bibbia è nel tuo cuore come lo era in quello del Jacques di un tempo? Conosci e ami la Parola? Sai resistere alla tentazione?

Ora la signora di Friesland cambia argomento. «Perché porti quel piccolo copricapo? Che significato ha nella cultura di oggi? Nessuno. I cristiani illuminati se ne stanno liberando ovunque. E tu, giovane Jacques, non pensi che la ragazza che hai accanto e che corteggi sarebbe più carina senza quel copricapo? In fondo è solo un simbolo.»

Jacques e Jacqueline, rimarrete fedeli a Dio? Sapete cosa rispondere?

È tempo di riflettere seriamente sulla vostra fede e sulle vostre convinzioni. Da giovane, Jacques si stava preparando a diventare la chiesa del domani della sua epoca. Oggi siete voi Jacques. Domani la chiesa sarà composta da voi e da tutti i Jacques e le Jacqueline che oggi vi stanno intorno. È questa una chiesa di cui volete far parte? Siete soddisfatti di ciò che vedete? Siete soddisfatti delle convinzioni che guidano il vostro stile di vita e della vostra fede? Vi sosterranno quando infurieranno le battaglie della vita?

Dunque, cari giovani di oggi, vi prenderete un po’ di tempo per esaminare sinceramente la vostra vita personale alla luce della Parola di Dio? Se lo Spirito di Dio vi dà una risposta di pace e riposo, lodate il Signore. Se in qualche modo il vostro cuore è turbato o convinto, non scoraggiatevi. Ricordate: è …la bontà di Dio [che] ti conduce al ravvedimento – Romani 2:4.

“My lady, I thank you very much for your affection and favor towards me, but I have given myself entirely to God to be His friend, and with that I hope to live and die,” rang the confident, faith-filled words of Jacques “zhahk” (a French form of the male name Jacob or James).

Persecution was fiercely raging in Europe in the year 1550. For their profession of faith in Jesus Christ, men, women, and even children were snatched from their homes and meeting places and thrown into the dark and cold dungeon cells of area castles. Among these captives, fifteen-year-old Jacques Dosie found himself imprisoned in Leeuwarden, Holland, for the truth of the Gospel. Even though he was only fifteen years old, he was known by his upright testimony and knowledge of the Scriptures, bringing glory to God through the power of the Spirit.

The Lord and Lady Friesland, with many nobles and ladies, were assembled in the royal halls in Leeuwarden. Their conversation turned to the “baptist heretics” that were filling the land.

“Let’s bring in that young lad, Jacques. Surely he has not been too contaminated with this heresy.”

So, he was brought in to be interrogated. Lord Friesland spoke only a few words and seemed in a hurry to finish. He had no time for this talk of religion, especially with guests waiting for a more enjoyable entertainment. Lady Friesland, however, seemed moved with compassion for this youth who was so cruelly bound in the dungeon.

“Why are you in prison? You are only a youth. What brought you here?” she asked.

Jacques answered, “I was captured and thrown into prison only because I believe in Jesus Christ. I abide by Him alone and will not forsake Him.”

The royal lady asked him, “Surely you are not one of those heretics who rebaptized themselves and have perpetrated so much evil in our country? They say they are dispersed on account of their faith and boast of being the church of God. But they are a wicked and rebellious people and cause great commotion in the land.”

“My lady, I do not know any rebellious people nor am I one of their number,” replied Jacques. “But we would much rather, according to the teachings of the Scriptures, assist our enemies. If they hunger and thirst, we bless them with food and drink. We never resist them with revenge or violence as we read in Matthew 5:39.”

“If you were in a position of power it would be seen whether you would assist your enemies,” sneered one of the nobles.

Jacques replied, “Oh, no, my lord, if it were permitted among us to resist the evil with the carnal sword, I would never do so.”

“I know there are sects among you who are very wicked and kill the people. They have their goods and wives in common,” said Lady Friesland.

“Oh, no,” replied Jacques. “We are unjustly charged with these wicked things. We are falsely accused of evil as a means to be persecuted. But as taught in Matthew 5:11, we must suffer and endure all this with patience.”

“Was it not your people who with great dishonor took up arms against the government at Amsterdam and Muenster?” asked Lady Friesland.

“No, my lady, we are not of them,” answered Jacques. “Those people erred greatly. We regard it as a doctrine of the devil to resist the authorities with the sword and violence. We would much rather suffer persecution and death from the authorities.”

“Nevertheless, you are considered to be one of them, because you too make an uproar in the land,” insisted the royal lady. “However, I believe what you say concerning those Muensterites.”

“But, my lady, don’t we read about this in Acts 24:5, how wicked men spoke evil of the apostles themselves as well as the whole band of Christians?” countered Jacques. “Did not wicked men seek to incite the authorities to vengeance against the Christians, though it was all falsehood?”

Lady Friesland didn’t answer but quickly diverted to another topic. “Do you believe that all are damned who are not baptized according to your way?” she asked.

“Oh, no, my lady,” answered Jacques. “Judgement concerning other men belongs to God alone, who shall reward everyone according to his works. This is clearly stated in many places of the Holy Scriptures. Moreover, the water does not have the power to cleanse us from sin, as 1 Peter 3:21 says, but is merely a sign of all obedience.”

“Can you still sin after you are baptized?” asked Lady Friesland.

“Yes, my lady, for this is clearly evident from the words of Paul in Romans 7:18,” replied Jacques. “We are still clothed in a weak and sinful body, and sin in many things. But we must constantly crucify and mortify the flesh, and not practice or fulfill the works of the flesh. If we fail to do this, the righteousness of God will condemn us to eternal death.”

Lady Friesland was becoming agitated. “Why don’t you listen to the church inquisitor?” she demanded.

Jacques replied, “My lady, because I will not accept his doctrine, unless he first can clearly prove to me that it agrees in all points with the Word of God. Otherwise he is laboring in vain. My faith is founded on the pure Word of God alone. As for the practice of infant baptism, I contradict his argument with reason since it is not a command of God Almighty but much rather the invention of men. Infants do not have the least bit of knowledge or discernment about what is required for baptism. But Christ in His love for such innocent ones has promised them the kingdom of God through grace, without requiring baptism.

“And further, my lady, I find that the Roman church is infected with many other errors besides this. They seek to make Christ come into the bread, or that the bread and wine should become changed into His flesh and blood. I do not believe this but regard it as an exceedingly gross error and absurdity. But I believe that Christ truly ascended to heaven and sits on the right hand of His Father as we find in Mark 16:19. There is no salvation in their flour, mass, purgatory, or any of their services for the dead. All of their human inventions, and there are many, are nowhere recognized in the Holy Scriptures. But on the contrary, we call upon God and seek our salvation in Him. Our salvation is not in any creation of man, that we may not corrupt God’s own glory and give it to any of His creatures.”

At this point the mayor, who was also present, interrupted, “So don’t you believe in the sacrament which Christ Himself instituted?”

“Sir, Paul says that the bread is broken in remembrance of Him, and that the cup of blessing is the communion of the blood of Christ,” replied Jacques.

The mayor had nothing to answer to this.

“I consider this the worst thing about you, that you will not have the children baptized,” stated Lady Friesland. “All Germany and every kingdom regard your doings as heresy.”

“It is indeed true we are despised everywhere even as the apostles were,” replied Jacques. “But we do not believe that unbaptized children shall perish at the judgment day.”

“My dear child,” said the lady pleadingly. “Come over to our side, and repent, and you shall get out of this trouble. I promise to secure your release.”

“My lady, I thank you very much for your affection and favor towards me,” answered Jacques boldly. “But I will not change my faith to please mortal man unless it be proven to me with the Scriptures. I have given myself entirely to God, to be His friend, and with that I hope to live and die.”

“My son, I have compassion for you,” she pleaded again. “Repent of your baptism and do not be so stubborn. It would be a heavy cross for my heart if you should die for this cause, being such a young child. If you repent, I will see that you are released and may go home.”

“I cannot see that there is any crime at all in my baptism. I have not followed my own cause but the Holy institution of our Lord Jesus Christ. I have not been able to find another better way to the kingdom of God except through baptism,” replied Jacques. “I am inclined to seek the Lord my God with my whole heart.”

“Look at all these men around you. Do you dare be so presumptuous to say all of them are in error?” asked Lady Friesland.

“My lady,” replied Jacques. “In Israel, four hundred prophets were against the prophet Micaiah, who alone spoke the truth. For speaking the truth, he was imprisoned on bread and water. Later in his distress, King Ahab realized prophet Micaiah spoke the truth, but it was too late. We read of this in 2 Chronicles 18.”

The lady finally said, “I find many good things in you; but your greatest error lies in your baptism. To me that does not seem to be of God.”

Lady Friesland had Jacques brought before her many times. Even though he was young in years, he was mature in the knowledge of Jesus Christ. He had built his foundation upon the Rock, Jesus Christ. With the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God, he valiantly repelled all the subtle devices of Satan, whether consisting in many severe threats, or in fair promises of the kingdom of this world. Nothing could move him to forsake Christ.

Jacques was condemned to death by the rulers of the darkness of this world. Consequently, he testified and confirmed the true faith with his death and blood and, through grace, obtained the crown of everlasting glory.

Now let us fast forward from this scene to 469 years later. Times have changed. Men, women, and children are no longer thrown into cold dungeons for their faith, at least not here in North America. But the enemy of our soul is the same. He may not go around as a roaring lion, but he surely comes around as an angel of light.

Dear youth, you may not realize it, but today you are on trial. Your faith and convictions are being challenged. Satan, in the form of the Lady Frieslands of today, is questioning you. In her audience are the worldly-wise men, the progressive Protestants, and even some contemporary folks bearing the Anabaptist name.

“Why are you looking so pious?” asks Lady Friesland. “In this day and age, you need to loosen up. How do you expect to win the world when you appear so somber?”

You are the Jacques of today, so what is your answer?

Lady Friesland continues, “You claim to be part of a separated people. Yet I see you immersing yourselves into sports, hunting, and fishing. I see you following fashions. How are you different from other Christians? Or even from the world for that matter?”

Jacques, do you have any convictions of your own? Do your choices make a difference in eternity for yourself or others? Are your lifestyle decisions a life-or-death matter to you?

Seductively, Lady Friesland leans in closer and whispers, “What does it matter? Your parents are old-fashioned. Everyone does it today. Just doing it once is harmless. Why are you such a prude?”

Jacques, is the Bible in your heart like it was with Jacques of old? Do you know and love the Word? Can you withstand temptation?

Now Lady Friesland comes from a different angle. “Why do you wear that small covering on your head? What does it mean to today’s culture? Nothing. Enlightened Christians are getting rid of it everywhere. And young Jacques, don’t you think that girl at your side who you are courting would look prettier with that covering gone? It’s just a symbol anyway.”

Jacques and Jacqueline, will you stand true to God? Do you have a ready answer?

It is time to take a serious reflection of your faith and convictions. Jacques, in his youth, was standing to become the church of tomorrow in his day. Today you are Jacques. Tomorrow the church will consist of you and all the Jacqueses and Jacquelines who are around you today. Is this a church you want to be a part of? Are you satisfied with what you see? Are you satisfied with your own lifestyle convictions and faith? Will they carry you through when the raging battles of life hit?

So, dear youth of today, will you take some time to honestly consider your personal life in the mirror of God’s Word? If God’s Spirit gives you an answer of peace and rest, praise the Lord. If in any way your heart is troubled, or convicted, don’t become discouraged. Remember it is …the goodness of God [that] leadeth thee to repentance –Rom 2:4.

“부인, 저를 아껴 주시고 호의를 베풀어 주셔서 대단히 감사합니다. 그러나 저는 하나님의 친구가 되기 위해 제 자신을 온전히 하나님께 드렸으며, 그 믿음으로 살다가 죽기를 바랍니다.” 자크 ‘자크’(프랑스어로 남자 이름 야곱 또는 제임스를 이르는 형태)는 확신과 믿음으로 가득 찬 목소리로 말했다.

1550년, 유럽에서는 박해가 맹렬히 일어나고 있었다. 예수 그리스도를 믿는 신앙을 고백했다는 이유로 남녀는 물론 아이들까지도 집과 모임 장소에서 끌려 나와 인근 성의 어둡고 차가운 지하 감옥에 갇혔다. 이 포로들 가운데 열다섯 살 자크 도시는 복음의 진리 때문에 네덜란드 레이우아르던에 갇혀 있었다. 겨우 열다섯 살이었지만, 그는 바른 증거와 성경 지식으로 알려져 있었으며 성령의 능력으로 하나님께 영광을 돌렸다.

프리슬란트 영주와 부인을 비롯해 많은 귀족과 귀부인들이 레이우아르던의 왕궁에 모여 있었다. 대화는 온 땅에 퍼져 있는 “재세례파 이단자들”에 관한 이야기로 이어졌다.

“그 어린 소년 자크를 데려오시오. 이 이단에 너무 물들지는 않았겠지.”

그리하여 그는 심문을 받기 위해 불려 나왔다. 프리슬란트 영주는 몇 마디만 하고는 서둘러 끝내려는 듯했다. 종교 이야기에 시간을 쓸 생각이 없었고, 특히 손님들이 더 즐거운 오락을 기다리고 있었다. 그러나 프리슬란트 부인은 지하 감옥에서 그토록 잔인하게 결박당한 이 젊은이를 불쌍히 여기는 듯했다.

“너는 왜 감옥에 있느냐? 아직 어린데, 어쩌다 여기까지 오게 되었느냐?” 그녀가 물었다.

자크가 대답했다. “저는 예수 그리스도를 믿는다는 이유만으로 붙잡혀 감옥에 던져졌습니다. 저는 오직 그분만을 따르며 그분을 버리지 않을 것입니다.”

왕실의 부인이 물었다. “너는 자신을 다시 세례 주고 우리나라에서 그토록 많은 악을 저질렀다는 그 이단자들 중 하나는 아니겠지? 그들은 신앙 때문에 흩어졌다고 말하고 하나님의 교회라고 자랑한다더구나. 그러나 그들은 사악하고 반역적인 무리이며 이 땅에 큰 소동을 일으킨다.”

“부인, 저는 반역하는 사람들을 알지 못하며 그들 중 한 사람도 아닙니다.” 자크가 대답했다. “그러나 우리는 성경의 가르침에 따라 차라리 원수들을 돕고자 합니다. 그들이 굶주리고 목말라하면 먹을 것과 마실 것을 주며 축복합니다. 마태복음 5장 39절에서 읽듯이, 우리는 복수나 폭력으로 그들에게 맞서지 않습니다.”

“네가 권력을 가진 위치에 있다면 과연 원수들을 돕는지 알 수 있겠지.” 한 귀족이 비웃으며 말했다.

자크가 대답했다. “아닙니다, 영주님. 우리 가운데 육신의 칼로 악에 맞서는 것이 허용된다 해도 저는 결코 그렇게 하지 않을 것입니다.”

“너희 가운데는 매우 사악하고 사람들을 죽이는 분파가 있다고 알고 있다. 그들은 재산과 아내를 공동으로 소유한다더구나.” 프리슬란트 부인이 말했다.

“아닙니다.” 자크가 대답했다. “우리는 이런 사악한 일들로 부당하게 비난받고 있습니다. 박해할 구실로 우리를 악하다고 거짓 고발하는 것입니다. 그러나 마태복음 5장 11절의 가르침처럼, 우리는 이 모든 일을 인내하며 견뎌야 합니다.”

“암스테르담과 뮌스터에서 정부를 거슬러 무기를 들고 큰 불명예를 저지른 것은 너희 사람들이 아니냐?” 프리슬란트 부인이 물었다.

“아닙니다, 부인. 우리는 그들과 다릅니다.” 자크가 대답했다. “그 사람들은 크게 잘못했습니다. 우리는 칼과 폭력으로 권세자들에게 대항하는 것을 마귀의 교리라고 여깁니다. 차라리 권세자들에게 박해와 죽임을 당하겠습니다.”

“그렇더라도 너희도 이 땅에 소동을 일으키니 그들과 같은 부류로 여겨진다.” 왕실의 부인이 단호히 말했다. “하지만 네가 뮌스터파 사람들에 관해 한 말은 믿는다.”

“그러나 부인, 사도행전 24장 5절에서 악한 사람들이 사도들과 그리스도인 무리 전체를 어떻게 악하다고 말했는지 읽지 않습니까?” 자크가 반문했다. “그 모든 것이 거짓이었는데도 악한 사람들이 그리스도인들을 향해 권세자들이 복수하도록 부추기려 하지 않았습니까?”

프리슬란트 부인은 대답하지 않고 재빨리 화제를 돌렸다. “너희 방식대로 세례를 받지 않은 사람은 모두 멸망한다고 믿느냐?” 그녀가 물었다.

“아닙니다, 부인.” 자크가 대답했다. “다른 사람에 대한 심판은 오직 하나님께 속하며, 하나님께서는 각 사람이 행한 대로 갚으실 것입니다. 이는 성경 여러 곳에 분명히 나와 있습니다. 또한 베드로전서 3장 21절이 말하듯 물은 우리를 죄에서 깨끗하게 하는 능력이 없으며, 오직 모든 순종의 표일 뿐입니다.”

“세례를 받은 뒤에도 죄를 지을 수 있느냐?” 프리슬란트 부인이 물었다.

“그렇습니다, 부인. 로마서 7장 18절에 나오는 바울의 말에서 분명히 알 수 있습니다.” 자크가 대답했다. “우리는 여전히 약하고 죄 많은 몸을 입고 있으며 많은 일에서 죄를 짓습니다. 그러나 우리는 끊임없이 육체를 십자가에 못 박고 죽이며, 육체의 일을 행하거나 이루지 말아야 합니다. 그렇게 하지 않으면 하나님의 의가 우리를 영원한 죽음에 처할 것입니다.”

프리슬란트 부인은 점점 언짢아졌다. “왜 교회 심문관의 말을 듣지 않느냐?” 그녀가 다그쳤다.

자크가 대답했다. “부인, 그가 자신의 교리가 하나님의 말씀과 모든 면에서 일치한다는 것을 먼저 분명히 입증하지 않는 한 저는 그 교리를 받아들이지 않을 것이기 때문입니다. 그렇지 않다면 그는 헛수고를 하는 것입니다. 제 믿음은 오직 하나님의 순수한 말씀에 기초하고 있습니다. 유아 세례의 관행에 관해서라면, 그것은 전능하신 하나님의 명령이 아니라 오히려 사람들의 발명이므로 저는 이성에 근거해 그의 주장을 반박합니다. 유아들은 세례에 필요한 것이 무엇인지 조금도 알거나 분별하지 못합니다. 그러나 그리스도께서는 그런 순진한 이들을 사랑하셔서 세례를 요구하지 않으시고 은혜로 하나님의 나라를 약속하셨습니다.

“그리고 더 말씀드리자면, 부인, 저는 로마 교회가 이 문제 외에도 많은 오류에 물들어 있음을 알게 되었습니다. 그들은 그리스도를 빵 안에 들어오게 하거나 빵과 포도주가 그분의 살과 피로 변해야 한다고 주장합니다. 저는 이것을 믿지 않으며, 지극히 큰 오류이자 터무니없는 일이라고 여깁니다. 그러나 마가복음 16장 19절에서 보듯, 그리스도께서는 참으로 하늘로 올라가셔서 아버지의 오른편에 앉아 계심을 믿습니다. 그들의 밀가루, 미사, 연옥, 또는 죽은 이를 위한 어떤 예식에도 구원은 없습니다. 그들의 인간적인 발명은 모두, 그리고 그런 것은 많지만, 성경 어디에서도 인정되지 않습니다. 오히려 우리는 하나님을 부르고 그분 안에서 구원을 구합니다. 하나님의 영광을 더럽히고 그분의 피조물 가운데 어느 하나에게 돌리지 않도록, 우리의 구원은 어떤 인간의 창조물에도 있지 않습니다.”

이때 그 자리에 함께 있던 시장이 끼어들었다. “그렇다면 그리스도께서 친히 제정하신 성례를 믿지 않는다는 말이오?”

“선생님, 바울은 빵을 그분을 기억하며 떼고, 축복의 잔은 그리스도의 피에 참여하는 것이라고 말합니다.” 자크가 대답했다.

시장은 이에 아무 대답도 하지 못했다.

“너희에 대해 가장 못마땅한 점은 아이들에게 세례를 주지 않으려는 것이다.” 프리슬란트 부인이 말했다. “독일 전체와 모든 왕국이 너희 행위를 이단으로 여긴다.”

“사도들이 그랬듯 우리도 어디에서나 멸시받는다는 것은 참으로 사실입니다.” 자크가 대답했다. “그러나 세례받지 않은 아이들이 심판 날에 멸망한다고 믿지는 않습니다.”

“사랑하는 아이야.” 부인이 간청하듯 말했다. “우리 편으로 와서 회개하면 이 곤경에서 벗어날 수 있다. 네 석방을 보장해 주마.”

“부인, 저를 아껴 주시고 호의를 베풀어 주셔서 대단히 감사합니다.” 자크가 담대히 대답했다. “그러나 성경으로 입증되지 않는 한, 죽을 사람을 기쁘게 하려고 제 믿음을 바꾸지 않겠습니다. 저는 하나님의 친구가 되기 위해 제 자신을 온전히 하나님께 드렸으며, 그 믿음으로 살다가 죽기를 바랍니다.”

“내 아들아, 너를 불쌍히 여긴다.” 그녀가 다시 간청했다. “네 세례를 회개하고 그렇게 고집을 부리지 말아라. 네가 아직 어린아이인데 이 일로 죽는다면 내 마음에 큰 십자가가 될 것이다. 네가 회개하면 석방되어 집으로 돌아가도록 해 주마.”

“제 세례에 어떤 죄가 있는지 전혀 모르겠습니다. 저는 제 뜻을 따른 것이 아니라 우리 주 예수 그리스도께서 거룩하게 제정하신 것을 따랐습니다. 세례를 통하는 것보다 하나님의 나라로 가는 더 나은 길을 찾지 못했습니다.” 자크가 대답했다. “저는 온 마음으로 주 나의 하나님을 찾고자 합니다.”

“네 주위에 있는 사람들을 모두 보아라. 그들 모두가 잘못했다고 감히 주제넘게 말하겠느냐?” 프리슬란트 부인이 물었다.

“부인.” 자크가 대답했다. “이스라엘에서는 사백 명의 예언자가 예언자 미가야를 대적했지만, 진리를 말한 사람은 미가야 한 명뿐이었습니다. 진리를 말한 죄로 그는 빵과 물만 먹으며 감옥에 갇혔습니다. 훗날 아합 왕은 곤경에 처하고 나서야 미가야 예언자가 진실을 말했다는 것을 깨달았지만, 이미 때는 늦었습니다. 역대하 18장에서 이 일을 읽을 수 있습니다.”

마침내 부인이 말했다. “네게 좋은 점이 많다고 생각한다. 그러나 가장 큰 오류는 네 세례에 있다. 그것은 하나님에게서 온 것 같지 않구나.”

프리슬란트 부인은 자크를 여러 차례 자기 앞에 불러오게 했다. 나이는 어렸지만 그는 예수 그리스도를 아는 지식에 성숙했다. 그는 반석이신 예수 그리스도 위에 기초를 세웠다. 하나님의 말씀인 성령의 검으로, 그는 세상의 왕국을 주겠다는 달콤한 약속이든 가혹한 위협이든 사탄의 온갖 교묘한 술책을 용감히 물리쳤다. 그 무엇도 그를 그리스도를 버리도록 흔들 수 없었다.

자크는 이 세상 어둠의 권세자들에게 사형 선고를 받았다. 그리하여 그는 죽음과 피로 참된 믿음을 증언하고 확증했으며, 은혜로 영원한 영광의 면류관을 얻었다.

이제 이 장면에서 469년 뒤로 훌쩍 건너가 보자. 시대는 변했다. 적어도 북아메리카에서는 더 이상 남녀와 아이들이 신앙 때문에 차가운 지하 감옥에 던져지지 않는다. 그러나 우리 영혼의 원수는 여전하다. 그는 으르렁거리는 사자처럼 돌아다니지 않을 수도 있지만, 분명 빛의 천사처럼 다가온다.

사랑하는 젊은이 여러분, 깨닫지 못할 수도 있지만 오늘 여러분은 심문대에 서 있습니다. 여러분의 믿음과 신념이 도전을 받고 있습니다. 오늘날의 프리슬란트 부인들의 모습으로 나타난 사탄이 여러분에게 질문하고 있습니다. 그녀의 청중 가운데는 세상 물정에 밝은 사람들, 진보적인 개신교인들, 심지어 재세례파라는 이름을 지닌 현대인들도 있습니다.

“왜 그렇게 경건한 체하느냐?” 프리슬란트 부인이 묻습니다. “이 시대에는 좀 느긋해질 필요가 있다. 그렇게 무거운 표정을 지으면서 어떻게 세상을 얻겠느냐?”

여러분은 오늘날의 자크입니다. 그렇다면 뭐라고 대답하겠습니까?

프리슬란트 부인이 계속 말합니다. “너희는 세상과 구별된 백성이라고 주장한다. 그런데 나는 너희가 스포츠와 사냥과 낚시에 빠져드는 것을 본다. 유행을 좇는 것도 본다. 너희가 다른 그리스도인들과 어떻게 다르냐? 아니, 세상과는 또 어떻게 다르냐?”

자크, 여러분만의 신념이 있습니까? 여러분의 선택은 여러분 자신이나 다른 사람의 영원에 영향을 줍니까? 여러분의 생활 방식에 관한 결정은 여러분에게 사느냐 죽느냐의 문제입니까?

프리슬란트 부인이 유혹하듯 몸을 더 가까이 기울이며 속삭입니다. “그게 무슨 상관이냐? 네 부모님은 시대에 뒤떨어졌다. 요즘은 다들 그렇게 한다. 한 번쯤 하는 건 해가 없다. 왜 그렇게 답답하게 구느냐?”

자크, 옛날의 자크에게 그랬듯 성경이 여러분의 마음속에 있습니까? 말씀을 알고 사랑합니까? 유혹을 견딜 수 있습니까?

이번에는 프리슬란트 부인이 다른 방향에서 다가옵니다. “왜 머리에 그 작은 가리개를 쓰느냐? 오늘날 문화에서 그게 무슨 뜻이 있느냐? 아무 뜻도 없다. 깨우친 그리스도인들은 어디서나 그것을 없애고 있다. 어린 자크야, 네 곁에서 구애를 받고 있는 그 아가씨도 그 가리개를 벗으면 더 예뻐 보이지 않겠느냐? 어차피 상징일 뿐이다.”

자크와 자클린, 하나님께 끝까지 충실하겠습니까? 즉시 대답할 준비가 되어 있습니까?

이제 믿음과 신념을 진지하게 돌아볼 때입니다. 젊은 자크는 그 시대의 내일을 이끌 교회가 될 준비를 하고 있었습니다. 오늘날 여러분이 자크입니다. 내일 교회는 여러분과 오늘 여러분 곁에 있는 모든 자크와 자클린으로 이루어질 것입니다. 여러분은 이런 교회의 일원이 되고 싶습니까? 여러분이 보는 모습에 만족합니까? 자신의 생활 방식에 관한 신념과 믿음에 만족합니까? 삶의 격렬한 싸움이 닥칠 때 그것들이 여러분을 지탱해 주겠습니까?

그러니 오늘날의 사랑하는 젊은이 여러분, 하나님의 말씀이라는 거울에 비추어 자신의 삶을 솔직히 돌아볼 시간을 내겠습니까? 하나님의 영이 평안과 안식의 대답을 주신다면 주님을 찬양하십시오. 마음이 조금이라도 괴롭거나 죄를 깨닫게 된다면 낙심하지 마십시오. …하나님의 인자하심이 너를 회개로 이끄심을 기억하십시오. –로마서 2:4.
