Behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud –Exo 16:10.

What a strange phenomenon is this concentrated mass of vapor that navigates the sky above us. In one instance, a cloud can minister such immense blessedness and hope, while in another it can be the instigator of nagging uncertainty and even the arousal of ragged fear. Clouds were often, no doubt, the welcome shade to the heads of weary fishermen upon Galilee and the propagator of hope to the toiling farmer. How often these clouds part at midday to allow the sun’s beaming rays access to the earth. Then in the evening, they provide the opaque structure for the exquisite beauty of a silver lineation.

We may marvel to see an airplane weighing over 700,000 pounds mount up with wings and soar through the heavens, yet a cloud can carry millions of tons of water without any of the dynamics of human intervention. Clouds are formed when moist, warm air rises to a cooler elevation and water condenses onto microscopic “seeds” such as dust, ash, or bacteria. If there’s more water vapor than places on which it can condense, then ice crystals can also serve as seeds and take on moisture—He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them –Job 26:8. Eventually, these seeds become too heavy for updrafts to support, and then, behold, it is time for the umbrella.

To the parched land in Elijah’s day, the smallest of clouds (like a man’s hand in 1 Kings 18:44) was the answer from the Almighty that He was again prepared to bless His people with rain. Yet, to others like Job and Jeremiah, the cloud represented the ultimate emblem of doubt, despair, and discouragement. Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud –Job 30:15, and Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through –Lam 3:44. It is often in such stressful conditions that God chooses to hide Himself in a cloud. At these times, we grope through the thick foreboding fog in search of the pathway of light, but we find it not. In our discouragement, we may long for the beam of a cloudless day, but it eludes us. We know that God is in the midst of the mist, but we cannot apprehend Him, nor see His blessedness. With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt –Job 36:32.

Why would our God, who loves to commune with us, the vessels of His own creation, choose to hide Himself in a cloud? Why does He often hide His will from our searching and aching hearts? Our finite minds often wonder what glory could possibly arise from such a seemingly distant God, and …to what purpose is this waste –Mat 26:8. While we would never expect it to be God’s divine plan to leave us in a foggy stupor forever, it may be His will for a time. Like a stroll through the valley of the shadow of death, there can be eternal character wrought in the soul who has experienced a seasonal lack of clarity in their path. We are well aware that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Pro 4:18. Still, most of us have, at times, experienced the hopeless fog that surrounds our present and our future. In these times, we meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night –Job 5:14. In our bedraggled discouragement, we can easily lose sight of the goodness of God. Our resulting lack of thankfulness is a sure road to a host of other temptations, while the giant of despair rises overhead in an attempt to weaken our resistance to sin.

We know that Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are –Jam 5:17. Yet, few of us have ever experienced a victory as exhilarating as he did when he triumphed over the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Still, many of us can well relate to the discouragement that followed as he came unto Horeb and lodged in a cave there. This is the same place as Mount Sinai where the first great mountain scene opened before us in the Scriptures. Then it was Moses who met God in the cloud. The law was given, and God’s glory was so marvelously manifested and so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake –Heb 12:21. This mount that might be touched was a formidable and intimidating mountain flanked by splintering dark granite peaks and stern ridges of indescribable grandeur. The bold and awful front of Horeb, rises in frowning majesty from twelve hundred to fifteen hundred feet in perpendicular height.

With Elijah’s vision clouded over and his spirit ebbing away at an all-time low, God responded to him in astounding methodology—…And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out… –1 Kin 19:11-13.

Somehow, we have come to believe that an earthshaking experience is the epitome of God’s manifest presence. We reckon that God was closer to Elijah on Mt. Carmel than He was on Mt. Horeb. It was Elijah’s “day in the sun” while speaking on Mt. Carmel. He chided the people and mocked the prophets. He preached boldly in the name of the Lord and commanded the people to repent of their duplicity. But now his voice has been silenced and he is listening … listening to the still small voice calling into account his own actions and ambitions. Thus, if we will but stop and listen, the memory of our dismal failures will escort us to the front porch of our Lord, rather than allow us to glory in our perceived successes.

This is the blessed ministration of the cloud. It is often the vehicle that the Lord will use to bring us to the place where we can truly receive His manifest glory in our hearts. This is not the white, fluffy, cumulus clouds of a balmy summer day but, rather, the flat and featureless stratus clouds that blanket the heavens from east to west and totally eclipse all the rays of heavenly sunshine. They can enshroud the day at high noon with an arsenal of gloom that rankles our hearts to the core. The little things, that on other days had little effect on our attitudes, now seem to tower as giants before us. We may face advents that we know are beyond our control, but our minds refuse to enter into rest. In times like these, if there happens to be an unfortunate soul on the other end of our conversation experiencing a similar plight, we may experience firsthand that …man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward –Job 5:7. At other times, our melancholy mood may be content to withdraw and feed itself with our own reclusive pity and foggy misery.

Some, in their desperation, turn to medication for the mind and there find a limited valve of relief. But God has not brought us into the cloud so that we may seek the help of physicians and psychologists. The ministration of the cloud is to shut off all other alternatives so that we may receive of Him the full blessedness of His consolation. God is willing that we should sacrifice the shimmering sunshine of today for the fullness of His presence tomorrow.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. In bygone years, I have preached on this verse, exhorting souls concerning the brevity of life and encouraging them to not squander their years away. But I had totally ignored the foundation of it—ye know not what shall be on the morrow. This, perhaps, seems trite to the young at heart, but as the fruit of my age continues to ripen, I have a growing appreciation for the common and obvious idioms. Our modern scientific world is so adamantly pursuing the love of life that it cannot appreciate the life of love that is begotten through suffering. While those who, in ages past, suffered in the flesh and ceased from sin (1 Pet 4:1), I see no reason why those who experience the frail sufferings of a clouded mind may not share the same glory if they will but endure and trust to God the results.

We are an arrogant people who lean on the predictions of tomorrow. We fancy that we can plan our retirement and schedule our life events with immaculate detail. The weather forecasters tell us of tomorrows temperature so that we can meticulously plan our day. Our insurance gives assurance that we will not be subject to future poverty. Our freezers and bank accounts are full enough to see us well past tomorrow, and we have grown accustomed to believing that we …sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow –Rev 18:7. Yet the sorrow of heart cannot be so easily absolved by earthly amenities. Our life is a vapour (cloud) because we …know not what shall be on the morrow… –Jas 4:14. In spite of all our technology we still cannot absolve that fact. It is here that we must lay aside all our intuitions, expectations, and ambitions of what our life ought to be and find our God in the cloud.

He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it –Job 26:9. To what benefit is the cloud covering the face of God’s throne? If it were easily beholden, most of us would be content to dwell with Him from afar. However, due to the impending fog, we must draw nigh to experience His fullness. How thankful we ought to be that it is thus, for how devastating would be our spiritual loss if it were not so.

If our self-sufficient life was always vibrantly full and God were easily apprehended, we would lose…

…Faith

We seek a guarantee that our trials will end happily ever after and that our prayers will naturally become unnecessary. In faith, we believe in God’s provision, but the fact that we know not what a day will bring demands that we fall upon our feeble knees and pray. There may be many things that make it hard for us to trust in God, but the shrouded tomorrow makes it easier. Researchers have spent millions in their efforts to control the weather. They have sown every imaginable cloud seed into the air in efforts to produce rain clouds. After reviewing 40 years of cloud-seeding efforts in an area north of Israel, researchers at Tel Aviv University have concluded that cloud seeding doesn’t actually produce any additional precipitation. How thankful we should be. The more we can control the unknown morrow, the less faith in the Master of the Universe we need.

Jacob, in leaving behind an angry brother, a disappointed father, and a severed tie with his mother, faced an altogether unknown future. This is a part of the ladder to the throne and it fortifies our commitment to our omnipotent God. Now we know in part and we see in part. Perhaps that fractional sliver brings us more inner wealth than if the whole were fully understood. If our future were amply within our manipulative power, we would formulate a perfect utopia supplied with the perfect number of children living sumptuously in the perfect home supported by the perfect job surrounded by perfect behavior that is perfectly sterile and dead.

…Hope

I question if we realize how deeply our debt is to the unexpected. The Hebrew writer declares our hope to be …an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast… –Heb 6:19. Children are happy because they have big dreams. Often the anticipation and planning of an event is almost as thrilling as the excursion itself. Every day is a bright new window to the unspoiled, hopeful mind. Experiences can often bring us to the brink of cynicism and bitterness when viewed through yesterday’s disappointments. Jacob, upon the marvelous reunification with his son, Joseph, still remarked, few and evil have been my days. Though it is naturally so, it needs not to be. Paul states …that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope –Rom 5:3-4. Surely, if we knew what was in store tomorrow (both good and evil) the invigorating element of hope would dwindle. Eve feigned that life would be better if she could only secure more knowledge. But what blessed hope was forfeited in her lustful pursuit of clarity.

…Love

There is a wistful tenderness in love that nothing but uncertainty can give. It is uncertain wonder that encompasses the way of a young man with a maid. The unknown perils of tomorrow drive a mother to love and prayer for her children. It is the vision of a brighter tomorrow for his family that moves a father to diligence in his daily work. Wherever a husband and his wife are knit together in Biblical oneness of holy matrimony, the mystery that envelops tomorrow is like the minor chord in a great melody. It speaks in joy of a suggested sorrow and brightens sorrow with encircling joy. Would Jacob’s seven-year wait have seemed like a few days if he had known what the morrow would bring? If we knew everything, love would be too hard. If we knew everything, love would be too easy. If we knew everything, we would be brokenhearted. If we knew everything, we would be unconcerned. In other words, it makes us stronger to not know the worst and it makes us more tender to not know the best. For in our clouded and darkened lens there …abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Cor 13:13.

It is no coincidence that while the disciples …beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight –Act 1:9. And so we dare not be surprised that, at times, we shall be called to suffer the mental strain and stress of an obscure and unknown tomorrow. …For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. There is coming a day when we shall …see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory –Luk 21:27. And again it is written, Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him … Even so, Amen –Rev 1:7.

구름 가운데서 여호와의 영광이 나타났더라 –출 16:10.

우리 머리 위 하늘을 떠다니는 이 응축된 수증기 덩어리는 참으로 기이한 현상입니다. 어떤 때 구름은 엄청난 복과 희망을 베풀기도 하지만, 또 어떤 때는 끈질긴 불확실성과 심지어 거친 두려움을 불러일으키는 원인이 되기도 합니다. 의심할 여지 없이 구름은 갈릴리에서 지친 어부들의 머리 위에 반가운 그늘을 드리우고, 수고하는 농부에게 희망을 안겨 주곤 했습니다. 구름이 한낮에 얼마나 자주 갈라져 햇살이 지상에 내리쬐도록 하는지요. 저녁에는 은빛 선의 아름다움을 빚어내는 불투명한 바탕이 되어 줍니다.

무게가 70만 파운드가 넘는 비행기가 날개를 달고 하늘로 솟아올라 날아가는 모습을 보면 감탄할 수 있습니다. 그러나 구름은 인간의 힘을 전혀 빌리지 않고도 수백만 톤의 물을 실어 나릅니다. 따뜻하고 습한 공기가 더 서늘한 고도로 올라가면 물이 응결하여 먼지, 재, 박테리아 같은 미세한 ‘씨앗’에 달라붙으면서 구름이 형성됩니다. 응결할 곳보다 수증기가 더 많으면 얼음 결정도 씨앗 역할을 하여 수분을 머금습니다—그가 물을 빽빽한 구름에 싸매시나니, 그 구름은 그 아래서 찢어지지 아니하느니라 –욥 26:8. 마침내 이 씨앗들이 상승 기류가 떠받치기에는 너무 무거워지고, 그러면 보라, 우산을 펼칠 때가 됩니다.

엘리야 시대의 메마른 땅에 작은 구름 하나(왕상 18:44에서 사람의 손만 한 구름)는 하나님께서 자기 백성에게 다시 비를 내려 복 주실 준비가 되셨다는 전능자의 응답이었습니다. 그러나 욥과 예레미야 같은 이들에게 구름은 의심과 절망과 낙담의 궁극적인 상징이었습니다. 두려움이 내게 임하고 그것들이 바람처럼 내 영혼을 뒤쫓으며 내 행복은 구름처럼 사라지는도다 –욥 30:15, 그리고 주께서 구름으로 자신을 가리시므로 우리의 기도가 주께 이르지 못하나이다 –애 3:44. 하나님께서 구름 속에 자신을 숨기기로 하시는 때는 흔히 이처럼 괴로운 상황일 때입니다. 그럴 때 우리는 빛의 길을 찾아 짙고 불길한 안개 속을 더듬지만, 그 길을 찾지 못합니다. 낙담한 우리는 구름 한 점 없는 날의 햇살을 간절히 바라지만, 햇살은 우리 손에 닿지 않습니다. 하나님께서 안개 속에 계심을 알지만, 그분을 깨닫지도 그분의 복을 보지도 못합니다. 그가 구름으로 빛을 가리시고 그 사이를 지나가는 구름에 명하여 빛을 비추지 못하게 하시느니라 –욥 36:32.

자신이 창조하신 그릇인 우리와 교제하기를 기뻐하시는 하나님께서는 왜 구름 속에 자신을 숨기기로 하실까요? 왜 그분은 우리의 간절하고 아픈 마음이 찾는 그분의 뜻을 자주 감추실까요? 우리의 유한한 생각은 그렇게 멀리 계신 듯한 하나님에게서 도대체 어떤 영광이 나올 수 있을지 종종 의아해하며, …무슨 목적으로 이런 낭비를 하느냐 –마 26:8. 하나님께서 우리를 영원히 안개 속에 어리둥절하게 내버려 두시는 것이 그분의 신성한 계획일 리는 없지만, 한동안은 그것이 그분의 뜻일 수도 있습니다. 사망의 음침한 골짜기를 거니는 것처럼, 길이 한동안 분명하지 않은 때를 겪은 영혼 안에는 영원한 성품이 빚어질 수 있습니다. 우리는 의인의 길은 돋는 햇살 같아서 점점 밝아져 한낮의 광명에 이르거니와 –잠 4:18.라는 말씀을 잘 압니다. 그래도 우리 대부분은 때때로 현재와 미래를 둘러싼 희망 없는 안개를 경험했습니다. 그런 때에 우리는 낮에도 어둠을 만나고 한낮에도 밤처럼 더듬느니라 –욥 5:14. 낙담하여 기진한 우리는 하나님의 선하심을 쉽게 놓칠 수 있습니다. 그로 인해 감사하는 마음을 잃으면 다른 여러 유혹으로 가는 확실한 길이 열리고, 절망이라는 거인이 머리 위로 솟아 죄에 저항하는 우리의 힘을 약하게 하려 합니다.

우리는 엘리야가 우리와 성정이 같은 사람이었음을 –약 5:17. 압니다. 하지만 우리 가운데 갈멜산에서 바알의 선지자들을 이겼을 때 그가 맛본 것만큼 짜릿한 승리를 경험한 사람은 거의 없습니다. 그런데도 그가 호렙에 이르러 그곳 동굴에서 묵은 뒤 찾아온 낙담에는 많은 이가 충분히 공감할 수 있습니다. 호렙은 시내산과 같은 곳으로, 성경에서 처음으로 위대한 산의 장면이 우리 앞에 펼쳐진 곳입니다. 당시에는 모세가 구름 가운데서 하나님을 만났습니다. 율법이 주어졌고 하나님의 영광이 놀랍도록 나타나서 그 광경이 심히 두려우므로 모세도 이르되 내가 심히 두렵고 떨린다 하였느니라 –히 12:21. 이 만질 수 있는 산은 어둡고 갈라진 화강암 봉우리와 묘사할 수 없이 장엄한 험준한 능선이 둘러싼 위압적이고 두려운 산이었습니다. 호렙의 대담하고도 무서운 전면은 노한 위엄을 띠고 수직으로 1,200에서 1,500피트 높이까지 솟아 있습니다.

엘리야의 시야가 흐려지고 그의 영혼이 사상 최저점까지 가라앉았을 때, 하나님은 놀라운 방식으로 그에게 응답하셨습니다—…보라, 여호와께서 지나가시는데 크고 강한 바람이 산을 가르고 여호와 앞에서 바위를 부수었으나 여호와께서 바람 가운데 계시지 아니하였고, 바람 후에 지진이 있었으나 여호와께서 지진 가운데 계시지 아니하였으며, 지진 후에 불이 있었으나 여호와께서 불 가운데 계시지 아니하셨더라. 불 후에 세미한 소리가 있는지라. 엘리야가 그 소리를 듣고 겉옷으로 얼굴을 가리고 나가니… –왕상 19:11-13.

어쩌다 우리는 땅을 뒤흔드는 경험이 하나님의 임재가 드러나는 정수라고 믿게 되었습니다. 우리는 하나님께서 호렙산에서보다 갈멜산에서 엘리야에게 더 가까이 계셨다고 여깁니다. 갈멜산에서 말할 때는 엘리야의 ‘햇빛 찬란한 날’이었습니다. 그는 백성을 꾸짖고 선지자들을 조롱했습니다. 주님의 이름으로 담대히 설교하고 백성에게 이중적인 태도를 회개하라고 명했습니다. 그러나 이제 그의 목소리는 잠잠해졌고, 그는 듣고 있습니다… 자신의 행동과 야망을 돌아보게 하는 세미한 소리를 듣고 있습니다. 그러므로 우리가 멈추어 귀 기울이기만 한다면, 참담한 실패의 기억은 우리가 생각하는 성공을 자랑하게 하는 대신 우리 주님의 문간으로 우리를 이끌 것입니다.

이것이 구름이 베푸는 복된 사역입니다. 주님께서 우리 마음에 자신의 나타난 영광을 참으로 받아들일 수 있는 자리로 우리를 이끄실 때 종종 사용하시는 수단입니다. 이것은 온화한 여름날의 하얗고 솜털 같은 적운이 아니라, 동쪽에서 서쪽까지 하늘을 뒤덮어 하늘의 햇살을 완전히 가리는 평평하고 특징 없는 층운입니다. 층운은 한낮에도 우울함의 무기고로 온종일을 뒤덮어 우리 마음 깊숙이 거슬리게 할 수 있습니다. 다른 날에는 우리의 태도에 별 영향을 주지 않던 작은 일들이 이제는 거인처럼 우뚝 서 있는 듯합니다. 우리가 통제할 수 없음을 아는 일들이 닥쳐도, 우리의 생각은 쉼으로 들어가기를 거부합니다. 이런 때 마침 대화의 상대가 된 불행한 영혼도 비슷한 곤경에 처해 있다면, 우리는 …사람은 고생을 위하여 났으니 불꽃이 위로 날아가는 것 같으니라 –욥 5:7.는 말씀을 직접 겪을 수 있습니다. 또 어떤 때에는 우울한 기분에 빠져 물러나서는 고립된 자기 연민과 안개 같은 비참함을 스스로 먹이며 지내기도 합니다.

절박한 나머지 마음을 위한 약에 의지하여 제한적인 위안을 얻는 이들도 있습니다. 그러나 하나님께서는 우리가 의사와 심리학자에게 도움을 구하도록 구름 속으로 이끄신 것이 아닙니다. 구름의 사역은 다른 모든 대안을 차단하여 그분에게서 위로의 충만한 복을 받게 하는 것입니다. 하나님께서는 우리가 오늘의 눈부신 햇살을 희생하고 내일 그분의 임재가 충만해지기를 바라십니다.

너희가 내일 일을 알지 못하는도다. 너희 생명이 무엇이냐? 너희는 잠깐 보이다가 없어지는 안개니라 –약 4:14. 지난 여러 해 동안 나는 이 구절을 설교하며 영혼들에게 인생의 짧음을 권면하고 세월을 허비하지 말라고 격려했습니다. 그러나 나는 그 토대, 곧 너희가 내일 일을 알지 못한다는 사실을 완전히 무시했습니다. 마음이 젊은 이들에게는 진부하게 들릴지 모르지만, 나이가 든 열매가 계속 익어 가면서 나는 흔하고 뻔한 격언을 점점 더 귀하게 여기게 됩니다. 현대 과학의 세계는 삶을 사랑하는 일에 그토록 완강히 매달려 고난을 통해 맺어지는 사랑의 삶을 깨닫지 못합니다. 과거 시대에 육체의 고난을 겪고 죄를 그친 이들(벧전 4:1)과 마찬가지로, 마음이 흐려지는 연약한 고통을 겪는 사람들도 견디며 결과를 하나님께 맡기기만 한다면 같은 영광에 참여하지 못할 이유가 없다고 나는 생각합니다.

우리는 내일을 예측하는 일에 기대는 오만한 사람들입니다. 은퇴를 계획하고 인생의 일을 완벽하게 세밀히 일정에 넣을 수 있다고 여깁니다. 일기예보는 내일의 기온을 알려 주어 하루를 꼼꼼히 계획하게 합니다. 보험은 미래에 가난해지지 않을 것이라고 안심시켜 줍니다. 냉동고와 은행 계좌는 내일을 훨씬 넘어서도 충분히 버틸 만큼 가득 차 있고, 우리는 …여왕으로 앉아 과부가 아니며 슬픔을 보지 아니하리라 –계 18:7.고 믿는 데 익숙해졌습니다. 그러나 마음의 슬픔은 세상의 편의만으로 쉽게 없앨 수 없습니다. 우리의 생명은 안개(구름)입니다. 우리가 …내일 일을 알지 못하기 때문입니다… –약 4:14. 모든 기술에도 불구하고 우리는 여전히 그 사실을 없앨 수 없습니다. 바로 이때 우리는 삶이 어떠해야 한다는 모든 직감과 기대와 야망을 내려놓고 구름 속에서 우리 하나님을 찾아야 합니다.

그가 보좌의 앞면을 가리시고 그 위에 구름을 펴시느니라 –욥 26:9. 구름이 하나님의 보좌 앞면을 가리는 것이 무슨 유익이 있습니까? 그 모습을 쉽게 볼 수 있다면 우리 대부분은 멀리서 그분과 함께 지내는 것으로 만족할 것입니다. 그러나 짙은 안개가 닥치므로 우리는 그분의 충만함을 경험하기 위해 가까이 나아가야 합니다. 그렇게 되어 있음에 얼마나 감사해야 하는지요. 그렇지 않았다면 우리의 영적 손실이 얼마나 참담했겠습니까.

우리의 자족적인 삶이 언제나 생기 넘치도록 충만하고 하나님을 쉽게 깨달을 수 있다면, 우리는…

…믿음을 잃을 것입니다

우리는 시련이 해피엔딩으로 끝나고 기도가 자연스럽게 더는 필요하지 않게 될 것이라는 보장을 찾습니다. 믿음으로 하나님의 공급하심을 믿지만, 하루에 무슨 일이 닥칠지 모른다는 사실은 연약한 무릎을 꿇고 기도하게 합니다. 하나님을 신뢰하기 어렵게 만드는 일이 많을 수도 있지만, 베일에 가려진 내일은 오히려 신뢰하기 쉽게 해 줍니다. 연구자들은 날씨를 통제하려고 수백만 달러를 쏟아부었습니다. 비구름을 만들려고 상상할 수 있는 모든 구름 씨앗을 대기 중에 뿌렸습니다. 텔아비브 대학교의 연구자들은 이스라엘 북쪽 지역에서 40년간 진행된 구름 씨뿌리기 시도를 검토한 뒤, 구름 씨뿌리기로는 실제로 강수량이 늘어나지 않는다고 결론 내렸습니다. 우리는 얼마나 감사해야 합니까. 알 수 없는 내일을 더 많이 통제할수록 우주의 주님을 믿는 믿음은 그만큼 덜 필요합니다.

야곱은 분노한 형제와 실망한 아버지, 어머니와의 단절을 뒤로하고 떠나면서 전혀 알 수 없는 미래를 마주했습니다. 이것은 보좌에 이르는 사다리의 한 부분이며 전능하신 하나님을 향한 우리의 헌신을 굳건하게 합니다. 이제 우리는 부분적으로 알고 부분적으로 봅니다. 어쩌면 그 작은 부분이 모든 것을 온전히 이해하는 것보다 우리 내면을 더 풍요롭게 해 줄지도 모릅니다. 미래가 충분히 우리의 조종 능력 안에 있다면, 우리는 완벽한 수의 자녀가 완벽한 집에서 풍족하게 살고, 완벽한 직업으로 뒷받침받으며, 완벽하게 무균하고 죽은 완벽한 행동에 둘러싸인 완벽한 유토피아를 만들어 낼 것입니다.

…희망

우리가 예상치 못한 일에 얼마나 큰 빚을 지고 있는지 깨닫고 있는지 의문입니다. 히브리서 기자는 우리의 소망을 …영혼의 닻 같아서 튼튼하고 견고하며… –히 6:19.라고 선언합니다. 아이들이 행복한 것은 큰 꿈을 꾸기 때문입니다. 어떤 일을 기대하고 계획하는 즐거움은 때로 그 일 자체만큼이나 설렙니다. 하루하루는 때 묻지 않고 희망에 찬 마음에 열리는 밝고 새로운 창입니다. 어제의 실망을 통해 경험을 바라보면 냉소와 쓰라림의 벼랑 끝에 서게 될 때가 많습니다. 아들 요셉과 놀랍게 재회한 야곱조차 내 나그네 길의 세월이 짧고 험악하였나이다라고 말했습니다. 본래는 그럴 수 있지만, 반드시 그래야 하는 것은 아닙니다. 바울은 …환난은 인내를, 인내는 연단을, 연단은 소망을 이루는 줄 앎이로다 –롬 5:3-4.라고 말합니다. 내일 무엇이 기다리는지(좋은 일이든 나쁜 일이든) 안다면 소망의 활력을 주는 요소는 틀림없이 줄어들 것입니다. 하와는 더 많은 지식만 얻으면 삶이 더 나아질 것처럼 가장했습니다. 그러나 명확함을 탐욕스럽게 좇으면서 얼마나 복된 소망을 놓쳤습니까.

…사랑

사랑에는 불확실성만이 줄 수 있는 애틋한 다정함이 있습니다. 젊은 남자와 처녀의 관계를 감싸는 것은 불확실한 경이로움입니다. 내일 닥칠지 모르는 위험은 어머니가 자녀를 사랑하고 기도하게 합니다. 가족의 더 밝은 내일을 바라보는 마음이 아버지를 날마다 부지런히 일하게 합니다. 남편과 아내가 성경적인 거룩한 결혼의 하나 됨으로 연합하는 곳마다, 내일을 둘러싼 신비는 웅장한 선율 속의 단조 화음과 같습니다. 그것은 기쁨 속에서 암시된 슬픔을 말하고, 둘러싼 기쁨으로 슬픔을 밝힙니다. 내일 무슨 일이 일어날지 알았더라면 야곱의 7년 기다림이 며칠처럼 느껴졌을까요? 모든 것을 안다면 사랑은 너무 어려울 것입니다. 모든 것을 안다면 사랑은 너무 쉬울 것입니다. 모든 것을 안다면 우리는 마음이 무너질 것입니다. 모든 것을 안다면 우리는 무관심해질 것입니다. 다시 말해, 최악을 모르는 것은 우리를 더 강하게 하고 최선을 모르는 것은 우리를 더 다정하게 합니다. 흐리고 어두워진 우리의 눈으로 바라보는 가운데 이제 믿음, 소망, 사랑 이 세 가지는 항상 있을 것인데 그중에 가장 큰 것은 사랑이라 –고전 13:13.

제자들이 …바라보는데 그가 올려져 가시니 구름이 그를 받아 그들의 시야에서 사라지게 하더라 –행 1:9.는 사실은 우연이 아닙니다. 그러므로 모호하고 알 수 없는 내일이 주는 정신적 긴장과 스트레스를 견뎌야 하는 때가 우리에게 올 것이라는 점에 놀라서는 안 됩니다. …너희 생명이 무엇이냐? 너희는 잠깐 보이다가 없어지는 안개니라 –약 4:14. 우리가 …인자가 구름을 타고 권능과 큰 영광으로 오는 것을 볼 –눅 21:27. 날이 오고 있습니다. 또 이렇게 기록되어 있습니다. 보라, 그가 구름을 타고 오시리니 모든 눈이 그를 보겠고… 그러하리라. 아멘 –계 1:7.

Behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud –Exo 16:10.

What a strange phenomenon is this concentrated mass of vapor that navigates the sky above us. In one instance, a cloud can minister such immense blessedness and hope, while in another it can be the instigator of nagging uncertainty and even the arousal of ragged fear. Clouds were often, no doubt, the welcome shade to the heads of weary fishermen upon Galilee and the propagator of hope to the toiling farmer. How often these clouds part at midday to allow the sun’s beaming rays access to the earth. Then in the evening, they provide the opaque structure for the exquisite beauty of a silver lineation.

We may marvel to see an airplane weighing over 700,000 pounds mount up with wings and soar through the heavens, yet a cloud can carry millions of tons of water without any of the dynamics of human intervention. Clouds are formed when moist, warm air rises to a cooler elevation and water condenses onto microscopic “seeds” such as dust, ash, or bacteria. If there’s more water vapor than places on which it can condense, then ice crystals can also serve as seeds and take on moisture—He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them –Job 26:8. Eventually, these seeds become too heavy for updrafts to support, and then, behold, it is time for the umbrella.

To the parched land in Elijah’s day, the smallest of clouds (like a man’s hand in 1 Kings 18:44) was the answer from the Almighty that He was again prepared to bless His people with rain. Yet, to others like Job and Jeremiah, the cloud represented the ultimate emblem of doubt, despair, and discouragement. Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud –Job 30:15, and Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through –Lam 3:44. It is often in such stressful conditions that God chooses to hide Himself in a cloud. At these times, we grope through the thick foreboding fog in search of the pathway of light, but we find it not. In our discouragement, we may long for the beam of a cloudless day, but it eludes us. We know that God is in the midst of the mist, but we cannot apprehend Him, nor see His blessedness. With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt –Job 36:32.

Why would our God, who loves to commune with us, the vessels of His own creation, choose to hide Himself in a cloud? Why does He often hide His will from our searching and aching hearts? Our finite minds often wonder what glory could possibly arise from such a seemingly distant God, and …to what purpose is this waste –Mat 26:8. While we would never expect it to be God’s divine plan to leave us in a foggy stupor forever, it may be His will for a time. Like a stroll through the valley of the shadow of death, there can be eternal character wrought in the soul who has experienced a seasonal lack of clarity in their path. We are well aware that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Pro 4:18. Still, most of us have, at times, experienced the hopeless fog that surrounds our present and our future. In these times, we meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night –Job 5:14. In our bedraggled discouragement, we can easily lose sight of the goodness of God. Our resulting lack of thankfulness is a sure road to a host of other temptations, while the giant of despair rises overhead in an attempt to weaken our resistance to sin.

We know that Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are –Jam 5:17. Yet, few of us have ever experienced a victory as exhilarating as he did when he triumphed over the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Still, many of us can well relate to the discouragement that followed as he came unto Horeb and lodged in a cave there. This is the same place as Mount Sinai where the first great mountain scene opened before us in the Scriptures. Then it was Moses who met God in the cloud. The law was given, and God’s glory was so marvelously manifested and so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake –Heb 12:21. This mount that might be touched was a formidable and intimidating mountain flanked by splintering dark granite peaks and stern ridges of indescribable grandeur. The bold and awful front of Horeb, rises in frowning majesty from twelve hundred to fifteen hundred feet in perpendicular height.

With Elijah’s vision clouded over and his spirit ebbing away at an all-time low, God responded to him in astounding methodology—…And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out… –1 Kin 19:11-13.

Somehow, we have come to believe that an earthshaking experience is the epitome of God’s manifest presence. We reckon that God was closer to Elijah on Mt. Carmel than He was on Mt. Horeb. It was Elijah’s “day in the sun” while speaking on Mt. Carmel. He chided the people and mocked the prophets. He preached boldly in the name of the Lord and commanded the people to repent of their duplicity. But now his voice has been silenced and he is listening … listening to the still small voice calling into account his own actions and ambitions. Thus, if we will but stop and listen, the memory of our dismal failures will escort us to the front porch of our Lord, rather than allow us to glory in our perceived successes.

This is the blessed ministration of the cloud. It is often the vehicle that the Lord will use to bring us to the place where we can truly receive His manifest glory in our hearts. This is not the white, fluffy, cumulus clouds of a balmy summer day but, rather, the flat and featureless stratus clouds that blanket the heavens from east to west and totally eclipse all the rays of heavenly sunshine. They can enshroud the day at high noon with an arsenal of gloom that rankles our hearts to the core. The little things, that on other days had little effect on our attitudes, now seem to tower as giants before us. We may face advents that we know are beyond our control, but our minds refuse to enter into rest. In times like these, if there happens to be an unfortunate soul on the other end of our conversation experiencing a similar plight, we may experience firsthand that …man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward –Job 5:7. At other times, our melancholy mood may be content to withdraw and feed itself with our own reclusive pity and foggy misery.

Some, in their desperation, turn to medication for the mind and there find a limited valve of relief. But God has not brought us into the cloud so that we may seek the help of physicians and psychologists. The ministration of the cloud is to shut off all other alternatives so that we may receive of Him the full blessedness of His consolation. God is willing that we should sacrifice the shimmering sunshine of today for the fullness of His presence tomorrow.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. In bygone years, I have preached on this verse, exhorting souls concerning the brevity of life and encouraging them to not squander their years away. But I had totally ignored the foundation of it—ye know not what shall be on the morrow. This, perhaps, seems trite to the young at heart, but as the fruit of my age continues to ripen, I have a growing appreciation for the common and obvious idioms. Our modern scientific world is so adamantly pursuing the love of life that it cannot appreciate the life of love that is begotten through suffering. While those who, in ages past, suffered in the flesh and ceased from sin (1 Pet 4:1), I see no reason why those who experience the frail sufferings of a clouded mind may not share the same glory if they will but endure and trust to God the results.

We are an arrogant people who lean on the predictions of tomorrow. We fancy that we can plan our retirement and schedule our life events with immaculate detail. The weather forecasters tell us of tomorrows temperature so that we can meticulously plan our day. Our insurance gives assurance that we will not be subject to future poverty. Our freezers and bank accounts are full enough to see us well past tomorrow, and we have grown accustomed to believing that we …sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow –Rev 18:7. Yet the sorrow of heart cannot be so easily absolved by earthly amenities. Our life is a vapour (cloud) because we …know not what shall be on the morrow… –Jas 4:14. In spite of all our technology we still cannot absolve that fact. It is here that we must lay aside all our intuitions, expectations, and ambitions of what our life ought to be and find our God in the cloud.

He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it –Job 26:9. To what benefit is the cloud covering the face of God’s throne? If it were easily beholden, most of us would be content to dwell with Him from afar. However, due to the impending fog, we must draw nigh to experience His fullness. How thankful we ought to be that it is thus, for how devastating would be our spiritual loss if it were not so.

If our self-sufficient life was always vibrantly full and God were easily apprehended, we would lose…

…Faith

We seek a guarantee that our trials will end happily ever after and that our prayers will naturally become unnecessary. In faith, we believe in God’s provision, but the fact that we know not what a day will bring demands that we fall upon our feeble knees and pray. There may be many things that make it hard for us to trust in God, but the shrouded tomorrow makes it easier. Researchers have spent millions in their efforts to control the weather. They have sown every imaginable cloud seed into the air in efforts to produce rain clouds. After reviewing 40 years of cloud-seeding efforts in an area north of Israel, researchers at Tel Aviv University have concluded that cloud seeding doesn’t actually produce any additional precipitation. How thankful we should be. The more we can control the unknown morrow, the less faith in the Master of the Universe we need.

Jacob, in leaving behind an angry brother, a disappointed father, and a severed tie with his mother, faced an altogether unknown future. This is a part of the ladder to the throne and it fortifies our commitment to our omnipotent God. Now we know in part and we see in part. Perhaps that fractional sliver brings us more inner wealth than if the whole were fully understood. If our future were amply within our manipulative power, we would formulate a perfect utopia supplied with the perfect number of children living sumptuously in the perfect home supported by the perfect job surrounded by perfect behavior that is perfectly sterile and dead.

…Hope

I question if we realize how deeply our debt is to the unexpected. The Hebrew writer declares our hope to be …an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast… –Heb 6:19. Children are happy because they have big dreams. Often the anticipation and planning of an event is almost as thrilling as the excursion itself. Every day is a bright new window to the unspoiled, hopeful mind. Experiences can often bring us to the brink of cynicism and bitterness when viewed through yesterday’s disappointments. Jacob, upon the marvelous reunification with his son, Joseph, still remarked, few and evil have been my days. Though it is naturally so, it needs not to be. Paul states …that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope –Rom 5:3-4. Surely, if we knew what was in store tomorrow (both good and evil) the invigorating element of hope would dwindle. Eve feigned that life would be better if she could only secure more knowledge. But what blessed hope was forfeited in her lustful pursuit of clarity.

…Love

There is a wistful tenderness in love that nothing but uncertainty can give. It is uncertain wonder that encompasses the way of a young man with a maid. The unknown perils of tomorrow drive a mother to love and prayer for her children. It is the vision of a brighter tomorrow for his family that moves a father to diligence in his daily work. Wherever a husband and his wife are knit together in Biblical oneness of holy matrimony, the mystery that envelops tomorrow is like the minor chord in a great melody. It speaks in joy of a suggested sorrow and brightens sorrow with encircling joy. Would Jacob’s seven-year wait have seemed like a few days if he had known what the morrow would bring? If we knew everything, love would be too hard. If we knew everything, love would be too easy. If we knew everything, we would be brokenhearted. If we knew everything, we would be unconcerned. In other words, it makes us stronger to not know the worst and it makes us more tender to not know the best. For in our clouded and darkened lens there …abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Cor 13:13.

It is no coincidence that while the disciples …beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight –Act 1:9. And so we dare not be surprised that, at times, we shall be called to suffer the mental strain and stress of an obscure and unknown tomorrow. …For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. There is coming a day when we shall …see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory –Luk 21:27. And again it is written, Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him … Even so, Amen –Rev 1:7.

看哪，耶和华的荣光在云中显现——出16:10。

我们头顶的天空中，有这样一团凝聚的水汽在移动，真是奇妙。云有时能带来极大的福分和盼望，有时却会引发挥之不去的不安，甚至激起支离破碎的恐惧。毫无疑问，云常常为加利利海上疲惫的渔夫遮荫，也给辛劳耕作的农夫带来盼望。这些云层常在正午散开，让阳光灿烂的光芒照到大地。到了傍晚，它们又构成一层不透明的屏障，映衬出银色线条的绝美景致。

我们或许会惊叹，一架重达七十多万磅的飞机竟能振翅升空、翱翔天际；然而，一朵云却能承载数百万吨的水，全然不需要人的力量介入。潮湿温暖的空气上升到较冷的高处，水便凝结在尘埃、灰烬或细菌等微小的“种子”上，云就此形成。如果水汽多于可供凝结的地方，冰晶也能充当种子，吸收水汽——他将水包在密云中，云却不破裂——伯26:8。最后，这些种子变得太重，上升气流无法托住，于是，看哪，到了该撑伞的时候。

以利亚时代的干旱土地上，一小片云（如王上18:44所说，像人手那么大）就是全能者给出的答案，表明他准备再次降雨赐福给他的子民。然而，对约伯和耶利米这样的人来说，云却代表着疑惑、绝望和沮丧的终极象征。惊恐临到我，追赶我的灵魂如风；我的福乐消散如云——伯30:15，又说：你以云彩遮蔽自己，以致祷告不得透入——哀3:44。上帝常常选择在这样的艰难处境中把自己隐藏在云里。此时，我们在浓重而令人不安的迷雾中摸索，寻找光明之路，却寻不着。我们灰心失望，渴望无云日子的一缕阳光，却始终无法得到。我们知道上帝就在雾中，却无法领会他，也看不见他的恩惠。他用密云遮掩亮光，又吩咐云彩不许发光，因为云彩横在其中——伯36:32。

我们的上帝爱与我们这些由他亲手创造的器皿交通，他为何要选择把自己隐藏在云里？他为何常向我们探求而痛苦的心隐藏自己的旨意？我们有限的心思常会疑惑，这样一位看似遥远的上帝，怎可能带来什么荣耀；我们也会说：……何用这样枉费呢？——太26:8。我们绝不会认为上帝的神圣计划是永远让我们陷在迷雾中昏昏沉沉，但有时这或许是他的旨意。就像走过死荫的幽谷，灵魂若曾经历一段道路不明的时期，里面便能塑造出永恒的品格。我们很清楚，义人的路好像黎明的光，越照越明，直到日午——箴4:18。然而，我们大多数人有时都曾经历那笼罩着当下和未来、令人绝望的迷雾。在这样的时刻，我们白昼遇见黑暗，午间摸索如在夜间——伯5:14。在狼狈沮丧之中，我们很容易看不见上帝的良善。由此而来的不知感恩，必然会引向种种其他试探；与此同时，绝望这个巨人高高耸立，试图削弱我们抵挡罪的力量。

我们知道，以利亚与我们是一样性情的人——雅5:17。然而，我们中很少有人经历过像他在迦密山战胜巴力先知那样令人振奋的胜利。即便如此，他后来来到何烈山，住在一个洞里时所经历的灰心，我们许多人都能感同身受。这地方就是西奈山，圣经中第一次向我们展现伟大山景之处。当时是摩西在云中遇见上帝。律法颁布，上帝的荣耀奇妙地显现出来，甚至那景象甚是可怕，摩西说：“我甚是恐惧战兢。”——来12:21。这座能摸的山巍峨险峻，令人敬畏；深色花岗岩山峰崩裂耸立，严峻的山脊气势壮丽，难以形容。何烈山巍峨雄伟、令人敬畏的正面，垂直拔地而起，高约一千二百至一千五百英尺。

以利亚的视线被云遮蔽，灵里也衰弱到了前所未有的低谷，上帝以令人惊叹的方式回应他——……耶和华从那里经过，在他面前有暴风大作，山被崩裂，磐石被耶和华震碎；风后地震，耶和华却不在其中；地震后有火，耶和华也不在其中；火后有微小的声音。以利亚听见，就用外衣蒙上脸，出来……——王上19:11-13。

不知从何时起，我们开始相信，震撼大地的经历就是上帝显明同在的极致。我们以为，上帝在迦密山时比在何烈山时更亲近以利亚。在迦密山发言时，那是以利亚的“高光时刻”。他责备百姓，嘲笑先知；他奉主的名大胆讲道，吩咐百姓悔改，不要再三心二意。但如今，他的声音沉寂了，他在聆听……聆听那微小的声音，追问他自己的行为和雄心。因此，我们若肯停下来聆听，惨败的记忆便会引领我们来到主的门廊前，而不是让我们因自以为是的成功而自夸。

这就是云所带来的蒙福服事。主常借着云，把我们带到一个地方，使我们能够在心里真正领受他彰显的荣耀。这不是和煦夏日里白而蓬松的积云，而是平坦无状的层云，从东到西铺满天空，把天上阳光的光芒完全遮蔽。它们能在正午以一股阴郁的力量笼罩白昼，令我们的心深处烦躁不安。其他日子里对我们情绪影响不大的小事，如今仿佛巨人般高高耸立在眼前。我们可能遭逢一些明知超出自己掌控的事，但心思仍不肯安息。在这样的时刻，若谈话的另一端恰好有个不幸的人也正遭遇类似困境，我们就可能亲身体验到：人生在世必遇患难，如同火星飞腾——伯5:7。有时，我们忧郁的心情或许甘愿退隐，自我封闭，在自怜和迷雾般的痛苦中自得其乐。

有些人在绝望之中转而服用精神类药物，从中得到有限的纾解。但上帝带我们进入云中，并不是要我们寻求医生和心理学家的帮助。云的服事是要切断其他一切选择，使我们能从他那里充分领受安慰的福分。上帝愿意我们牺牲今天闪耀的阳光，好在明天得到他同在的丰盛。

其实明天如何，你们还不知道。你们的生命是什么呢？你们原来是一片云雾，出现少时就不见了——雅4:14。过去这些年，我曾讲解这节经文，劝勉人们要留意人生短暂，不要虚度年华。但我完全忽略了它的根基——你们还不知道明天如何。这话对心境年轻的人或许显得平淡无奇，但随着岁月的果实日渐成熟，我越来越体会到那些寻常而显而易见的话语的可贵。我们现代科学世界如此执着于追求生命本身，以致无法体会由苦难孕育而来的爱之生命。古时那些肉身受苦、止住罪恶的人（彼前4:1），既然如此，我看不出为何那些经历心灵蒙云之脆弱痛苦的人，只要他们忍耐，并把结果交托给上帝，就不能同享那份荣耀。

我们是骄傲的人，倚赖对明天的预测。我们自以为能够详尽地规划退休生活，安排人生中的各项大事。天气预报告诉我们明天的气温，好让我们可以周密地安排一天。保险让我们确信将来不会陷入贫困。我们的冰箱和银行账户里都储备充足，足以让我们平安度过明天；我们也习惯相信自己……坐了女王的位，并不是寡妇，也绝不见悲哀——启18:7。然而，世间的便利无法轻易消解内心的忧伤。我们的生命是一片云雾，因为我们……还不知道明天如何……——雅4:14。尽管科技日新月异，我们仍无法消除这一事实。正是在这里，我们必须放下对人生应当如何的种种直觉、期望和抱负，在云中寻见我们的上帝。

他把宝座的脸遮住，将云铺在其上——伯26:9。上帝宝座的面容被云遮住，对我们有什么益处？如果很容易看见，大多数人就会满足于远远地与他同住。然而，正因为前方迷雾重重，我们必须亲近他，才能经历他的丰盛。我们应当何等感恩，事情正是如此；若非如此，我们灵里的损失将会多么惨重。

如果我们的自足生活总是充满活力，上帝也总是容易被人领会，我们就会失去……

……信心

我们寻求一个保证，确信试炼最终会有圆满结局，祷告也自然会变得不再必要。凭着信心，我们相信上帝的供应；但我们不知道一天会带来什么，这事实促使我们俯伏在软弱的膝上祷告。许多事情可能使我们难以信靠上帝，但被遮蔽的明天却让信靠容易一些。研究人员花费数百万，努力控制天气。他们把各种可以想象的造云种子播撒到空中，试图制造雨云。特拉维夫大学的研究人员回顾以色列北部地区四十年来的人工增雨尝试后得出结论：播云并没有实际带来额外降水。我们应当何等感恩。我们越能掌控未知的明天，就越不需要信靠宇宙的主宰。

雅各离开愤怒的哥哥、失望的父亲，又与母亲断了联系，面对的是一个全然未知的未来。这是通往宝座的阶梯的一部分，也坚固了我们对全能上帝的委身。如今我们所知道的有限，所看见的也有限。或许，这一小部分反而带给我们更多内在的财富，胜过完全明白一切。如果未来完全在我们操纵的能力之内，我们就会构想一个完美的乌托邦：有恰到好处数量的孩子，在完美的家中生活优渥；有完美的工作作为支撑，周围的一切行为完美无瑕，却死气沉沉。

……盼望

我不禁怀疑，我们是否意识到自己对意外有多么亏欠。希伯来书的作者称我们的盼望为……灵魂的锚，又坚固又牢靠……——来6:19。孩子们快乐，因为他们有远大的梦想。常常，期待和筹划一件事，几乎与真正出发去做同样令人兴奋。对未经世事、满怀盼望的心来说，每一天都是一扇明亮崭新的窗。若用昨日的失望来看待经历，我们往往会走到愤世嫉俗、心怀苦毒的边缘。雅各与儿子约瑟奇妙团聚之后，仍说：我平生的年日又少又苦。这虽是自然会有的情形，却不必如此。保罗说：……患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望——罗5:3-4。诚然，若我们知道明天会有什么等着自己（无论好坏），盼望那振奋人心的力量就会减退。夏娃假装认为，只要获得更多知识，生活就会更好。但她在贪恋清楚明白的过程中，失去了多么蒙福的盼望啊。

……爱

爱中有一种惆怅而温柔的情愫，唯有不确定才能赋予。年轻男子与女子同行的情景，笼罩在一种因未知而生的奇妙之中。明日未知的危险，促使母亲疼爱儿女、为儿女祷告。对家庭更光明未来的憧憬，激励父亲勤勉工作。在丈夫和妻子以圣洁婚姻的圣经原则合而为一之处，笼罩着明日的奥秘就像一首宏大乐曲中的小调和弦。它以喜乐诉说隐约可感的忧伤，又以环绕的喜乐照亮忧伤。雅各若知道明天会带来什么，他那七年的等待还会仿佛只有几天吗？如果我们什么都知道，爱就会太难；如果我们什么都知道，爱就会太容易；如果我们什么都知道，就会伤心欲绝；如果我们什么都知道，就会漠不关心。换句话说，不知道最坏的事使我们更坚强，不知道最好的事使我们更温柔。因为在我们蒙云遮蔽、昏暗不明的视野中，常存的有信，有望，有爱这三样，其中最大的是爱——林前13:13。

门徒……正看的时候，他就被取上升，有一朵云彩把他接去，便看不见他了——徒1:9。这绝非偶然。因此，我们不敢因有时要承受心灵的重压、面对晦暗未知的明天而感到惊讶。……你们的生命是什么呢？你们原来是一片云雾，出现少时就不见了——雅4:14。有一天将要来到，那时我们要……看见人子有能力、有大荣耀，驾云降临——路21:27。经上又说：看哪，他驾云降临！众目都要看见他……阿们！——启1:7。

Behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud –Exo 16:10.

What a strange phenomenon is this concentrated mass of vapor that navigates the sky above us. In one instance, a cloud can minister such immense blessedness and hope, while in another it can be the instigator of nagging uncertainty and even the arousal of ragged fear. Clouds were often, no doubt, the welcome shade to the heads of weary fishermen upon Galilee and the propagator of hope to the toiling farmer. How often these clouds part at midday to allow the sun’s beaming rays access to the earth. Then in the evening, they provide the opaque structure for the exquisite beauty of a silver lineation.

We may marvel to see an airplane weighing over 700,000 pounds mount up with wings and soar through the heavens, yet a cloud can carry millions of tons of water without any of the dynamics of human intervention. Clouds are formed when moist, warm air rises to a cooler elevation and water condenses onto microscopic “seeds” such as dust, ash, or bacteria. If there’s more water vapor than places on which it can condense, then ice crystals can also serve as seeds and take on moisture—He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them –Job 26:8. Eventually, these seeds become too heavy for updrafts to support, and then, behold, it is time for the umbrella.

To the parched land in Elijah’s day, the smallest of clouds (like a man’s hand in 1 Kings 18:44) was the answer from the Almighty that He was again prepared to bless His people with rain. Yet, to others like Job and Jeremiah, the cloud represented the ultimate emblem of doubt, despair, and discouragement. Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud –Job 30:15, and Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through –Lam 3:44. It is often in such stressful conditions that God chooses to hide Himself in a cloud. At these times, we grope through the thick foreboding fog in search of the pathway of light, but we find it not. In our discouragement, we may long for the beam of a cloudless day, but it eludes us. We know that God is in the midst of the mist, but we cannot apprehend Him, nor see His blessedness. With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt –Job 36:32.

Why would our God, who loves to commune with us, the vessels of His own creation, choose to hide Himself in a cloud? Why does He often hide His will from our searching and aching hearts? Our finite minds often wonder what glory could possibly arise from such a seemingly distant God, and …to what purpose is this waste –Mat 26:8. While we would never expect it to be God’s divine plan to leave us in a foggy stupor forever, it may be His will for a time. Like a stroll through the valley of the shadow of death, there can be eternal character wrought in the soul who has experienced a seasonal lack of clarity in their path. We are well aware that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Pro 4:18. Still, most of us have, at times, experienced the hopeless fog that surrounds our present and our future. In these times, we meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night –Job 5:14. In our bedraggled discouragement, we can easily lose sight of the goodness of God. Our resulting lack of thankfulness is a sure road to a host of other temptations, while the giant of despair rises overhead in an attempt to weaken our resistance to sin.

We know that Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are –Jam 5:17. Yet, few of us have ever experienced a victory as exhilarating as he did when he triumphed over the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Still, many of us can well relate to the discouragement that followed as he came unto Horeb and lodged in a cave there. This is the same place as Mount Sinai where the first great mountain scene opened before us in the Scriptures. Then it was Moses who met God in the cloud. The law was given, and God’s glory was so marvelously manifested and so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake –Heb 12:21. This mount that might be touched was a formidable and intimidating mountain flanked by splintering dark granite peaks and stern ridges of indescribable grandeur. The bold and awful front of Horeb, rises in frowning majesty from twelve hundred to fifteen hundred feet in perpendicular height.

With Elijah’s vision clouded over and his spirit ebbing away at an all-time low, God responded to him in astounding methodology—…And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out… –1 Kin 19:11-13.

Somehow, we have come to believe that an earthshaking experience is the epitome of God’s manifest presence. We reckon that God was closer to Elijah on Mt. Carmel than He was on Mt. Horeb. It was Elijah’s “day in the sun” while speaking on Mt. Carmel. He chided the people and mocked the prophets. He preached boldly in the name of the Lord and commanded the people to repent of their duplicity. But now his voice has been silenced and he is listening … listening to the still small voice calling into account his own actions and ambitions. Thus, if we will but stop and listen, the memory of our dismal failures will escort us to the front porch of our Lord, rather than allow us to glory in our perceived successes.

This is the blessed ministration of the cloud. It is often the vehicle that the Lord will use to bring us to the place where we can truly receive His manifest glory in our hearts. This is not the white, fluffy, cumulus clouds of a balmy summer day but, rather, the flat and featureless stratus clouds that blanket the heavens from east to west and totally eclipse all the rays of heavenly sunshine. They can enshroud the day at high noon with an arsenal of gloom that rankles our hearts to the core. The little things, that on other days had little effect on our attitudes, now seem to tower as giants before us. We may face advents that we know are beyond our control, but our minds refuse to enter into rest. In times like these, if there happens to be an unfortunate soul on the other end of our conversation experiencing a similar plight, we may experience firsthand that …man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward –Job 5:7. At other times, our melancholy mood may be content to withdraw and feed itself with our own reclusive pity and foggy misery.

Some, in their desperation, turn to medication for the mind and there find a limited valve of relief. But God has not brought us into the cloud so that we may seek the help of physicians and psychologists. The ministration of the cloud is to shut off all other alternatives so that we may receive of Him the full blessedness of His consolation. God is willing that we should sacrifice the shimmering sunshine of today for the fullness of His presence tomorrow.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. In bygone years, I have preached on this verse, exhorting souls concerning the brevity of life and encouraging them to not squander their years away. But I had totally ignored the foundation of it—ye know not what shall be on the morrow. This, perhaps, seems trite to the young at heart, but as the fruit of my age continues to ripen, I have a growing appreciation for the common and obvious idioms. Our modern scientific world is so adamantly pursuing the love of life that it cannot appreciate the life of love that is begotten through suffering. While those who, in ages past, suffered in the flesh and ceased from sin (1 Pet 4:1), I see no reason why those who experience the frail sufferings of a clouded mind may not share the same glory if they will but endure and trust to God the results.

We are an arrogant people who lean on the predictions of tomorrow. We fancy that we can plan our retirement and schedule our life events with immaculate detail. The weather forecasters tell us of tomorrows temperature so that we can meticulously plan our day. Our insurance gives assurance that we will not be subject to future poverty. Our freezers and bank accounts are full enough to see us well past tomorrow, and we have grown accustomed to believing that we …sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow –Rev 18:7. Yet the sorrow of heart cannot be so easily absolved by earthly amenities. Our life is a vapour (cloud) because we …know not what shall be on the morrow… –Jas 4:14. In spite of all our technology we still cannot absolve that fact. It is here that we must lay aside all our intuitions, expectations, and ambitions of what our life ought to be and find our God in the cloud.

He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it –Job 26:9. To what benefit is the cloud covering the face of God’s throne? If it were easily beholden, most of us would be content to dwell with Him from afar. However, due to the impending fog, we must draw nigh to experience His fullness. How thankful we ought to be that it is thus, for how devastating would be our spiritual loss if it were not so.

If our self-sufficient life was always vibrantly full and God were easily apprehended, we would lose…

…Faith

We seek a guarantee that our trials will end happily ever after and that our prayers will naturally become unnecessary. In faith, we believe in God’s provision, but the fact that we know not what a day will bring demands that we fall upon our feeble knees and pray. There may be many things that make it hard for us to trust in God, but the shrouded tomorrow makes it easier. Researchers have spent millions in their efforts to control the weather. They have sown every imaginable cloud seed into the air in efforts to produce rain clouds. After reviewing 40 years of cloud-seeding efforts in an area north of Israel, researchers at Tel Aviv University have concluded that cloud seeding doesn’t actually produce any additional precipitation. How thankful we should be. The more we can control the unknown morrow, the less faith in the Master of the Universe we need.

Jacob, in leaving behind an angry brother, a disappointed father, and a severed tie with his mother, faced an altogether unknown future. This is a part of the ladder to the throne and it fortifies our commitment to our omnipotent God. Now we know in part and we see in part. Perhaps that fractional sliver brings us more inner wealth than if the whole were fully understood. If our future were amply within our manipulative power, we would formulate a perfect utopia supplied with the perfect number of children living sumptuously in the perfect home supported by the perfect job surrounded by perfect behavior that is perfectly sterile and dead.

…Hope

I question if we realize how deeply our debt is to the unexpected. The Hebrew writer declares our hope to be …an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast… –Heb 6:19. Children are happy because they have big dreams. Often the anticipation and planning of an event is almost as thrilling as the excursion itself. Every day is a bright new window to the unspoiled, hopeful mind. Experiences can often bring us to the brink of cynicism and bitterness when viewed through yesterday’s disappointments. Jacob, upon the marvelous reunification with his son, Joseph, still remarked, few and evil have been my days. Though it is naturally so, it needs not to be. Paul states …that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope –Rom 5:3-4. Surely, if we knew what was in store tomorrow (both good and evil) the invigorating element of hope would dwindle. Eve feigned that life would be better if she could only secure more knowledge. But what blessed hope was forfeited in her lustful pursuit of clarity.

…Love

There is a wistful tenderness in love that nothing but uncertainty can give. It is uncertain wonder that encompasses the way of a young man with a maid. The unknown perils of tomorrow drive a mother to love and prayer for her children. It is the vision of a brighter tomorrow for his family that moves a father to diligence in his daily work. Wherever a husband and his wife are knit together in Biblical oneness of holy matrimony, the mystery that envelops tomorrow is like the minor chord in a great melody. It speaks in joy of a suggested sorrow and brightens sorrow with encircling joy. Would Jacob’s seven-year wait have seemed like a few days if he had known what the morrow would bring? If we knew everything, love would be too hard. If we knew everything, love would be too easy. If we knew everything, we would be brokenhearted. If we knew everything, we would be unconcerned. In other words, it makes us stronger to not know the worst and it makes us more tender to not know the best. For in our clouded and darkened lens there …abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Cor 13:13.

It is no coincidence that while the disciples …beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight –Act 1:9. And so we dare not be surprised that, at times, we shall be called to suffer the mental strain and stress of an obscure and unknown tomorrow. …For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. There is coming a day when we shall …see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory –Luk 21:27. And again it is written, Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him … Even so, Amen –Rev 1:7.

Se, HERRENS herlighet viste seg i skyen – 2 Mos 16:10.

For et merkelig fenomen denne konsentrerte dampmassen som beveger seg over himmelen over oss, er. I ett øyeblikk kan en sky bringe umåtelig velsignelse og håp, mens den i et annet kan bli årsak til gnagende usikkerhet og til og med vekke en rå frykt. Skyer var utvilsomt ofte en kjærkommen skygge for hodene til slitne fiskere ved Galilea-sjøen og en kilde til håp for den strevende bonden. Hvor ofte deler ikke disse skyene seg midt på dagen og slipper solens strålende stråler ned til jorden. Om kvelden gir de så den ugjennomsiktige bakgrunnen for den utsøkte skjønnheten i en sølvskimrende kant.

Vi kan undres over å se et fly på over 700 000 pund løfte seg med vingene og sveve gjennom himmelen, men en sky kan bære millioner av tonn vann uten noen form for menneskelig inngrep. Skyer dannes når fuktig, varm luft stiger til en kjøligere høyde og vann kondenserer på mikroskopiske «frø» som støv, aske eller bakterier. Hvis det er mer vanndamp enn det finnes steder den kan kondensere på, kan også iskrystaller fungere som frø og ta opp fuktighet – Han samler vannet i sine tette skyer; skyen revner ikke under det – Job 26:8. Til slutt blir disse frøene for tunge til at oppdriften kan holde dem oppe, og da, se, er tiden kommet for paraplyen.

For det uttørkede landet på Elias’ tid var den minste skyen (som en manns hånd i 1. Kongebok 18:44) svaret fra Den Allmektige om at han igjen var rede til å velsigne sitt folk med regn. Men for andre, som Job og Jeremia, sto skyen for det ytterste symbolet på tvil, fortvilelse og motløshet. Redsel kommer over meg; de jager min sjel som vinden, og min lykke svinner som en sky – Job 30:15, og Du har hyllet deg i en sky, så vår bønn ikke trenger gjennom – Klag 3:44. Det er ofte under slike belastende forhold Gud velger å skjule seg i en sky. På slike tider famler vi oss gjennom den tette, illevarslende tåken på jakt etter lysets sti, men finner den ikke. I vår motløshet lengter vi kanskje etter strålene fra en skyfri dag, men de unngår oss. Vi vet at Gud er midt i tåken, men vi kan ikke fatte ham eller se hans velsignelse. Han dekker lyset med skyer og lar det ikke skinne gjennom skyen som kommer imellom – Job 36:32.

Hvorfor skulle vår Gud, som gjerne taler med oss, skapningene han selv har formet, velge å skjule seg i en sky? Hvorfor skjuler han ofte sin vilje for våre søkende og sårede hjerter? Vårt begrensede sinn undrer seg ofte over hvilken herlighet som vel kan komme fra en Gud som synes så fjern, og … hva skal denne sløsingen være til? – Matt 26:8. Selv om vi aldri ville vente at det skulle være Guds guddommelige plan å la oss bli værende i en tåketilstand for alltid, kan det være hans vilje for en tid. Som på en vandring gjennom dødsskyggens dal kan det skapes en evig karakter i sjelen til den som har opplevd at stien en tid var uklar. Vi vet godt at de rettferdiges sti er som det strålende lys, som skinner klarere og klarere til høylys dag – Ordsp 4:18. Likevel har de fleste av oss tidvis opplevd den håpløse tåken som omgir nåtiden og framtiden vår. I slike tider møter vi mørke om dagen og famler ved middagstid som om det var natt – Job 5:14. Når vi er nedkjørte og motløse, kan vi lett miste Guds godhet av syne. Vår mangel på takknemlighet som følger av dette, fører oss rett inn i en rekke andre fristelser, mens fortvilelsens kjempe rager over oss og forsøker å svekke vår motstand mot synd.

Vi vet at Elias var et menneske undergitt de samme lidenskaper som vi – Jak 5:17. Likevel har få av oss noen gang opplevd en seier så berusende som den han vant da han seiret over Ba’als profeter på Karmel-fjellet. Mange av oss kan likevel godt kjenne oss igjen i motløsheten som fulgte da han kom til Horeb og tok inn i en hule der. Dette er samme sted som Sinai-fjellet, der den første store fjellscenen åpnet seg for oss i Skriften. Den gangen var det Moses som møtte Gud i skyen. Loven ble gitt, og Guds herlighet ble åpenbart så underfullt, og så fryktinngytende var synet at Moses sa: «Jeg er så redd at jeg skjelver» – Hebr 12:21. Dette fjellet som kunne berøres var et mektig og skremmende fjell, flankert av taggete, mørke granittopptinder og strenge fjellrygger av ubeskrivelig storhet. Den dristige og fryktinngytende fronten av Horeb reiser seg i truende majestet fra tolv hundre til femten hundre fot rett opp.

Mens Elias’ syn ble tåkete og ånden hans svant hen til et historisk lavmål, svarte Gud ham på en forbløffende måte – … Og se, HERREN drog forbi, og en stor og sterk vind rev fjellene i stykker og knuste klippene foran HERREN; men HERREN var ikke i vinden. Etter vinden kom et jordskjelv, men HERREN var ikke i jordskjelvet. Etter jordskjelvet kom en ild, men HERREN var ikke i ilden. Etter ilden kom en stille, lav røst. Da Elias hørte den, hyllet han ansiktet i kappen sin og gikk ut … – 1 Kong 19:11–13.

På en eller annen måte har vi kommet til å tro at en jordskjelvende opplevelse er selve høydepunktet av Guds nærvær. Vi regner med at Gud var nærmere Elias på Karmel-fjellet enn han var på Horeb-fjellet. Det var Elias’ «dag i solen» da han talte på Karmel-fjellet. Han irettesatte folket og hånte profetene. Han forkynte frimodig i Herrens navn og befalte folket å angre sin troløshet. Men nå er stemmen hans stilnet, og han lytter … lytter til den stille, lave røsten som stiller ham selv til ansvar for hans handlinger og ambisjoner. Hvis vi derfor bare stanser opp og lytter, vil minnet om våre sørgelige nederlag følge oss til vår Herres dør, i stedet for å la oss rose oss av våre antatte seire.

Dette er skyens velsignede tjeneste. Den er ofte det redskapet Herren bruker for å føre oss til et sted der vi virkelig kan ta imot hans åpenbarte herlighet i hjertene våre. Dette er ikke de hvite, luftige cumulusskyene på en mild sommerdag, men snarere de flate og formløse stratusskyene som dekker himmelen fra øst til vest og fullstendig stenger ute alle strålene fra den himmelske solen. De kan hylle dagen ved høylys dag i et arsenal av tungsinn som gnager oss inn til beinet. Småting som andre dager knapt påvirket holdningen vår, synes nå å rage foran oss som kjemper. Vi kan møte hendelser som vi vet er utenfor vår kontroll, men sinnet vårt nekter å finne ro. I slike tider kan vi, hvis det tilfeldigvis er en ulykkelig sjel i den andre enden av samtalen vår som opplever en lignende prøvelse, selv erfare at … mennesket er født til møye, som gnistene flyr oppover – Job 5:7. Andre ganger kan vårt melankolske humør trekke seg tilbake og nære seg av vår egen isolerte selvmedlidenhet og tåkete elendighet.

Noen tyr i sin fortvilelse til medisiner for sinnet og finner der en begrenset ventil for lettelse. Men Gud har ikke ført oss inn i skyen for at vi skal søke hjelp hos leger og psykologer. Skyens tjeneste er å stenge ute alle andre alternativer, så vi kan ta imot hele fylden av hans trøst. Gud er villig til at vi skal ofre dagens skinnende sol for fylden av hans nærvær i morgen.

Dere vet jo ikke hva morgendagen vil bringe. Hva er livet deres? Dere er en damp som viser seg en kort stund og så forsvinner – Jak 4:14. I tidligere år har jeg prekt over dette verset, formant mennesker om livets korthet og oppmuntret dem til ikke å sløse bort årene sine. Men jeg hadde fullstendig oversett grunnlaget for det – dere vet ikke hva morgendagen vil bringe. Dette virker kanskje banalt for den som er ung til sinns, men etter hvert som frukten av min alder fortsetter å modnes, setter jeg stadig større pris på de vanlige og åpenbare talemåtene. Vår moderne, vitenskapelige verden jager så iherdig etter kjærligheten til livet at den ikke kan verdsette kjærlighetens liv, som fødes gjennom lidelse. Når jeg tenker på dem som i tidligere tider led i kjødet og sluttet med synd (1 Pet 4:1), ser jeg ingen grunn til at de som opplever sinnets skjøre lidelser under en skyet himmel, ikke skulle få del i den samme herligheten dersom de bare holder ut og overlater resultatene til Gud.

Vi er et arrogant folk som støtter oss på spådommer om morgendagen. Vi innbiller oss at vi kan planlegge pensjonisttilværelsen og tidfeste livets begivenheter med nøyaktige detaljer. Værmelderne forteller oss morgendagens temperatur, så vi kan planlegge dagen omhyggelig. Forsikringen vår garanterer at vi ikke skal bli rammet av framtidig fattigdom. Fryserne og bankkontoene våre er fulle nok til at vi skal klare oss godt forbi morgendagen, og vi er blitt vant til å tro at vi … sitter som dronning og er ikke enke og skal ikke se sorg – Åp 18:7. Likevel kan hjertesorg ikke så lett fjernes med jordiske bekvemmeligheter. Livet vårt er en damp (sky) fordi vi … ikke vet hva morgendagen vil bringe … – Jak 4:14. Til tross for all teknologien vår kan vi fortsatt ikke oppheve dette faktum. Her må vi legge til side alle våre intuisjoner, forventninger og ambisjoner om hvordan livet vårt burde være, og finne Gud i skyen.

Han holder sitt trones ansikt tilbake og brer sin sky over det – Job 26:9. Hvilken nytte er det i at skyen dekker Guds trones ansikt? Hvis det var lett å se det, ville de fleste av oss være tilfredse med å bo hos ham på avstand. Men på grunn av den forestående tåken må vi komme nær for å oppleve hans fylde. Hvor takknemlige vi bør være for at det er slik, for hvor ødeleggende vårt åndelige tap ville vært om det ikke var slik.

Hvis vårt selvtilstrekkelige liv alltid var sprudlende fullt og Gud var lett å fatte, ville vi miste …

…Tro

Vi søker en garanti for at prøvelsene våre skal ende lykkelig alle sine dager, og at bønnene våre naturlig nok skal bli unødvendige. I tro tror vi på Guds omsorg, men det faktum at vi ikke vet hva en dag vil bringe, krever at vi faller på våre svake knær og ber. Det kan være mange ting som gjør det vanskelig for oss å stole på Gud, men morgendagens usikkerhet gjør det lettere. Forskere har brukt millioner i sine forsøk på å kontrollere været. De har sådd alle tenkelige skyfrø i luften i forsøk på å skape regnskyer. Etter å ha gjennomgått 40 års forsøk på skysåing i et område nord for Israel har forskere ved Tel Aviv-universitetet konkludert med at skysåing faktisk ikke gir noen ekstra nedbør. Hvor takknemlige vi bør være. Jo mer vi kan kontrollere den ukjente morgendagen, desto mindre tro trenger vi på universets Herre.

Da Jakob etterlot seg en sint bror, en skuffet far og et brutt bånd til moren sin, sto han overfor en helt ukjent framtid. Dette er en del av stigen til tronen, og det styrker vår hengivenhet til vår allmektige Gud. Nå vet vi stykkevis, og vi ser stykkevis. Kanskje gir denne brøkdelen oss større indre rikdom enn om helheten var fullt ut forstått. Hvis framtiden vår lå helt og holdent innenfor vår manipulerende makt, ville vi utforme en perfekt utopi, fylt med det perfekte antallet barn som lever i overflod i det perfekte hjemmet, forsørget av den perfekte jobben og omgitt av en perfekt adferd som er fullstendig steril og død.

…Håp

Jeg spør meg om vi innser hvor mye vi skylder det uventede. Hebreerbrevets forfatter sier at vårt håp er … et anker for sjelen, både sikkert og fast … – Hebr 6:19. Barn er glade fordi de har store drømmer. Ofte er forventningen og planleggingen av en begivenhet nesten like spennende som selve utflukten. Hver dag er et lyst, nytt vindu for et ufordervet, håpefullt sinn. Erfaringer kan ofte føre oss til randen av kynisme og bitterhet når vi ser dem gjennom gårsdagens skuffelser. Da Jakob på underfullt vis ble gjenforent med sønnen Josef, sa han likevel: Få og onde har mine dager vært. Selv om det naturlig nok er slik, behøver det ikke være slik. Paulus sier: … trengselen virker tålmodighet, og tålmodigheten prøvethet, og prøvetheten håp – Rom 5:3–4. Hvis vi visste hva morgendagen rommet (både godt og ondt), ville håpets livgivende kraft visselig avta. Eva lot som om livet ville bli bedre hvis hun bare kunne skaffe seg mer kunnskap. Men hvilken velsignet håp hun ga avkall på i sin lystne jakt på klarhet.

…Kjærlighet

Det finnes en lengselsfull ømhet i kjærligheten som bare usikkerhet kan gi. Det er en usikker undring som omgir en ung manns ferd med en ung kvinne. Morgendagens ukjente farer driver en mor til å elske og be for barna sine. Det er synet av en lysere morgendag for familien hans som får en far til å arbeide flittig hver dag. Når en mann og hans kone er bundet sammen i Bibelens enhet i det hellige ekteskapet, er mysteriet som omslutter morgendagen som en mollakkord i en stor melodi. Den uttrykker glede over en antydet sorg og lysner sorgen med omsluttende glede. Ville Jakobs sju år lange ventetid ha virket som bare noen få dager hvis han hadde visst hva morgendagen ville bringe? Hvis vi visste alt, ville kjærligheten være for vanskelig. Hvis vi visste alt, ville kjærligheten være for lett. Hvis vi visste alt, ville vi få knuste hjerter. Hvis vi visste alt, ville vi være likegyldige. Med andre ord blir vi sterkere av ikke å kjenne det verste, og mer ømme av ikke å kjenne det beste. For i vårt tilslørte og formørkede syn … blir disse tre: tro, håp og kjærlighet; men størst blant dem er kjærligheten – 1 Kor 13:13.

Det er ingen tilfeldighet at mens disiplene … så på, ble han løftet opp, og en sky tok ham bort fra øynene deres – Apg 1:9. Derfor bør vi ikke bli overrasket over at vi til tider blir kalt til å lide under den mentale belastningen og påkjenningen ved en uklar og ukjent morgendag. … For hva er livet deres? Dere er en damp som viser seg en kort stund og så forsvinner – Jak 4:14. Det kommer en dag da vi skal … se Menneskesønnen komme i en sky med kraft og stor herlighet – Luk 21:27. Og igjen står det skrevet: Se, han kommer med skyene, og hvert øye skal se ham … Ja, amen – Åp 1:7.
